item.title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[ \delta(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v), \qquad E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[ \delta(u),\delta(v)<\frac n2, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[ E_{\cap}=\varnothing, \qquad \sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[ \delta(u)+\delta(v)<n, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph. Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.
item.dc:creator: Ailian Chen, Hao Chen

item.title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=\Theta(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.
item.dc:creator: Richard P. Anstee, Attila Sali, Pei Wu

item.title: A proof of the Auluck-Chowla-Gupta Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let p(n,k) denote the number of partitions of n into exactly k parts. In 1942 Auluck, Chowla and Gupta conjectured that for every n the sequence p(n,1), p(n,2), ..., p(n,n) is unimodal. Szekeres proved this for all sufficiently large n, but with a threshold that was never made explicit. We prove the conjecture for every n >= 1. For n >= 10^5 we give an analytic argument with fully explicit constants: an exact probabilistic representation of the ratio p(n,k+1)/p(n,k), a second-order saddle-point main term with a rigorous uniform error bound in the transition window, and separate elementary or saddle-point estimates in the two tails. Every numerical constant in this argument is certified in ball arithmetic. For n <= 2*10^5 the conjecture is verified exhaustively by two independent programs, one of them using exact integer arithmetic only. Since log-concavity of k -> p(n,k) fails for every n >= 4, the argument works with first differences and never uses log-concavity.
item.dc:creator: Jaideep Sai Padhi

item.title: Maximally symmetric $(23_4)$ configurations and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, following his 1990 paper with Rigby that gave the first geometric $4$-configuration, a $(21_4)$. Successive work of Bokowski-Schewe, of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum and Schewe, of Bokowski-Pilaud, and of Cuntz settled every case but one. Cuntz's 2018 paper, which constructed $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations, states that only $n=23$ remained open. We settle this last case. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$, in particular for $n=23$, the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, which explains why $n=23$ resisted the symmetric constructions that settled the other values. Reducing the case of a Klein four-group of symmetries to a few thousand bilinear polynomial systems in $18$ unknowns, and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases and saturation, we show that exactly two geometric $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound, up to projective equivalence, and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar with respect to a conic. The first has integer homogeneous coordinates; the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$, but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. A third configuration, self-polar and defined over a real cubic field, has only a single symmetry of order two. The same classification at $n=22$ and $n=26$ recovers Cuntz's configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$, among them a $(26_4)$ configuration that is self-polar with respect to a conic without real points.
item.dc:creator: Wenhao Lu

item.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$, and we describe $\Lambda_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$. For a vector whose components are the $n$ distinct $n$th roots of unity, every $Z_i(v)$ equals $S_n$. We then show that the conjecture is false for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with one vertex duplicated has an eigenvalue lying $2.1\cdot10^{-4}$ beyond one edge of $S_7$. For the analogous digraph of order $n$, the corresponding eigenvalue lies at signed distance $\delta_n\sim\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$ beyond the supporting line of the analogous edge of $S_n$, so the construction yields counterexamples for all sufficiently large $n$; numerically, it does so for every $7\le n\le300$. We also prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$, with $S_m\setminus\{0,1\}$ lying in the interior of $S_n$ for $n\ge3m$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev

item.title: New mixed cages, bounds and computational results
item.description: arXiv:2610.14110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $(r,z,g)$-mixed cage is a mixed graph that is $r$-regular in edges, $z$-regular in arcs, of girth $g$ and of minimum order $n=n(r,z,g)$. We give a general lower bound for $n(r,z,g)$. In the case $g=3$, we determine the exact value $n(r,z,3)=r+2z+1$. For $g=4$ we give two improved lower bounds and we determine the exact value $n(r,z,4)=2r+4z$ for $r\geq 2z-2$. We also present computational results, obtaining mixed cages and computational lower bounds by means of exhaustive backtracking searches with symmetry reductions. Moreover, we give an upper bound for $n(1,z,g)$ that matches all our computed values.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Marlene De la Cruz, Miguel \'Angel Piza\~na

item.title: Free products, principal sums, bipartition complete matroids and the linking operation $(\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we examine the special class of bipartition complete matroids, which includes free products and principal sums of matroids (Crapo and Schmitt, 2005; Bonin and Kung, 2015). A matroid $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}$ on $S \uplus Q$ is said to be $\{S,Q\}$--complete iff whenever $b^1_S \uplus b^1_Q, \, b^1_S \uplus b^2_Q,$ and $b^2_S \uplus b^1_Q$ are bases of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ},$ we also have $b^2_S \uplus b^2_Q$ as a base of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}.$ We use the linking operation $\mathcal{M}_{SP} \leftrightarrow_{\mathcal{M}} \mathcal{M}_{PQ} :\equiv (\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$ (Theja and Narayanan, 2014) for this study. We construct the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an arbitrary matroid and show that this augmentation is again a matroid, that the dual of the augmentation is the augmentation of the dual matroid and that the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an $\{S, Q\}$--complete matroid leaves it unchanged. We also show that bipartition completeness is stable under minors in the appropriate bipartitioned sense. Finally, we show that free products and principal sums of matroids $\mathcal{M}_{S},\mathcal{M}_{Q}$ are $\{S, Q\}$--complete and give explicit minimal decompositions for them.
item.dc:creator: H. Narayanan

item.title: Reconstruction and Symmetry of Two-Token Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a proof of the two-token graph reconstruction conjecture. Every finite simple graph $G,H$ of order at least three, $F_2(G) \cong F_2(H)$ if and only if $G \cong H$. We also classify the automorphism groups of two-token graphs whose connected roots have order at least five. Combining these results, we show that, for connected graphs $G,H$ of order at least five, every isomorphism $\phi:F_2(G)\to F_2(H)$ admits a factorization $\phi=\eta\circ\sigma^{(2)}$, where $\sigma^{(2)}$ is induced by a graph isomorphism $\sigma:G\to H$, and $\eta\in \operatorname{Aut}(F_2(H))$ is a product of twin-cut switches or Cartesian exchanges.
item.dc:creator: Yuanming Luo, Hao Hu

item.title: The Path Partition Conjecture and 3-(quasi-)Transitive Digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A digraph $D = (V,E)$ is 3-transitive (respectively, 3-quasi-transitive) if whenever $(u,v,w,z)$ is a directed path of length 3, $(u,z) \in E$ (respectively, $(u,z) \in E$ or $(z,u) \in E$). These digraphs extend the concepts of transitive and quasi-transitive digraphs, respectively. For 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs, only the strong case has been characterized. In this paper, we introduce the notion of semi-acyclic digraphs and use it to describe completely the structure of 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs. As an application of this type of structure description, we prove that the path partition conjecture holds for the class of extended semi-acyclic digraphs, which generalizes two previously known results on the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Shamik Ghosh, Jing Huang

item.title: Restricting Odd Antiholes in Critical Graphs via List Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2610.14241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(\Delta-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole. We verify this extremal characterization when $\Delta\geq 2k-5$, extending recent results for $\Delta=k$, and construct $k$-critical odd-hole-free graphs showing that the next possible odd antihole length $2(\Delta-k)+5$ below the extremal bound can occur. Our proofs use a list-coloring theorem for graphs on $2\ell-1$ vertices whose complements are hypomatchable. This motivates the conjecture that every odd antihole $\overline{C_{2\ell-1}}$ is strongly $\ell$-chromatic-choosable; we show that this conjecture would imply the full extremal characterization. We also obtain degree and attachment restrictions for odd antiholes in critical graphs.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Fiujlaali, Jessica McDonald

item.title: The Exact Degree Threshold for Complement Connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.14292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, we investigate sufficient degree conditions under which either $G$ or its complement $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $\delta(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $\Delta(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. We prove that $\mathcal{C}(k)=2k-2$ for every $k\ge2$, thereby determining the exact degree threshold. As an application, we derive a Nordhaus--Gaddum type product condition, showing that for $n\ge4k-5$, the condition $\delta(G)\delta(\overline{G}) \ge (2k-3)(n-2k+2)$ guarantees that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Finally, we show that no analogous product condition depending only on $k$ can exist.
item.dc:creator: Arsen Berk Tekda\c{s}

item.title: Cardinalities of Kiselman monoids and their parity asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2610.14331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The cardinalities of Kiselman's semigroups $K_n$ are known to grow double exponentially in $n$: the sequence $2^{-n/2}\log_2|K_n|$ converges along the even and odd $n$ subsequences to positive limits $c_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $c_{\mathrm{odd}}$ that appear to coincide. In this paper we prove that they are indeed distinct. Since Kiselman's semigroups are $\mathcal{L}$-trivial, the suffix relation defines a partial order on $K_n$. We introduce the \emph{Kiselman transform} $\mathsf{Kis}(P)$ of a poset $P$, a construction recovering the poset associated with $K_{n+1}$ from that associated with $K_n$. Counting strictly increasing chains in $P$ and $\mathsf{Kis}(P)$ yields a linear recurrence governed by a symmetric infinite matrix with explicit binomial entries. This can be used towards efficiently computing $|K_n|$, allowing the values listed in OEIS sequence A125625 to be extended beyond $n=14$. A generating functions analysis gives formulas for the above asymptotic limits, together with rigorous numerical bounds establishing that \[ c_{\mathrm{even}} - c_{\mathrm{odd}} = 1.9945066605\ldots\times10^{-6} \]
item.dc:creator: Alessandro D'Andrea, Salvatore Stella

item.title: A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor
item.description: arXiv:2610.14370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the nonloop simplification of $M$ is $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds.
item.dc:creator: Haozhou Zhang

item.title: Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.14373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $\Gamma(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto \Gamma(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$. We compute the first nontrivial moments through order six. In particular, the fourth moment already contains the Coxeter triangle relation and determines the signed local invariant $6N_{K_3}(G)-N_{P_3}(G)$, rather than $N_{P_3}(G)$ alone. Consequently, for triangle-free graphs the spectrum determines the second moment of the degree sequence. We also give a simplified sixth-moment formula for triangle-free graphs, showing that in this class the spectrum determines $5N_{K_{1,3}}(G)+2N_{P_4}(G)+12N_{C_4}(G)$. Further structural consequences include bipartiteness and spectral symmetry of $\Gamma(G)$, a precise connectedness test, and the identification of the standard irreducible component with the shifted graph Laplacian $mI-L_G$.
item.dc:creator: Boris Shapiro

item.title: Greedy Coloring and Simple Exponential Strengthenings of Brooks-Type Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brooks' Theorem is a foundational result in graph coloring: if a graph is connected, not a clique, and has maximum degree $\Delta \geq 3$, then it admits a proper $\Delta$-coloring. In this paper, we give a new proof of a much stronger result: every such graph admits exponentially many proper $\Delta$-colorings. Exponential lower bounds have been obtained previously by applying the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz. In contrast, our proof is via a surprisingly simple and constructive analysis of a textbook greedy coloring algorithm. The entire argument is accessible to non-specialists. We extend our techniques to provide quantitative lower bounds on the number of colorings in several more general settings, namely $\Delta$-length list coloring, degree-length list coloring (degree-choosability), and degenerate partitioning. In the latter setting, one is asked to partition the vertices such that each partite set induces a subgraph of bounded degeneracy. In contrast to the other coloring variants considered, no clean Brooks-type characterization is possible, since it is known that for some combinations of parameters determining the existence of even one valid partition is NP-hard. We give a new reduction which significantly extends the parameter regime for which determining the existence of a valid partition is NP-hard. Finally, we give a new proof of the classic degree-choosability theorem, generalizing the techniques behind a recent proof of Brooks' Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Alex Crane, Carl Feghali, Felicia Lucke, Blair D. Sullivan, Madelyn J. Warr

item.title: A framework for spanning forest identities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identities of spanning forest polynomials can come from determinantal identities such as the classical Dodgson identity. They can also be useful in quantum field theory calculations, particularly the quadratic ones. To better understand the structure of spanning forest polynomial identities, we look at when identities on a given graph are generic for all graphs, we ask about dimensions of spaces of spanning forest identities indexed by certain parameters, and we set up a framework that we hope will be helpful for further progress in these directions. As part of this framework, we identify a family of maps naturally given by the all-minors matrix-tree theorem, and we show that their ranks are counted by the Narayana numbers via explicit construction of bases.
item.dc:creator: Kai Choi, Rowan Yeats

item.title: Local Antimagic Chromatic Number of Middle Graph and Direct Product of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An edge labeling of a connected graph $G=(V, E)$ is called a local antimagic labeling if it is a bijection $f: E\rightarrow \{1, 2, \cdots, \left | E \right | \}$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, $f^{+}(u)\neq f^{+}(v)$ where $f^{+}(x)=\sum f(e)$, with $e$ ranging over all the edges incident to $x$. The local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $\chi_{la}(G)$, is the minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels across all possible local antimagic labelings of $G$. This paper investigates two families of graphs $G(m^{[n]})$ (a graph class constructed by augmenting a bipartite structure $B(m^{[n]})$ with cyclic edges) and $K_{1,s}\times C_n$ (the direct product of a star $K_{1,s}$ and a cycle $C_n$). Under the conditions odd integer $m\ge 1$ and even integer $n\ge 4$, we establish the exact values of $\chi_{la}(G(m^{[n]}))$ and $\chi_{la}(K_{1,s}\times C_n)$ for various $s$. Furthermore, we characterize several graph families achieving $\chi_{la}(G)=2$ or $3$.
item.dc:creator: Huimin Xu, Gee-Choon Lau, Ruixue Zhang

item.title: When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?
item.description: arXiv:2610.14496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a subset $A$ of a finite abelian group $G$, let $\Sigma_k(A)$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$, and let $\Sigma(A)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\Sigma_k(A)$. The problem of determining when $\Sigma(A)=G$ goes back to Erd\H{o}s and Heilbronn. Nguyen and Vu later formulated the corresponding fixed-length question: for a prescribed $k$, when does $\Sigma_k(A)=G$? For groups of odd order, we prove the sharp large-order threshold $|A|>|G|/3+1$, which forces $\Sigma_k(A)=G$ throughout the entire middle range $4\le k\le |A|-4$. This determines the limiting thresholds posed by Girard, Griffiths and Hamidoune. If $p$ is the least prime divisor of $|G|$, then, for fixed odd $p$ and sufficiently large $|G|$, the exact threshold $|A|\ge |G|/p+p-1$ forces covering throughout the middle range beginning at $2p-2$. Thus, throughout this range, prescribing the number of summands does not change the sharp covering threshold. For $3\le k\le2p-3$, the restricted and ordinary $k$-fold covering problems have the same asymptotic threshold. As an application to MDS elliptic codes on an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$, we sharpen the half-scale conjecture of Li, Wan and Zhang, obtaining the sharp $1/3$-scale bound when $|E(\F_q)|$ is odd and, more generally, the exact bound determined by the least prime divisor of $|E(\F_q)|$.
item.dc:creator: Dongchun Han, Yuan Ren

item.title: Monophobic Neighborhoods of Cubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a $d$-cube in a graph $G$ to be monophobic in $G$ if, whenever it supports a $d$-face of a discrete singular $d+1$-cube, it must also support another face. In many cases, the presence of such cubes implies the nontriviality of discrete cubical homology and homotopy groups associated with $G$. We describe several large classes of examples and characterize the property completely when $d=2$.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Greene, Samira Sahar Jamil

item.title: A sharp bound for the least signless Laplacian eigenvalue of triangle-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ on $n\geq1$ vertices satisfies $q_{\min}(G)\leq7n/50$, where $q_{\min}(G)$ is the least eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian matrix $Q_G=D_G+A_G$, with $D_G$ the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A_G$ the adjacency matrix. The constant is sharp, since the Higman--Sims graph and its balanced blow-ups attain equality, as shown by de Lima, Nikiforov and Oliveira (2016). This proves the bound conjectured by Balogh, Clemen, Lidick\'y, Norin and Volec (2023). The proof uses five test column vectors associated with an ordered edge to obtain a matrix Rayleigh inequality. Our use of local Rayleigh inequalities together with flag-algebra semidefinite programming is inspired by Zhou (2026). We use semidefinite programming and rational approximation to find the required positive semidefinite matrices, and complete the proof by exact correction and verification.
item.dc:creator: Dongxiu Cai, Zhengbo Chen, Xiao-Dong Zhang

item.title: Sharp projection inequalities for antichains in cone orders
item.description: arXiv:2610.14563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp projection inequalities for $k$-antichains under orders defined by open convex cones. For integers $n\geq2$ and $k\ge 1$, let $C\subsetneq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open convex cone. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is a $k$-antichain with respect to the order $x\prec_C y\iff y-x\in C$ if it contains no chain $x^1\prec_C\cdots\prec_C x^{k+1}$. For every such set $A$ and every $v\in C$, we prove \[ \mathcal H^{n-1}(A) \leq k\frac{\|v\|}{\alpha_C(v)} \mathcal H^{n-1}(P_v(A)), \] where $P_v$ is the orthogonal projection onto $v^\perp$, $\mathcal H^{n-1}$ denotes normalized Hausdorff outer measure, and $\alpha_C(v)$ is the minimum of $\langle\xi,v\rangle$ over unit vectors in the dual cone $C^*$. In particular, every weak antichain $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq\mathcal H^{n-1}(\Delta_i(A))$ for each $i$, where $\Delta_i(x)=(x_j-x_i)_{j\ne i}$. This proves the skewed projection conjecture of Engel, Mitsis, Pelekis and Reiher. As an application, we recover the bound $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq kn$ for $k$-antichains in the unit cube under the coordinatewise order.
item.dc:creator: Yuxian Dong, Lili Mu

item.title: Generalized reflection complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.14637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reflection complexity of a sequence, introduced recently by Allouche, Campbell, Li, Shallit, and Stipulanti, counts the factors of a given length up to reversal. We generalize this notion considering a group $G$ generated by antimorphisms over a given alphabet $\mathcal A$. The $G$-complexity of a sequence over $\mathcal A$ counts the factors of a given length up to the action of $G$. For $G$ generated by the reflection alone, the $G$-complexity coincides with the reflection complexity. We characterize eventual periodicity in terms of the $G$-complexity. Then we focus on the binary alphabet and the group $H$ generated by reflection and the antimorphism exchanging letters. We provide a simple formula for the $H$-complexity in the case of $H$-rich sequences and determine the precise values for complementary symmetric Rote sequences and generalized binary Thue-Morse sequences. Finally, we describe the aperiodic recurrent sequences having the minimum $H$-complexity -- they are exactly the complementary symmetric Rote sequences, while the binary sequences with the minimum reflection complexity correspond to the Sturmian sequences.
item.dc:creator: Adam Bla\v{z}ek, Lubom\'ira Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Edita Pelantov\'a

item.title: Induced-Count Discrepancy in Uniform Hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ be the maximum, over all $k$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs $F$, of the absolute difference between the number of induced copies of $F$ in $H$ and its expectation in the binomial random $r$-graph with the same number of vertices as $H$ and edge probability $p$. Let $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ be the minimum of $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ over all $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $D_r(n,p)$ be the distance from $p\binom nr$ to the nearest integer. For fixed $r\ge3$, $k\ge2r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the quantity $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ has order $\max\!\left\{D_r(n,p),p(1-p)\right\}n^{k-r}$ whenever $p(1-p)n^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor/(\binom{2r-2}{r}-1)}\ge\varepsilon$. Using local moment estimates and switchings in a sparse reservoir, we construct one hypergraph with the nearest-integer edge count that controls all induced orders simultaneously.
item.dc:creator: Chenglong Yu

item.title: Combinatorics of degeneracy in vertical systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the generic consistency of vertical systems in terms of the iterated circuits of the column matroid of the coefficient matrix. More precisely, we prove that such a system is generically consistent if and only if there exists an iterated circuit such that the dimension of the Minkowski sum of the associated Newton polytopes is equal to the rank of the coefficient matrix. We also give an equivalent characterization in terms of $G$-spanning flags of the dual matroid. With this, we derive a combinatorial formula for the codimension of the locus of parameter values for which the system has a solution, extending known results on dual defects of toric varieties. When this locus has codimension one, its defining equation yields a generalization of the sparse resultant to vertical systems, which applies also to $\mathcal{A}$-discriminants. Finally, we characterize when the solution set is contained, for generic parameter values, in a finite union of hyperplanes parallel to a coordinate hyperplane.
item.dc:creator: Carles Checa, Nidhi Kaihnsa

item.title: New bounds for off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.14829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"ete, and Yu, which characterizes the $3$-graphs $H$ for which the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,n)$ is polynomial. We prove the conjecture for $3$-graphs with at most five tight components. Additionally, we show that the full conjecture is equivalent to its specialization to linear $3$-graphs. We prove quasipolynomial upper bounds for a class of `forward-doubleable' $3$-graphs, which includes the Fano plane. Finally, we give an exponential lower bound for `non-forward-laminar' $3$-graphs and use this to completely classify the Ramsey growth of a natural family of 3-graphs called chains.
item.dc:creator: David Conlon, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Logan Post

item.title: Coefficientwise Extremality and Rigidity for Independent Sets in Bipartite Graph Covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.14892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph and let $\widetilde G$ be an $M$-fold cover. We compare independent sets of $\widetilde G$ with those of the trivial cover, consisting of $M$ disjoint copies of $G$, after prescribing how many vertices are selected above each vertex of $G$. A conjecture from 2011, motivated by the Bethe approximation, asserts that the trivial cover maximizes every such count. We prove this for every feasible occupation profile whose active graph has treewidth at most two or is chordal bipartite. Equality holds exactly when the restricted cover is flat, meaning that fibre relabelings make it trivial. For $M\ge2$ and positive feasible occupations, a nonflat cover of a connected bipartite graph of treewidth at most two has a deficit of at least twice the coefficient of $p_G^{M-2}$ with every occupation reduced by one. A holonomy-dependent bound improves the factor to three for odd-order holonomy; both uniform constants are sharp. Comparison and rigidity survive finite compositions along an edge or a vertex, and quantitative bounds from one piece propagate to the whole graph, giving results beyond the two original classes. On any bipartite base, the first nonzero homogeneous defect is determined by the shortest cycles with nontrivial holonomy. At singleton occupations, our counts are numbers of DP-colorings of full covers. The dual DP color function on these classes and their finite seam compositions equals the chromatic polynomial, with equality attained precisely by canonical labelings. Dong's chromatic-polynomial inequality then yields the Dual-DP Shameful inequality on the same graph class. The main theorems have been formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Watanabe

item.title: Sharp bounds and extremal structure of minimally strongly $k$-connected digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be a finite simple minimally strongly $k$-connected digraph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $n=|V(D)|$. Mader proved in 1985 that $|A(D)|\le 2k(n-k)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with equality if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$ (JCTB 1985). We prove that this bound holds whenever $n\ge 3k-1$ and that the order threshold $3k-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $n\ge 3k$, then equality holds if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$. The threshold $3k$ is also best possible. These results resolve the conjecture of Mader in (JCTB 1985).
item.dc:creator: Junran Yu, Gregory Gutin, Hong-Jian Lai, Xiaoyan Zhang

item.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank II: Generalizing Linusson's count to sumsets of f-vectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.14985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra of an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field, let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$, and let $M$ range over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The Hilbert function of $F/M$ is a shifted sum of $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes; the companion paper determines the convex hull of such sums, and here we count them. For $r = 1$ the count is Linusson's (1999); we show that no new recursion is needed for general $r$. Using two statistics of an $f$-vector -- its top nonvanishing degree and the initial degree of the corresponding ideal -- we prove that the number of achievable Hilbert functions is a product of $r-1$ transfer matrices, one per generator-degree gap, with entries differences of Linusson's refined counts $E^p(n,k)$. The rank enters only as the length of a matrix product. The same holds for the proper variant. Consequences: a linear recurrence in $r$ for constant gaps, with exact exponential asymptotics $K \lambda^r$ when the gap is positive; polynomiality in $r$ when all gaps vanish; a threshold beyond which the count is a plain power; and polynomiality in the number of vertices.
item.dc:creator: Jan Snellman

item.title: Sharp lower bounds for bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.15024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts whose sizes differ by at most one. We prove that every graph with $m$ edges and maximum degree at most $k$ has a bisection of size at least $\frac{k+1}{2k}m$ when $k$ is odd, and at least $\frac{k+2}{2(k+1)}m$ when $k$ is even. Both bounds are sharp, with equality for complete graphs. This establishes the unweighted case of the bisection conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo and Zhou (arXiv 2024), removes the additive error from the corresponding bounds of Lee, Loh and Sudakov (JCTB 2013), and extends the odd-degree regular case proved by Bollob\'as and Scott (JGT 2004) to arbitrary graphs of bounded maximum degree. The proof combines the matching-and-pairing method with the Gallai--Edmonds decomposition. Hall's theorem controls the number of uncovered factor-critical components whose internal degrees are all even. A boundary-edge count bounds this obstruction by the total degree deficiency, while the remaining uncovered components supply the required pairing gain.
item.dc:creator: Qiwen Guo, Gregory Gutin

item.title: How iterated sumsets grow under the assumption of small doubling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K>1$ be a real number and let $A\subsetneq \mathbb Z$ be a finite and nonempty subset. Suppose $|A+A|<K|A|$. A fundamental open problem is to characterize the size of higher iterated sumsets $nA = A+\cdots+A$ ($n$-fold sumset). In 2004, Terry Tao formally posed the problem of determining the optimal growth function governing iterated sumsets of small-doubling sets. In this manuscript, we give a solution to this long-standing open problem for large enough $n$.
item.dc:creator: Dongchun Han, Qinghai Zhong

item.title: Davenport Constants of Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central problem in zero-sum theory is to determine the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group. For a finite abelian group $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$, with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$, let $\mathsf D(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, and denote $\mathsf D^*(G):= 1+\sum_{i=1}^r(n_i-1)$. The standard construction shows that $\mathsf D(G)\ge\mathsf D^*(G)$. Equality holds for several important classes of groups but fails in general, and even the question whether $\mathsf D(G)/\mathsf D^*(G)$ is bounded by an absolute constant remains open. In this paper, we prove the upper bound \[ \mathsf D(G)<4.86\,\exp(G)\frac{\log|G|}{\log\exp(G)} \] for every finite abelian group. When $|G|$ is large compared with $\exp(G)$, it improves the previous classical upper bound by a factor of order $\log\exp(G)$. We also prove that, for almost all finite abelian groups (counting isomorphism classes by order), \[ \mathsf D(G)\sim\exp(G)\frac{\log|G|}{\log\exp(G)}\sim\mathsf D^*(G). \] We also study the difference $\mathsf D(G)-\mathsf D^*(G)$: for every function $L$ with $L(x)\to\infty$, almost all groups satisfy $\mathsf D(G)-\mathsf D^*(G)\le L(\mathsf D^*(G))$. However, for every fixed $C\ge0$, the groups with $\mathsf D(G)-\mathsf D^*(G)>C$ have positive lower density.
item.dc:creator: Dongchun Han, Hanbin Zhang

item.title: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.15131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches. One approach uses the Girard-Waring formula, while the other relies on Binet's formula and linear algebra.
item.dc:creator: Joey Glampe, Aryaman Joshi, Swagat Malla, Matthew Richey, Matthew Wright

item.title: Cones of Theta Graphs are Enumeratively Chromatic-Choosable
item.description: arXiv:2610.15132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chromatic choosability is a fundamental notion in list coloring. A graph $G$ is chromatic-choosable if its chromatic number $\chi(G)$ equals its list chromatic number $\chi_{\ell}(G)$. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list-coloring analogue of its chromatic polynomial $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable if $P_{\ell}(G,m)=P(G,m)$ for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In 2002, Ohba proved that for every graph $G$, there exists an $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $K_p \vee G$ is chromatic-choosable whenever $p \geq N$. Allred and Mudrock recently conjectured that an analogous statement holds for enumerative chromatic choosability. In this paper, we prove that $K_1 \vee G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $G$ is a theta graph. Our proof combines classical inequalities, the polynomial method, and ideas from DP (or correspondence) coloring.
item.dc:creator: Kingston Barnes, Vincent Fesenmeier, Braxton Gaither, Michael Guthrie, Leonardo Marciaga, Lucas Miller, Fennec Morrissette, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Gavin Nguyen, Rose Zellner

item.title: Nim heaps in the Game of Cycles: the parity conjecture fails on trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.15145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Game of Cycles, invented by Francis Su, is a two-player game in which the players take turns drawing arrows on the edges of a plane graph, never creating a sink or a source. On a tree only the sink-source rule matters, and the player who makes the last move wins. Several authors conjectured that on a tree the second player wins exactly when the number of markable edges is even. We show that this parity conjecture is false, and we explain why. The explanation is a hidden game of Nim: a path segment that is blocked by an arrow at one end and free at the other behaves exactly like a nim heap whose size is its length. Combined with a calculus for cutting and gluing trees at vertices next to leaves, this shows that the conjecture fails as soon as a single tree has Grundy value at least 2. The smallest counterexamples have 15 vertices. Trees with Grundy values 2 and 4 first appear at 17 vertices, and every value up to 63 occurs, which answers a question of Fokkink and Zandee. We also refute a related conjecture of Zandee. We then look closely at spiders. The spiders S(2,3,z) violate the conjecture for every z >= 14. The Grundy values of S(1,2j,z) are given by an exact formula governed by binary carries. For 99 pairs (x,y), the value of S(x,y,z) is eventually the parity of z. On the positive side, the conjecture holds for all trees in which every thread has at most two edges, and this bound is sharp. Along the way we prove a twin-branch reduction, give an algorithm that is polynomial for spiders with a fixed number of legs, and collect the questions that we could not answer. The boldest asks whether every non-negative integer is the Grundy value of some tree.
item.dc:creator: Muchen Xu

item.title: Extremal graphs with cycle lengths in a fixed residue class
item.description: arXiv:2610.15151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $k\ge3$ and $0\le \ell<k$, we call a graph $(\ell\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted if every cycle has length congruent to $\ell$ modulo $k$. Akbari, Jamaali, Mahmoody, and Seyed Fakhari [On the size of graphs whose cycles have length divisible by a fixed integer, Australas. J. Combin. 45 (2009), 67--72] determined the maximum number of edges in a $2$-connected $(0\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted graph and characterized the graphs attaining equality. In this paper, we determine the maximum number of edges in a $2$-connected $(\ell\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted graph for every $\ell \neq 0$, and completely characterize all graphs attaining equality. Combined with the result of Akbari et al., our result gives a complete solution for all residue classes modulo $k$.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Ueoro

item.title: Tuza's Conjecture for Graphs of Maximum Degree at Most 10
item.description: arXiv:2610.15269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of pairwise edge disjoint triangles and $\tau(G)$ the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza conjectured in 1981 that every such $G$ satisfies $\tau(G) \le 2 \nu(G).$ We prove the conjecture for the class of graphs with $\Delta\le10.$
item.dc:creator: Amrit Kandasamy

item.title: A note on the logarithmic exponent of Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we point out that the recent lower bounds for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(s,t)$ with fixed $s\ge 5$, together with the recent proof of the Ajtai--Erd\H{o}s--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi independence conjecture, imply \[ r(4,t)=\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}. \] This note is solely for informal circulation and will not be submitted for publication.
item.dc:creator: Kaizhe Chen

item.title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.15348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal K_k(F)$ be the expanded graph obtained by adding $k-2$ new vertices to each edge of $F$, with disjoint sets of new vertices for distinct edges. Mubayi proved that, for every clique $K_r$ with $r\ge4$ and fixed $ q>0$, $ h_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,q)\ge qt_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,1)$ for every sufficiently large $n$. Pikhurko and Yilma later proved that, for every color-critical graph $F$, there is a constant $\epsilon_F>0$ such that $h_{F}(n,q)=t_{F}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon_F n$. We extend this equality to expanded color-critical graphs. Let $d>k\ge3$. For every color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F)=d+1$, there is a constant $\epsilon>0$ such that $ h_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)=t_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon n^{k-1}$. Let $q_L(n)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that $h_L(n,s)=t_L(n,s)$ for every integer $1\le s\le q$. We give a sufficient condition for $q_L(n)=\Theta_L(n^{k-1})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. We also give a different sufficient condition under which $q_L(n)=\Omega_L(n^{k-1/2})$. \noindent \emph{Keywords.} Supersaturation; extremal graph; color-critical graph; chromatic number; expanded graph; hypergraph.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Yanmei Hong, Jinze Hu

item.title: Maximum index of unbalanced signed graphs without a positive odd cycle
item.description: arXiv:2610.15383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$ be the set of all balanced signed graphs with underlying graphs $C_r$. A signed graph is called $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$. In this paper, we characterize the extremal graphs that achieve the maximum index among all $\mathcal{C}_{2k+1}^+$-free unbalanced signed graphs of order $n$ when $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 187k$.
item.dc:creator: Li Ma, Linfeng Xie, Xiaogang Liu

item.title: General Constructions of Permutation-Fair Dice
item.description: arXiv:2610.15421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that each of $n$ players rolls a different die and the players are ordered by their rolls. Can the dice use disjoint labels such that ties are impossible, while all $n!$ orders remain equally likely? We give two general constructions of such dice and solve some related problems.
item.dc:creator: Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Bernhard Haeupler, V\'aclav Rozho\v{n}

item.title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.15424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of D\'ucz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csisz\'arik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zs\'amboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.
item.dc:creator: Shisheng Li, Yong Su

item.title: Tur\'an Numbers of Linear Stars and Expanded Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.15447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$, let $\ex_r(n,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $\mathcal H$. The $r$-uniform expansion $T^{(r)}$ of a tree $T$ is obtained by adding $r-2$ new vertices to each edge, with the added sets pairwise disjoint and disjoint from $V(T)$. In particular, the expansion of $K_{1,k}$ is the linear star $\mathcal L_k^r$, whose $k$ edges intersect pairwise in a single common vertex. Chung and Frankl (1987) determined $\ex_3(n,\mathcal L_k^3)$ and all extremal hypergraphs for every $k\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$. We extend the odd-$k$ part of their result to every $r\ge5$, determining the exact Tur\'an number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism for sufficiently large $n$. More generally, we extend this result to expansions of trees for which the minimum degree among the vertices in the smaller color class is odd and at least three. For every $r\ge5$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish lower and upper bounds on their Tur\'an numbers. When no two vertices attaining this minimum degree in that color class have a common neighbor, we determine the exact Tur\'an number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism. The proofs combine the delta-system method with stability arguments and a detailed analysis of extremal constructions.
item.dc:creator: Xinmin Hou, Anyao Wang

item.title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
item.description: arXiv:2610.15534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J. Graph Theory, 2026] proved that for every planar extremal brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar extremal bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ has a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$, where $G_i/T_i$ means contracting the triangle $T_i$ into a single vertex. In this paper, the result of Zhou et al. is generalized to planar PM-compact bricks, a larger class of bricks including extremal bricks. We present a chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks: for every planar PM-compact brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar PM-compact bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ contains a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$.
item.dc:creator: Yaxian zhang, Qiuli Li, Fuliang Lu

item.title: Hull Variation in Symplectic Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.15535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the variation of hull dimensions of symplectic linear codes under equivalence transformations preserving the symplectic distance. For a symplectic linear code $C$, we introduce an even-valued invariant $\Delta(C)$, which depends only on the equivalence class of $C$. This invariant can be expressed as the generic rank of an associated space of alternating matrices and, equivalently, as twice a corresponding matroid matching number. If $C$ has dimension $k$, we prove that the minimum symplectic hull dimension among all codes equivalent to $C$ is $k-\Delta(C)$. Consequently, $C$ is equivalent to a symplectic LCD code if and only if $\Delta(C)=k$. We further show that every symplectic MDS code of even dimension is monomially equivalent to a symplectic LCD code. For a symplectic self-orthogonal code $C$, we determine all attainable hull dimensions: for every integer $r$ with $0\le r\le \Delta(C)/2$, there exists a monomially equivalent code whose symplectic hull has dimension $k-2r$. We also refine a standard form for the generator matrix of a symplectic self-orthogonal code and derive the corresponding parity-check matrix and the Gram matrix of the dual code. In the self-dual case, we characterize $\Delta(C)$ through minors of an associated symmetric matrix. Furthermore, we relate hull variation to graph matchings, establish a bound for $\Delta(C)$, and give graph constructions producing symplectic self-dual MDS, optimal, and best-known codes.
item.dc:creator: Kanat Abdukhalikov, Somi Gupta, Duy Ho

item.title: Tuza's Conjecture under an Edge-Count Condition
item.description:
arXiv:2610.15539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, let $
u(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and let $	au(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture asserts that $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$ for every graph $G$. We first note that Tuza's conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: for every fixed $c\ge 0$, if $G$ is a sufficiently large $n$-vertex graph with $e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn$, then $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$. In this paper, we prove this statement for every $c<2$.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Liu, Qinghou Zeng

item.title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
item.dc:creator: Zhanping Yang

item.title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph. In addition, we give a constructive proof that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many chemical nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Furthermore, for $3 \leq d \leq 8$, the values $k$, for which a $d$-regular nut graph $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$ exists, are characterised. It is shown here that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many cubic polyhedral nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Two ways of producing larger nut graphs from smaller are described: the cut and frustration constructions. One straightforward consequence is that total double subdivision of a nut graph (i.e. simultaneous insertion of two degree-$2$ vertices into every edge) yields a nut graph.
item.dc:creator: Nino Ba\v{s}i\'c, Patrick W. Fowler

item.title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.15849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.
item.dc:creator: Ahaan Kallat

item.title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$V\'elez permutation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and V\'elez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Floros

item.title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
item.description: arXiv:2610.15909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity. First, we resolve the core open problem on the topic by showing the virtual extension complexity can be exponentially smaller than extension complexity. Second, we show there are matroid base polytopes with exponential virtual extension complexity by adapting a semi-algebraic counting argument by Hrube\v{s} that extends the counting arguments of Rothvoss. Finally, we show that the maximum virtual extension complexity of a polygon with $n$ vertices is $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$. This resolves an analogue of a question on extension complexity of Fiorini, Rothvoss, and Tiwary in 2011 in the case of virtual extension complexity.
item.dc:creator: Alexander E. Black, Christoph Hertrich, Stefan Kober, Georg Loho

item.title: The $\lambda$-chain condition of a finite partially ordered set
item.description: arXiv:2610.15971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that a certain finite partially ordered set arising from an algebra with straightening laws on a finite distributive lattice satisfies the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, its application to commutative algebra is briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Sora Miyashita

item.title: Dot actions and Hessenberg spaces for dihedral groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.16001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Splines on Weyl groups model the equivariant cohomology of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties, and the natural group action on them encodes the monodromy action. The resulting representations are of great interest in algebraic combinatorics for their connections to Hecke algebra characters, LLT polynomials, and chromatic symmetric functions. We study the analogous construction for dihedral groups, which in general have no underlying geometry. Using purely algebraic methods, we show that these spline modules are free, construct explicit bases, and compute their Hilbert series, recovering the familiar properties of the geometric setting. We also determine the associated dihedral group representations completely. Unlike what is conjectured for the symmetric group case, these need not be permutation representations.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Boretsky, Reuven Hodges, Nathan Lesnevich, Tyrrell McAllister, Joseph Pappe

item.title: Uniform Asymptotics for Andrews-Beck Partition Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2610.16024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\NT(m,n)$ be the total number of parts in the partitions of $n$ with rank $m$, and let $\MW(m,n)$ be the total number of ones in the partitions of $n$ with crank $m$. Using the uniform generalized-rank estimate of Liu and Zhou, we establish asymptotic formulas for $NT(m,n)$ and $\MW(m,n)$. Put $\beta_n=\pi/\sqrt{6n}$ and $L_n=\log(1/\beta_n)$. For every fixed $A>0$, uniformly for $|m|\le A\sqrt n$, we prove \begin{align*} \NT(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)L_n}{4}\sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\log L_n\bigr) \intertext{ and} \MW(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)}4\log(1+e^{-\beta_nm}) \sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\sqrt{\beta_nL_n}\bigr). \end{align*}
item.dc:creator: Renrong Mao

item.title: A Proof of the Erd\H{o}s Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.16203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve a conjecture of \L{}uczak, Mieczkowska and \v{S}ileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erd\H{o}s Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chi, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang

item.title: Subgroup Perfect Codes in Bi-Cayley Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.16235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study perfect codes in bi-Cayley graphs, focusing on when two subgroups $H$ and $K$ of a group G can form a perfect code of the form $H_0 \cup K_1$. We first consider the problem for a general group G and then examine what happens for special classes of groups, particularly abelian groups. Along the way, we obtain several results, including a necessary and sufficient condition for normal subgroups to form a perfect code, as well as an equivalent condition for abelian groups in terms of their Sylow 2-subgroups. Finally, we study the same problem for dihedral groups, providing results for this important class of non-abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Masoumeh Koohestani, Nasrin Soltankhah, Mohsen Ghasemi

item.title: Tournaments with many Hamilton cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.16245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The object of interest is the maximum number, $h(n)$, of Hamilton cycles in an $n$-tournament. By considering the expected number of Hamilton cycles in various classes of random tournaments, we obtain new asymptotic lower bounds on $h(n)$. The best result so far is approximately $ 2.85584...$ times the expected number $g(n)$ of Hamilton cycles in a random $n$-tournament, and it is conjectured that $h(n)\sim cg(n)$ where $c\approx 2.855958$. The same statements hold for Hamilton paths.
item.dc:creator: N. C. Wormald

item.title: Elementary graphs are chromatic-choosable
item.description: arXiv:2610.16258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is \emph{elementary} if its edges can be coloured with two colours so that the two edges of every induced path on three vertices receive different colours. Elementary graphs are one of the two basic classes in the Chv\'atal--Sbihi decomposition of claw-free perfect graphs; they include all line graphs of bipartite multigraphs and all complements of bipartite graphs. We prove that every elementary graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=\chi(G)=\omega(G)$, confirming for this class the conjecture of Gravier and Maffray that claw-free graphs are chromatic-choosable. The proof combines the Maffray--Reed description of elementary graphs as augmentations of line graphs of bipartite multigraphs, Galvin's theorem, an extremal (edge-maximal) choice of counterexample, and a Hall-type lemma describing how list colourings of a complete graph minus a matching can fail.
item.dc:creator: Narayanan N, Nandana K. Vasudevan, K. Somasundaram

item.title: Towards a Sum-of-Squares Proof for the Nonexistence of Conway's 99-graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.16266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conway's $99$-graph is a strongly regular graph with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu) = (99,14,1,2)$ and whose existence has long been an open problem. We use both a sum-of-squares program and the fact that a strongly regular graph with $\lambda = 1, \mu = 2$ has no diamond or $K_{2,3}$ subgraph to derive a loose upper bound for the number of triangles that such a graph could contain. This bound is less than the number of triangles that the graph's spectrum asserts, implying that it does not exist.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Natal, Oleksiy Al-saadi

item.title: The $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive integers $k,m,n$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, we prove a $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem: the symmetric function $(-1)^{k-1}\frac{[km]_q}{[k]_q}p_k[-MX^{m,n}]\cdot1$ is a weighted sum over $(km,kn)$-preference functions. This proves a corrected form of the conjecture of Iraci, Pagaria, Paolini, and Vanden Wyngaerd and generalizes the square paths theorem of Sergel. We encode preference functions by row strict tableaux and closed walks on a set of states, compare them with parking functions for each value of the touch statistic, and apply Mellit's compositional $(km,kn)$-shuffle theorem. Finally, we establish a fall Delta square theorem conjectured by Iraci, Pagaria, and Paolini.
item.dc:creator: Dun Qiu, Minhao Zhang

item.title: The rich-neighbor chromatic index is linear in the maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.16446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An edge of a multigraph is rich with respect to a proper edge-coloring if all the edges adjacent to it receive mutually distinct colors, and a proper edge-coloring is a rich-neighbor coloring if every non-isolated edge has a rich edge adjacent to it. The least number of colors in such a coloring is the rich-neighbor chromatic index chi'_rn(G). So far it was studied for subcubic graphs only, and multigraphs of larger maximum degree are considered here for the first time. The only upper bound valid in general was the quadratic one inherited from the strong chromatic index, while a single rich edge already requires 2D-1 colors in a D-regular graph, where D denotes the maximum degree. We give an upper linear bound chi'_rn(G) <= 6D-8 which holds for every loopless multigraph G with D >= 3, and we show that a coloring realizing this bound can be found in polynomial time. Consequently chi'_rn(G) = Theta(D). For D-regular graphs with D >= 3 the lower bound is 2D-1, and the upper bound is 5D-8. The bound 5D-8 holds more generally for every multigraph with D >= 3 which has a dominating P_{>=3}-system, and we characterize these multigraphs: such a system exists if and only if k_2(G-T) <= 2|T| holds for every set T of vertices, where k_2 counts the components on two vertices. In particular the bound holds for every graph with 3 <= D <= 4d-4, where d denotes the minimum degree. The paper is concluded with a conjecture on the tight upper bound on chi'_rn(G).
item.dc:creator: Masaki Kashima, Mirko Petru\v{s}evski, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

item.title: Edge and spectral conditions for rainbow bipancyclicity in bipartite graph collections
item.description: arXiv:2610.16459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{2n}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct balanced bipartite graphs of order $2n$ with a common bipartition $V=(X,Y)$. A cycle $C$ with $V(C)\subseteq V$ and $|E(C)|\leq 2n$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $\phi\colon E(C)\to [2n]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(C)$. The graph collection $\mathbf{G}$ is said to be \emph{rainbow bipancyclic} if it contains a rainbow cycle of every even length from 4 to $2n$. In this paper, we show that if $e(G_i)\ge n^2-n+1$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, where $B_{n}^1$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n,n}$ by deleting all edges in its one subgraph $K_{n-1,1}$. As a corollary, we obtain that if $\rho(G_i)\ge \rho(B_{n}^1)>\sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, which strengthens Theorem $5$ of [Electron. J. Combin., \textbf{33}(3)(2026), \#P3.29] and Theorem $1.6$ of [Linear Algebra Appl., \textbf{743}(2026), 250--270] from rainbow Hamiltonicity to rainbow bipancyclicity. We also characterize all bipartite graph collections that are not rainbow bipancyclic under the condition $\rho(G_i)\ge \sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$
item.dc:creator: Lihua You, Xiaoxue Zhang, Xinghui Zhao

item.title: New tools for sparse graph embeddings: Hybrid expanders and application to nested cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.16572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce \emph{hybrid expanders}, sparse graphs which combine sublinear expansion across all scales with strong constant-factor expansion on smaller, polylogarithmic sets. We show that every $n$-vertex graph of average degree at least $2^{\omega(\log^*n)}$ contains such a subgraph, and use this local expansion to bring into the sparse setting tree-embedding and rollback tools more commonly associated with random or pseudorandom graphs. As an application, for fixed $k\in\mathbb N$, we prove that every graph satisfying this average-degree condition contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles with nested vertex sets and compatible cyclic orders, resolving up to a quasi-constant factor a problem of Thomassen, originating in work of Erd\H{o}s.
item.dc:creator: Nemanja Dragani\'c

item.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood \(B\) of \(0\) and every \(\eps>0\), restricting the common difference to \(B\) increases the extremal number for \(k\)-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of \(1+\eps\), provided \(k\) is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Perfect matchings in planar 3-connected graphs: girth five and minimum degree five
item.description: arXiv:2610.16648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Phi(G)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of a graph $G$. Goedgebeur et al. posted two questions about the perfect matchings of planar 3-connected graphs: does there exist an infinite family of matchable planar 3-connected graphs of girth 5 with a constant number of perfect matchings? Whether there exist infinitely many planar 3-connected graphs with minimum degree 5 which have a constant number of perfect matchings. We present answers to those questions. First, we construct, for every even $n\ge196$, a simple planar 3-connected graph of order $n$ and girth five with exactly $c$ perfect matchings, where $c$ is a fixed positive integer. Second, for a simple planar 3-connected graph $G$ with a perfect matching and minimum degree at least five, we show that $\Phi(G)\ge2^{\lceil(|V(G)|+20)/22\rceil}$. This implies that, for each positive integer $t$, only finitely many such graphs, up to isomorphism, have at most $t$ perfect matchings.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Dai

item.title: Piercing boxes and products of trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.16703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new upper bound on the piercing number $\tau(\mathcal{F})$ of a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of axis-parallel rectangles in the plane when every $p$ members contain an intersecting pair. Namely, we prove $\tau(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$, improving the factor $(\log\log p)^2$ in the best previously known bound to $(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p)$. For each $d>2$, when $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$, this yields $\tau(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log p)^{d-2}(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$. We also study an analogous problem replacing $\mathbb{R}^d=\mathbb{R}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{R}$ with the Cartesian product $T_1\square\cdots\square T_d$ of trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$, and boxes with objects of the form $S_1\square\cdots\square S_d$ where $S_i$ is a subtree of $T_i$. For a finite family of such objects under the same intersection assumption as above, we establish an upper bound $\tau(\mathcal{F})=O(p(\log p)^{d-1})$ for each $d$. We also construct examples showing that this upper bound cannot be improved in order of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Wei Rao, Taehyun Eom, Minki Kim

item.title: Spectral extremal problems on $[a,b]$-factors in binding graphs, and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.16712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The binding number $b(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum value of $|N_{G}(X)|/|X|$ taken over all nonempty sets $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N_{G}(X)\neq V(G)$. A graph $G$ is 1-binding if $b(G)\geq 1$. Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024) P1.30] characterized the unique spectral extremal graphs among 1-binding graphs with $\delta(G)\geq k$ that contain no $k$-factor for $k=1$, $2$. Subsequently, Tang and Zhang solved the problem for $k\geq 3$. Note that $\delta(G)\geq a$ is a necessary condition for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in a graph $G$. For $1\leq a<b$, Fan et al. [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 115103] determined the unique spectral extremal graph $H_n^{a,b}$ among connected graphs with $\delta(G)\geq a$ that contain no $[a,b]$-factor. Note that $b(H_n^{a,b})<1$. This motivates the corresponding spectral extremal problem for 1-binding graphs. Note that every 1-binding graph with $\delta(G)\geq 1$ contains a $[1,b]$-factor for $b>1$. For $2\leq a<b$, we in this paper determine the unique extremal graph $\mathcal{B}_n^{a,b}$ with the maximum spectral radius among 1-binding graphs of order $n$ with $\delta(G)\geq a$ that contain no $[a,b]$-factor. The toughness of a non-complete graph $G$ is $t(G)=\min\{\frac{|X|}{c(G-X)}\mid X\subseteq V(G)\, \text{and}\, c(G-X)\geq 2\}$. A graph $G$ is 1-tough if $c(G-X)\leq |X|$ for every $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-X)\geq 2$. Every 1-tough graph of order $n\geq2$ is 1-binding. Note that $t(\mathcal{B}_n^{a,b})<1$. This leads us to investigate the corresponding spectral extremal problem for 1-tough graphs. Note that every 1-tough graph with $\delta(G)\geq 1$ contains a $[1,b]$-factor for $b>1$. For $2\leq a<b$, we in this paper characterize the unique extremal graph with the maximum spectral radius among 1-tough graphs of order $n$ with $\delta(G)\geq a$ containing no $[a,b]$-factor.
item.dc:creator: Ting Xu, Ruifang Liu

item.title: The nabla operator, Hall--Littlewood polynomials and LLT polynomials
item.description:
arXiv:2610.16756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler conjectured that $(-1)^{n-\ell(\mu)}
abla\widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t]$ and $
abla\omega \widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t^{-1}]$ are Schur positive, and that $
abla\omega \widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t^{-1}]-
abla\omega \widetilde H_
u[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is Schur positive when $\mu$ dominates $
u$. The first statement follows from the compositional shuffle conjecture of Haglund, Morse, and Zabrocki, proved by Carlsson and Mellit. We prove the other two statements. All three statements also hold for $

item.dc:creator: Feng Gu, Mingyang Kang, Dun Qiu, Minhao Zhang

item.title: The weak cylinder conjecture for polynomial graphs of bounded degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.16803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ball's weak cylinder conjecture asserts that a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathrm{AG}(3,p)$ with at least $p$ non-determined directions is a union of $p$ parallel lines. We prove the conjecture for sets admitting a polynomial graph representation of total degree at most $D$, provided that $p>D^{9/2}$. More precisely, a non-cylindrical graph of degree $D\ge3$ satisfies $|\mathcal{N}_S|\le p+1-\lceil p/(D-1)\rceil$ under the same hypothesis. This bound is attained when $p\equiv1\pmod{D-1}$. The proof relates non-determined directions to permutation polynomials on parallel affine lines. A rigidity lemma for moving line restrictions, together with a reconstruction of their compositional components, bounds the number of contributing directions uniformly in $p$. Directions with affine restrictions are treated separately; all other contributions are bounded using geometric indecomposability and the Weil bound for plane curves.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Alessandro Giannoni

item.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
item.description: arXiv:2610.16818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Louf, Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Finite noncommutative coinvariant algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quotients of free associative algebras by the two-sided ideals generated by positive-degree symmetric, quasisymmetric, or free quasisymmetric polynomials. Free quasisymmetric functions give a word realization of the Malvenuto-Reutenauer Hopf algebra of permutations. For quotients on $n$ variables, finiteness in the symmetric and quasisymmetric cases follows from a theorem of Bergman--Isaacs when $n!$ is invertible in the field. Our main result is a nilpotence criterion for families of relations compatible with restriction to subalphabets. The criterion proves finiteness over every field for quasisymmetric, $r$-quasisymmetric, and free quasisymmetric coinvariants, with explicit degree bounds exponential in $n$ for fixed $r$. In the quasisymmetric and $r$-quasisymmetric cases, these improve the bounds inherited from Bergman--Isaacs. A principal application is to the free quasisymmetric case, where, for $n\geq3$, the group-invariant argument used for the symmetric case does not apply. For the symmetric quotient $C_n$, we prove that invertibility of $n!$ is also necessary for finiteness. In characteristic zero, an auxiliary presentation and the Golod--Shafarevich inequality give $\log\dim C_n\geq(1-o(1))n^5(\log n)^2$ as $n\to\infty$. The same inequality shows that quasisymmetric and free quasisymmetric coinvariant dimensions grow faster than every fixed power of $n!$. For all three families on several freely noncommuting alphabets, we determine all multigraded Hilbert series and, for symmetric coinvariants in characteristic zero, Frobenius characteristics from one-alphabet data. In characteristic zero, projection gives stable Schur multiplicities for compatible quotients in mixed commuting, anticommuting, and free alphabets.
item.dc:creator: Farid Aliniaeifard, Nantel Bergeron, Huilan Li, Shu Xiao Li

item.title: The quarter-point theorem for Gromov hyperbolic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.16932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gromov hyperbolicity measures the geometric complexity of metric spaces and metric graphs through geodesic triangles and four-point conditions. While calculating the exact continuous hyperbolicity constant $\delta^*(G)$ of a graph $G$ typically requires evaluating quadruples of points over an infinite metric continuum, discretizing this domain is a fundamental challenge in metric graph theory. In this paper, we study the continuous Gromov hyperbolicity constant via the Gromov product.
