Our main result, the Quarter-Point Theorem, establishes that the search space for quadruples $(x,y,z,w)$ attaining the exact hyperbolicity constant $\delta^*(G)$ can be reduced from the entire metric graph to a finite or discrete subset $J'(G)$, comprising solely the vertices, edge midpoints, and quarter-points of $G$. This result holds for every graph, finite or infinite. This theoretical result provides a considerably simplified combinatorial framework for calculating hyperbolicity in complex networks and metric graphs. Furthermore, we exploit this discretization to significantly improve classical results by establishing and structural bounds relating the global hyperbolicity constant $\delta^*(G)$ with its restrictions to vertices ($\delta_V^*(G)$) and midpoints ($\delta_J^*(G)$).
item.dc:creator: Walter Carballosa, Jesus Mendez, Rosalio Reyes, Jos\'e M. Sigarreta

item.title: On Intersection Hypergraph of Finite Non-Cyclic Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.16941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study various structural properties like girth, chromatic num ber, etc. of the intersection hypergraph on the subgroups of nite non-cyclic abelian group and we characterize for the star and hypertree structures. Fur thermore, we characterize hypergraphs which are embeddable on plane, torus and projective plane.
item.dc:creator: A N Ardra, S Ballal

item.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
item.description: arXiv:2610.16955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.
item.dc:creator: Vsevolod A. Pokhachevskiy, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are Boolean functions invariant under cyclic permutation of their variables and can be represented by binary necklaces. We express local sensitivity as a weighted bichromatic degree in the necklace quotient and derive an exact formula for the multiplicities between neighboring necklaces. For an odd prime number of variables, we obtain explicit sensitivity formulas and show that multiplicity corrections occur only on an asymptotically negligible family of necklaces. For monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions, we prove that every odd-degree function has maximum sensitivity, determine the sensitivity of every quadratic function, and determine the sensitivity of the consecutive quartic family. We also determine exactly the sensitivity of cyclic run-threshold functions for arbitrary length and threshold.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Li, Jing Zhang

item.title: Construction of Regular Fat Linear Sets and Non-Representable q-Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.17055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power. An $(r, i)$-regular fat $\mathbb F_q$-linear set has exactly $r$ points of weight $i\ge2$, called fat points. All of its remaining points have weight one, and at least one such point occurs. We solve two open problems posed by three of the authors of this paper. First, we derive divisibility constraints on the point weights using the scalar stabilizer of the defining subspace. Consequently, a regular fat linear set of rank $2i$ in $\operatorname {PG}(1,q^n)$ has at most two or exactly $q + 1$ fat points. In the latter case, the fat points form an $\mathbb F_q$-subline. Second, we construct higher-dimensional regular fat linear sets whose fat points do not form an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry. In particular, for every $k\geq 3$ we obtain examples of rank $2k$ whose fat locus consists of an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry $\operatorname {PG}(k-2,q)$ in $\operatorname {PG}(k-1,q^4)$ together with one external point. This construction is then generalized further. Finally, we apply our projective-line results to $q$-matroid representability and present an infinite family of non-representable rank-two $q$-matroids arising from partial spreads.
item.dc:creator: Yufei Qiu, Valentino Smaldore, Zhenpeng Wang, Corrado Zanella, Ferdinando Zullo

item.title: Sustainable trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.17078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a connected graph and let $\lambda_1(X)$ denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. An edge $e$ of $X$ is sustainable if it can be deleted and replaced by a non-edge so that the resulting graph is connected and its spectral radius does not decrease; $X$ is sustainable if every edge is. We study this edgewise notion of spectral robustness for trees, where each replacement is an elementary exchange between trees on the same vertex set. We establish basic properties of sustainability and exhibit infinite families of sustainable and non-sustainable trees. Our main results concern trees with a vertex of large degree: if $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices with $\Delta(T)\geq n/2$, then every vertex of maximum degree is a principal vertex, that is, a vertex at which the Perron vector is maximal. Building on this, we prove that every tree with $\Delta(T)\geq n/2+1$ is non-sustainable, and we classify the sustainable trees in the boundary case $\Delta(T)=n/2$: for $n\geq 4$, the only such trees are the double broom $B(2,n/2,n/2-1)$ and one exceptional tree on eight vertices. We conclude with open problems on the generalized tree-shift order and the asymptotic proportion of sustainable trees.
item.dc:creator: Ferenc Bencs, Maarten van Dijk, Krystal Guo

item.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.17100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study block sensitivity and certificate complexity of rotation symmetric Boolean functions, with particular emphasis on monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions. We first show that every odd-degree monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables satisfies $s=bs=C=n$. We then determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity for every quadratic monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function. For the quadratic function $Q_{n,k}$ generated by $x_0x_k$, we prove, outside the short-orbit case, that \[ C(Q_{n,k})= \begin{cases} n,&4\mid n/\gcd(n,k),\\ n-\gcd(n,k),&4\nmid n/\gcd(n,k). \end{cases} \] Moreover, \(bs(Q_{n,k})=C(Q_{n,k})\) for every quadratic MRS function, and outside the short-orbit case, strict separation \(s<bs=C\) occurs exactly when \[ \frac{n}{\gcd(n,k)}\equiv2\pmod4. \] Finally, for the consecutive quartic family \[ R_n(x)=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z_n}x_ix_{i+1}x_{i+2}x_{i+3}, \] we determine all three measures in every residue class modulo $6$, using the sensitivity formulas and, in one residue class, finite-state results established in our companion preprint~\cite{LiZhangRSBFSensitivity}. In particular, for $r=2,3$ and $6q+r\ge5$ we obtain strict separation, \[ \boxed{s(R_{6q+r})=6q<bs(R_{6q+r})=C(R_{6q+r})=6q+1,\qquad r=2,3.} \] Thus this family gives an infinite collection of rotation symmetric Boolean functions for which sensitivity is strictly smaller than block sensitivity, while block sensitivity and certificate complexity coincide.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Li, Jing Zhang

item.title: The majority of a cactus is prickly
item.description: arXiv:2610.17107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterise all (undirected) cacti graphs, and forests of cacti, with an edge-preserving near-unanimity operation, by means of forbidden induced subgraphs. Indeed all such graphs also have an edge-preserving majority operation. We show that said majority can be chosen to be symmetric and explicitly construct it for all forests of cacti without the forbidden induced subgraphs.
item.dc:creator: Catarina Carvalho, Mathison Knight, Barnaby Martin

item.title: Chow polynomials and chain polynomials of matroids are not log-concave
item.description: arXiv:2610.17135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hilbert--Poincar\'{e} series of the Chow rings of the toric varieties of matroids, often called the \emph{Chow polynomials}, and the $f$-polynomial of their boundary complexes, called the \emph{chain polynomials}, have been conjectured to only have real zeros. We construct several explicit infinite families of matroids from finite geometries, whose multichain counts fail to be log-concave. They share a common geometric construction called \emph{hyperplane coalescence}, together with several classical operations in projective geometry and combinatorial designs. This induces failures of log-concavity for Chow, augmented Chow, chain, and $h$-polynomials of several explicit infinite families of matroids, disproving the real-rootedness conjectures of Ferroni--Schr\"oter, Huh--Stevens, and Athanasiadis--Kalampogia-Evangelinou from the lowest possible ranks. As an application of the same mechanism, we also give counterexamples to the log-concavity of $h$-polynomials of graph associahedra, answering in the negative a question of Sack.
item.dc:creator: Gergely B\'erczi, Basile Coron, Christopher Eur, Shiyue Li

item.title: Pushed colorful polytopal KKMS Theorem and orthogonal star transversals
item.description: arXiv:2610.17157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem of Kaiser and Rabinovich implies that if every subfamily of size at most $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ of a finite family of compact connected sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has a common axis-parallel hyperplane transversal, then the entire family has an orthogonal star transversal, i.e., a union of $d$ hyperplanes, one perpendicular to each coordinate axis. We study colorful variants of this result. First, we use standard KKM machinery to establish a colorful analogue with $d+1$ color classes and a $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ transversal hypothesis for rainbow subfamiles. Then we focus on reducing the required number of colors. To this end, we introduce the rainbow pushability $\pi_r(P)$ of a polytope and we use it to state and prove few-color variants of the colorful Carath\'eodory theorem and the colorful polytopal KKMS theorem. Applying the latter to the $d$-dimensional cube, we show that $\lfloor\log_2 d\rfloor+2$ color classes suffice for our transversal problem, provided that every rainbow choice has a common axis-parallel hyperplane transversal. We also extend both colorful results to the setting of convex $(n,D)$-bodies and we show that three colors are needed for $d\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Mart\'inez-Sandoval, Ariadna Olvera-Sampieri

item.title: A Generalisation of Maximal $(k,b)$-Linear-Free Sets of Integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.17188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix integers $k,b,q$ with $k\ge 2,b\ge 0,q\ge 2$. Define the function $p$ to be: $p(x)=kx+b$. We call a set $S$ of integers $(k,b,q)$-linear-free if $x\in S$ implies $p^i (x)\notin S$ for all $i=1,2,\dots,q-1$, where $p^i (x)=p\left(p^{i-1}(x)\right)$ and $p^0 (x)=x$. Such a set $S$ is maximal in $[n]:=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ if $S\cup \{t\},\forall t\in [n]\backslash S$ is not $(k,b,q)$-linear-free. Let $M_{k,b,q} (n)$ be the set of all maximal $(k,b,q)$-linear-free subsets of $[n]$, and define $g_{k,b,q} (n)=\min_{S\in M_{k,b,q} (n)}|S|$ and $f_{k,b,q} (n)=\max_{S\in M_{k,b,q} (n)}|S|$. In this paper, formulae for $g_{k,b,q} (n)$ and $f_{k,b,q} (n)$ are proposed. Also, it is proven that there is at least one maximal $(k,b,q)$-linear-free subset of $[n]$ with exactly $x$ elements for any integer $x$ between $g_{k,b,q} (n)$ and $f_{k,b,q} (n)$, inclusively.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Combinatorial Mathematics and Combinatorial Computing 120, no. 1 (2024) 315-21
item.dc:creator: Minh Quang Nguy\^en

item.title: Integer decomposition property of three-dimensional smooth polytopes: a shorter proof
item.description: arXiv:2610.17270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oda's smoothness conjecture asserts that every smooth lattice polytope has the integer decomposition property. The three-dimensional case of this conjecture was recently proven by AI. Here we give a much shorter proof of this result.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Curtis, Gaku Liu

item.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
item.description: arXiv:2610.17394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[ \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.
item.dc:creator: Ziqin Feng

item.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2610.17441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Daisey

item.title: Another Brick in the Wall: A Computationally Assisted Proof of an Improved Upper Bound for Thrackles
item.description: arXiv:2610.17508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a thrackle, where a thrackle is a graph drawing in which each edge meets every other edge exactly once, either at a vertex or at a crossing. It is conjectured that, for all thrackles, the number of edges is less than or equal to the number of vertices. Fulek and Pach created a program to determine whether or not a graph can be a thrackle. Through a reconstruction and improvement of their algorithm, we computationally prove a key dumbbell to be non-thrackleable. Using this exclusion, we improve Xu's 8-face half-edge bound from five to four. Finally, using this stronger restriction with Xu's framework, together with separate arguments for graphs containing triangles and disconnected graphs, we improve the known upper bound toward this conjecture to $m\le1.385(n-1)$ for $n\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Truman Scoppetto

item.title: On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4
item.description: arXiv:2610.17548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case. For connected rank-$4$ chain graphs, we derive four explicit equations in the cell parameters that are necessary and sufficient for generalized cospectrality. These equations reduce to a quadratic equation in a single parameter. As a consequence, every connected rank-$4$ chain graph has at most one generalized cospectral mate, and the possible mate can be reconstructed explicitly. We further obtain a simple sufficient condition for a rank-$4$ chain graph to be determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) and, in particular, prove that every double star graph is DGS. Finally, we construct an explicit infinite family of non-double-star rank-$4$ chain graphs that are DGS but not determined by their adjacency spectra, with both the graphs and their complements being connected.
item.dc:creator: Wei Wang, Siqi Wu

item.title: The $\ell$-degree Tur\'an densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies
item.description: arXiv:2610.17558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Tur\'an density $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=\alpha$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$. This confirms the conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao on codegree Tur\'an densities for every $k > 3$. As an immediate consequence, the set $\Gamma^{k,\ell}_{\infty}$ of $\ell$-degree Tur\'an densities of nonempty $k$-graph families is $[0,1)$ whenever $k>\ell>2$, which answers a question of Lo and Markstr\"om from 2014.
item.dc:creator: Hao Lin, Wenling Zhou

item.title: On extending induced subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$. Second, we establish how to grow $H$ inside $G$ while preserving twin-freeness and certain forms of connectivity. Third, we establish {\it finite test theorems} for various graph classes, proving that agreement with the recursively generated graphs for a few initial iterations forces agreement at all subsequent iterations. Consequently, such an infinite graph family can be completely determined by finitely many of its initial generations. As an application, we characterize $\{\mathbb L_1,\mathbb L_3\}$-free graphs, where $\mathbb L_1$ is the claw and $\mathbb L_3$ is another forbidden graph for line graphs. Our structural results reduce this problem to a finite verification, which is completed through computer-assisted computation.
item.dc:creator: Guoli Ding, Jake Weber, Weihao Xia

item.title: Clean handshake sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.17602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.
item.dc:creator: John Byrne, Colby Sherwood, Ioannis Tsokanos, Brian Wilmarth

item.title: Lattice Bruhat intervals are polytopal
item.description: arXiv:2610.17798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Bruhat interval $[x,y]$ in an arbitrary Coxeter group which is a lattice, we give a type-uniform construction of a convex polytope whose complete face lattice realizes $[x,y]$. This gives a polytopal realization of the coincidence between classical Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for lattice Bruhat intervals and Stanley's toric $g$-polynomials. Consequently, the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial of a lattice Bruhat interval cannot have internal zeros, satisfies a multiplicative strengthening of monotonicity, and obeys the generalized upper bound theorem for polytopes. For lattice Bruhat intervals in finite Weyl groups, we explain the relation with the toric geometry of Richardson varieties and derive formulas for their local and global intersection cohomology, as well as a Boolean criterion for rational smoothness. We conjecture that the coefficients of these Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials form an $M$-sequence.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Gao, Tao Gui

item.title: Counting triangles in graphs without suspensions of paths
item.description: arXiv:2610.17839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $H$, the suspension $\widehat H$ of $H$ is a graph obtained from $H$ by joining a new vertex to every vertex of $H$. The generalized Tur\'an number $\textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat H)$ is the maximum number of triangles in an $n$-vertex $\widehat H$-free graph. For fixed $k \ge 4$, Mubayi and Mukherjee conjectured that \[ \textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat P_k) =\left\lfloor\frac{k-2}{2}\right\rfloor\frac{n^2}{8}+o(n^2), \] as $n \to \infty$, where $P_k$ is the path on $k$ vertices. They verified the conjecture for $k=4,5,6$. In this paper, we determine the asymptotic value of $\textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat P_k)$ for every $k\ge 4$ via a unified approach and thus prove the conjecture of Mubayi and Mukherjee.
item.dc:creator: Chunyang Dou, Xing Peng

item.title: The chromatic number of $G$-stable Kneser graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extending the notions of Kneser graphs and Schrijver graphs, we define the $G$-stable Kneser graph $KG(G,k)$ (where $k\geq 2$ and $G$ is a graph on $n\geq 2k$ vertices) as the graph whose vertices are the $k$-element independent sets in $G$ and whose edges join pairs of disjoint independent sets. The well-known result of Lov\'{a}sz on the chromatic number of Kneser graphs implies that $\chi(KG(G,k)) \leq n-2k+2$ for any $G$. We call $G$ $k$-tight if equality holds, and we study the following question: Which graphs are $k$-tight? A result of Daneshpajouh et al.\ implies a characterization of $2$-tight graphs. We prove a necessary condition for a graph to be $k$-tight for $k\geq 3$ which extends this characterization, and we conjecture it to be sufficient. Another result gives a lower bound to the chromatic number of the $G$-stable Kneser graphs when $G$ is a disjoint union of cycles. We use this result to give a short proof of the fact that $4$-regular graphs on $3k$ vertices consisting of two vertex-disjoint cycles and $k$ cycles of length $3$ admit an independent set of size $k$.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, Tom\'{a}\v{s} Kaiser, Mat\v{e}j Stehl\'{i}k

item.title: The logarithmic exponent of the Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that $r(4,t) \ge \frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}$. This improves the lower bound of Mattheus and Verstra\"ete (Ann. of Math., 2024) by a factor of $(\log t)^{2-o(1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Qizhong Lin, Qiuyang Zhang

item.title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
item.description: arXiv:2610.17988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Clarke

item.title: Colored Tur\'an densities and finite directed templates
item.description: arXiv:2610.17992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Tur\'an theory relates the asymptotic extremal problem for an ordinary forbidden graph to its chromatic number. This principle fails when a forbidden copy must respect prescribed vertex colors, as occurs naturally in multipartite extremal problems and in embeddings with prescribed clusters. We study properly vertex-colored graphs whose hosts have a prescribed density between every pair of color classes, with containment interpreted through color-preserving homomorphisms. Our main theorem gives a finite directed reduction: for every fixed $m$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently many-colored $d$-dense host admits a colored homomorphism from an $m$-layer half-blowup $D[m]$ of a finite digraph $D$ with density at least $d-\varepsilon$, where $D$ may be chosen with $\lceil\varepsilon^{-1}\rceil$ vertices. Consequently, the colored Tur\'an density of every non-empty finite forbidden family equals the homomorphism Tur\'an density of its associated acyclic orientations. We then determine the complete finite value set: these densities are exactly the Lagrangians of finite loopless digraphs, and hence are rational. The main technical input is a low-resolution sampling method that preserves all pairwise bipartite degree profiles on a large subfamily of color classes while keeping the sample size independent of the number of retained classes.
item.dc:creator: Nannan Chen, Ander Lamaison, Heng Li, Hong Liu

item.title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
item.dc:creator: Marta Messia, Ferdinando Zullo

item.title: Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products
item.description: arXiv:2610.18152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl. Math., 2013]. Furthermore, we characterize the divisor lattices admitting alternating Hamilton paths and cycles.
item.dc:creator: Yuxian Dong, Jianxi Mao

item.title: A counting proof for the smallest critical set in a Latin square
item.description: arXiv:2610.18199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A critical set in a Latin square is a set of entries that determines the square uniquely and is minimal with this property. We prove that every partial Latin square of order $n$ with fewer than $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ filled cells has an even number of completions. Consequently every critical set in every Latin square of order $n$ has at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ entries. Since the cyclic Latin square has a critical set of exactly this size, the minimum size of a critical set over all Latin squares of order $n$ is $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. This confirms a conjecture attributed to Nelder (1979) and made independently by Mahmoodian and by Bate and van Rees. Hatami and Qian had shown that this minimum is at least $n^2/10^4$ for large $n$. The proof is a counting argument modulo two that uses only expansion of products, cancellation in pairs and the pigeonhole principle, and it is illustrated with partial Latin squares of orders three to seven. An appendix discloses the substantial use of AI in developing the proof and writing the exposition.
item.dc:creator: Richard Bean

item.title: On Chen's conjecture for the log-concavity of the longest increasing subsequence distribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.18235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P_{n,k}$ count permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. Chen conjectured that $(P_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave for every positive integer $n$. In this paper, we prove that Chen's conjecture is true when $n\ge 10^{10^{65}}$. The proof combines Gessel's determinantal formula with quantitative coefficient extraction, Tracy--Widom density estimates, and exact inequalities for the extreme lengths.
item.dc:creator: Ernest X. W. Xia

item.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.18239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and F\'eray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for odd cycles I: The dense regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.18277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goodman proved a lower bound on triangle counts which, in graphon language, states that every graphon of edge density $p$ has triangle density at least $2p^2-p$. Bennett, Dudek, Lidick\'{y}, and Pikhurko established the corresponding bound for $C_5$, determining its minimum density at every Tur\'an density $p=1-1/k$ with an integer $k\ge3$. We extend this bound to every odd cycle in the dense regime: for every odd integer $m\ge3$ and every graphon $W$ with edge density $p\ge2/3$, $t(C_m, W) \ge p^m-p(1-p)^{m-1}.$ For $2/3\le p<1$, equality holds precisely for balanced complete $k$-partite graphons with an integer $k\ge3$, up to graphon equivalence, and we establish qualitative stability at these densities. In the same density range, we also strengthen Kim and Lee's density-sensitive commonality inequality for odd cycles by adding the nonnegative term $t(P_{m-1},1-W)-(1-p)^{m-1}$ to the lower bound, where $P_{m-1}$ is the path with $m-1$ edges. To prove the main results, we develop a spectral excursion expansion and use Dirichlet averaging to reduce the resulting polynomial inequalities in arbitrarily many spectral variables to a one-variable problem. We prove the one-variable inequality through a uniform inequality comparing odd and even moments of shifted Gamma random variables. We also formalise the odd-cycle lower-bound theorem in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Seonghyuk Im, Taeyoung Kim, Hongseok Yang

item.title: Prescribed and simultaneous failures of log-concavity in trees with perfect matchings
item.description: arXiv:2610.18340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct trees with perfect matchings and independence sequences that fail log-concavity near the independence number $\alpha$. For every integer $k\geq1$, one family fails at $\alpha-k$ and has a witness of order $O(k^2\log(k+2))$. For every integer $t\geq2$, a single tree has simultaneous failures at $\alpha-1,\alpha-3,\ldots,\alpha-(2t-1)$, with a witness of order $O(t^3)$. All these trees satisfy $\alpha=N/2$, where $N$ is the number of vertices, and contradict Conjecture 4.2 of Ramos and Sun. A sufficient condition uses a fixed tree and the numbers of attached leaves. For fixed $k$ or $t$, explicit bounds give geometric decay of $a_j^2/(a_{j-1}a_{j+1})$ at these indices as the trees grow; $a_j$ counts independent $j$-sets. The proofs count independent sets by empty matching pairs. The Lean proof assistant checks formal proofs of the parameterized results and their quantitative bounds; exact 90- and 180-vertex examples illustrate the constructions.
item.dc:creator: Heshun Fan

item.title: On the existence of $F$-irregular graphs for disconnected graphs $F$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a given graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if all its vertices have pairwise distinct $F$-degrees, where the $F$-degree of a vertex $v$ is the number of subgraphs of $G$ containing $v$ and isomorphic to $F$. While the existence of $F$-irregular graphs has been actively studied for connected graphs $F$, the case where $F$ is disconnected remains entirely unexplored. In this paper, we provide a complete solution to this problem. We prove that for every disconnected graph $F$ with $|E(F)| \ge 2$, there exist infinitely many $F$-irregular graphs. Conversely, if $|E(F)| \le 1$, we show that no non-trivial $F$-irregular graph exists.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Dovzhenok

item.title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
item.description: arXiv:2610.18377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. The latter conjecture implies the former. In this paper, we prove a stronger result concerning coefficientwise nonnegativity of another power series, which implies the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton. The proof uses a M\"obius correction from Gaussian polynomials, weight-preserving injections on partitions, explicit linearly independent vectors in the kernel of a derivation operator and the KOH identity.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Zhang Ai, Lili Mu, Bao-Xuan Zhu

item.title: Ramsey properties of trees and $C$-relations via the partite construction
item.description: arXiv:2610.18402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite convexly ordered binary branching $C$-relations have been viewed as a notable exception to the broad applicability of the partite construction in structural Ramsey theory. The absence of a proof of their Ramsey property by the partite construction was noted by Bodirsky in his 2015 survey and pointed out again by Hubi\v{c}ka and Kone\v{c}n\'y in their 2026 survey. We overcome this limitation by giving proofs based on the partite construction of the known Ramsey properties of the class $\mathcal{CT}$ of finite convexly ordered treeable meet semilattices and of the classes of finite convexly ordered $C$-relations with arbitrary branching and with binary branching. Our proofs do not rely on Milliken's tree theorem. The key is to expand $\mathcal{CT}$ by level predicates and a predecessor function so that the locally finite subclass method applies. We then transfer the resulting Ramsey witnesses to the corresponding reduct classes and to the classes of convexly ordered $C$-relations.
item.dc:creator: Hyoyoon Lee

item.title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.18463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed. We offer partial results on which groups can appear as leap groups, and study hops and leaps for infinite and directed graphs.
item.dc:creator: Mark Schachner, Gabe Udell

item.title: Tur\'an numbers of triangular pyramids
item.description: arXiv:2610.18493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\TP_k$ denote the triangular pyramid with $k$ layers. For a graph family $\mathcal F$, let $\ex(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal F$ as a subgraph. For a graph $H$, let $\cJ(H)$ be the family of subgraph-minimal graphs among all such graphs $H-I$, where $I\subseteq V(H)$ is an independent set. For every integer $k\ge4$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that \[ \ex(n,\TP_k)=\max_{0\le m\le n}\{m(n-m)+\ex(m,\cJ(\TP_k))\}+O_k(n)=\left\lfloor n^2/4\right\rfloor+\Theta_k(n^{4/3}). \] Moreover, for $k=4$, we characterize all extremal graphs and show that \[ \ex(n,\TP_4)=\max_{0\le m\le n}\bigl\{m(n-m)+\ex\big(m,\cJ(\TP_4)\big)\bigr\} \] for sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Chuanqi Xiao, Long-Tu Yuan, Xiaowen Zhang

item.title: High-Arity Rademacher Complexity and Uniform Laws of Large Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.18528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize several properties of higher-arity function classes, specifically finite $\VC_k$-dimension, slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension, and finite slicewise Littlestone dimension, in terms of generalizations of Rademacher complexity. These characterizations sets up simple new proofs of several results on finite $\VC_k$-dimension and slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension. These include the preservation of finite $\VC_k$-dimension under taking expectations and uniform law of large numbers statements for both properties. All of these results apply naturally to real-valued function classes as well as boolean-valued classes. We also prove a new adversarial uniform law of large numbers for classes with finite slicewise Littlestone dimension.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Anderson, Henry Towsner

item.title: Spectral radius and edge-disjoint spanning trees of graphs with edge connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.18574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\tau(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees contained in a graph $G$. Zhang and Fan [J. Graph Theory, 2026] posed the problem of determining the corresponding tight spectral-radius condition for every $s$-edge-connected graph with \[ k+1\leq s\leq2k-1, \] together with a characterization of the associated extremal graphs. In this paper, we completely resolve this problem.
item.dc:creator: Jia Wei, Muhuo Liu, Zhifu You, Hong-Jian Lai

item.title: Saturation and semisaturation of oriented graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a natural extension of the classical saturation problem to oriented graphs, defined as the minimum number of edges in an oriented graph $H$ on $n$ vertices that avoids a fixed oriented graph $G$, but adding any missing edge to $H$ creates a copy of $G$. Our main result shows that saturation functions of oriented graphs attain at least four distinct orders of magnitude. In particular, if $G$ is acyclic, then its saturation function is bounded if and only if $G$ contains an isolated edge; otherwise, it is linear. Certain tournaments together with an isolated edge give further infinite examples of bounded and linear saturation functions. Two additional orders of magnitude are $\Theta(n \sqrt{\log n})$ and $\Theta(n \log n)$. For these two, the lower bounds are obtained by adapting a recently developed approach for the saturation problem in edge-ordered graphs, while the matching upper bounds are constructive. Finally, we study the semisaturation problem, in which we require only that adding any missing edge to $H$ creates a copy of $G$. We completely characterize the possible orders of magnitude: the semisaturation function is either bounded, linear, or $\Theta(n \log n)$.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Bo\v{s}kovi\'c, Bal\'azs Keszegh

item.title: Two conjectures on the cospectrality of complete tripartite graphs are false
item.description: arXiv:2610.18636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph G of order n with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), the cospectrality of G within the set G of all graphs of order n is the smallest spectral distance from G to another graph of G. Abdollahi and Zakeri conjectured that for every n >= 4 the cospectrality of the complete tripartite graph K_{n,n,n}, both in the Manhattan and in the Euclidean spectral distance, is attained precisely at K_{n-1,n,n+1}. We show that both conjectures are false for every n >= 4, that is, in the whole range in which they are stated. The counterexample is the graph H_n obtained from K_{n-1,n,n} by adding a vertex adjacent to the part of cardinality n - 1, and it is the natural generalization of the graph which the authors themselves exhibited for n = 3 and considered to be exceptional. We determine the spectrum of H_n in a closed form, and we show that the two spectral distances tend to 1 and to 1/2 respectively, instead of to (2*sqrt(3))/3 and to 2/3 as conjectured. On the other hand, we show that in the Euclidean distance the conjecture becomes asymptotically true when the competing graphs are restricted to complete multipartite graphs, so that it fails because a graph of rank four beats the conjectured minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

item.title: Proofs of four Takigiku--Tsuchioka conjectures on level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove four conjectures of Takigiku and Tsuchioka consisting of eight Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Two conjectures involve triple sums and a third involves quadruple sums, and their product sides are certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{13}^{(2)}$. The fourth conjecture gives multisum representations of certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$. The proofs rely on the Bailey pair method, finite sum identities involving Gaussian polynomials, and the quintuple product identity.
item.dc:creator: Liuquan Wang

item.title: A proof of the rational exponents conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.18713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rational exponents conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Simonovits asserts that for every rational $r\in [1,2]$ there exists a graph $H$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)=\Theta(n^r)$. We present a proof of this conjecture claimed by Epoch AI, explaining how it builds upon ideas and methods developed by many researchers.
item.dc:creator: David Conlon, Oliver Janzer, Tao Jiang, Jaehoon Kim, Joonkyung Lee, Hong Liu, Sean Longbrake, Liana Yepremyan

item.title: Szemer\'edi's theorem with random differences and arithmetic Kakeya
item.description: arXiv:2610.18859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there exists an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that the following holds for every $k \ge 3$ and $p \ge n^{-c / \log \log k}$. Letting $\delta > 0$ and $D \sim [n]_p$, with high probability every ${S \subset [n]}$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ contains a $k$-term arithmetic progression whose common difference lies in $D$. This improves the best known bounds for the threshold of Szemer\'edi's theorem with random differences for all sufficiently large $k$, previously of the form ${p \ge n^{-2/k+o(1)}}$, due to Bri\"et and Castro-Silva. We obtain our improvement via a small cover lemma, in the sense of Alon and Pham's work on random Cayley graphs, and its proof crucially relies on a construction of Green and Ruzsa in the context of the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture. The usage of the latter was suggested to us by GPT 6 Astra.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dahia

item.title: Jensen's inequality on parity classes of jump M-convex functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Jensen's inequality on each coordinatewise parity class of a jump $M$-convex function on $\mathbb{Z}^n$, without assuming strong base orderability or a finite effective domain. If a finite convex combination of domain points has its barycenter in the same parity class, then the barycenter belongs to the domain and satisfies Jensen's inequality. We also prove that every domain point admits an affine support on its entire parity class. The set of support vectors is characterized by at most $3^n-1$ local inequalities, which yield optimality certificates, attained duality, and an exact formula for linear growth and stability under linear perturbations. The same conclusions hold for distributions with finite first moment supported on domain points of a single parity class, provided their mean lies in that class. We characterize equality by contact sets and give a quantitative bound on the Jensen gap. The proof combines induction on dimension with the known closure under infimal convolution: convolution with an even-box indicator gives finite-domain supports, a quadratic kernel proves barycenter feasibility, and a fixed local kernel yields global supports. A two-dimensional example shows that total parity alone does not suffice.
item.dc:creator: Xinyue Liu

item.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.13972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$, where the cylinders are the same size as the ball, is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, resolved recently. We also make progress on a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman, confirming the first decimal digit of their predicted value for the largest radius of four non-overlapping cylinders that touch a ball.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.
item.dc:creator: Annalisa Cesaroni, Matteo Novaga

item.title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
item.description: arXiv:2610.13983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is $p^{1+o(1)}$ as $p\to\infty$. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus $p=4$ marks the boundary: $n+1$ is exact in every dimension for $2\leq p\leq4$, while at every fixed finite $p>4$ the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers, Aran S. Ziegler

item.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.14032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.
item.dc:creator: Sohail (Neel), Sarkar

item.title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.14037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[ \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025). More generally, the same inequality holds for finite positive Borel measures. The main input is a uniform $L^2$ estimate, at cap thickness comparable to lattice spacing, for a supporting-direction incidence operator. In gnomonic coordinates, this operator is controlled by an incidence estimate for small Fenchel--Young gaps.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Korsky

item.title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Li

item.title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope. The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued). The lack of symmetry in the set of potential solutions leads to new questions and phenomena, such as the distribution of the coordinate sizes in typical solutions, and requires the development of new information-theoretic techniques to deal with higher-dimensional optimization problems arising in the method of moments.
item.dc:creator: Dylan J. Altschuler, Ruben Ascoli, Will Perkins

item.title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo A. Podest\'a, Denis E. Videla

item.title: Explicit Solutions in a Probabilistic Cellular Automaton Model for Self-Assembled Monolayer Degradation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), formed by the adsorption of a monomolecular layer of adsorbate onto a surface, have emerged as leading candidates for plat- forms for electrochemical biosensors. In order to characterize the working age of a SAM-based biosensor, it is necessary to understand the long-term degradation of the monolayer, with particular emphasis on the intermolecular forces present in the self-assembly process. In this work, discrete- and continuous-time proba- bilistic cellular automaton (PCA) models for the degradation of SAMs involving adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are proposed in which adsorbate molecules desorb at a rate dependent only on the number of adsorbed neighbors. Impor- tantly, we make no assumptions on the relationship between degradation rate and adsorbed neighbors. Using techniques from generating function theory and complex analysis, the expected degradation curve is solved for explicitly in one dimension and shown to be a sigmoid curve related to the Gompertz function.
item.dc:creator: Wes Caldwell, Ryan Evans, Jacob Majikes, Anthony Kearsley

item.title: Bipartite Carrier Compression and Machine-Certified Bounds in Sch\"onhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.14263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-\kappa}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Sch\"onhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles in h=25), reducing the global physical wire width by 377,890 wires from the reviewed baseline W = 177,284,805 down to W = 176,906,915. Evaluated over the exact 10^{-14} rational grid, this wire reduction certifies an improved second-moment coefficient AB = 5,164,059 / 125,000,000,000 and establishes the sharpened conditional exponent \kappa = 826,215,307 / 20,000,000,000,000 \approx 4.131076535 \times 10^{-5}, strictly surpassing the preceding record on this architecture (\kappa \approx 4.123864 \times 10^{-5}). All 47 polynomial constraints and 7 rational security margins are audited in exact Q-arithmetic with zero floating-point error, and the fundamental wire reduction identity is formally verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover without unproven axioms.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}

item.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Libedinsky

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Pairwise Compatibility Graphs of Unweighted Caterpillars
item.description: arXiv:2610.14681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study pairwise compatibility graphs whose witness tree is required to be an unweighted caterpillar. This is a natural restriction of PCGs, in the same line of research as the study of star witnesses, which led to the class of double-threshold graphs. In the caterpillar case, we show that this restriction is equivalent to a one-dimensional difference-labelling problem: a graph admits such a representation if and only if its vertices can be assigned integer labels so that adjacency is determined exactly by whether the absolute difference of two labels belongs to a given interval. Using this characterization, we derive structural properties of the class, including bounded twin-width, and study its relation with familiar graph families. We show that the class contains cycles and two-dimensional grids, while it excludes natural obstructions such as the subdivided star $S_{2,2,2,2,2}$, the cube graph $Q_3$, the wheel $W_6$, and the complement of the $3$-sunlet. We also consider restricted representations, including centipede witnesses and representations with a given interval and we give a polynomial-time recognition algorithm when the interval is fixed.
item.dc:creator: Cyriac Antony, Manuel Lafond, Angelo Monti, Blerina Sinaimeri

item.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.14991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincar\'e duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He, Qingchao Yu

item.title: Almost every Boolean function has central threshold degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.15057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The polynomial threshold degree (or threshold degree) of a Boolean function is the least degree of a real polynomial whose sign represents it. We prove that almost every Boolean function has polynomial threshold degree among the central one or two integers. More precisely, a uniformly chosen Boolean function on $n$ variables has threshold degree $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/2\rceil$ except with probability at most $\exp(-c2^{n/2}/n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. A parity example gives a lower bound on the exceptional probability whose exponent differs from ours by a factor of order $n$. The proof relates polynomial sign representation to recovery of Reed--Muller codes from random erasures, and combines sharp-threshold estimates with bounds on generalized Hamming weights and minimum distance.
item.dc:creator: Martin Anthony

item.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.
item.dc:creator: Luis Arenas-Carmona, Claudio Bravo, Ignacio Saavedra

item.title: Quantum Pick's Theorem in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider an $n$-dimensional sum of the form $S_k=\sum{q^{f({\bf z})}}$ over lattice points ${\bf z}$ which lie in $K{\mathcal P}$, the $K$ scaling of an $n$-dimensional rational polytope $\mathcal P$. We formulate a conjecture on the structure of $S_K$ considered for $K$ prime, as a power series in $h=q-1$ modulo the $K^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial, and in particular the existence of a decomposition in powers of the Gauss sum $\mathbb G$, up to the $n^{th}$, whose coefficients are almost independent of $K$, where the leading coefficient is related to the volume of $\mathcal P$ and the coefficient of ${\mathbb G}^r$ has contributions from the codimension $r$ skeleton of $\mathcal P$. The conjecture is proved for $n=1,2$.
item.dc:creator: Moris Metin Bardavid, Ruth Lawrence

item.title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.15265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehl\'{e} and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehl\'{e}, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.
item.dc:creator: Thijs Laarhoven

item.title: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
item.description: arXiv:2610.15288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\in\Lambda_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$. The proof uses a Gaussian-integer model in which lattice automorphisms arising from Clifford unitaries transform a vector into a pair of coordinate subvectors in a lower-dimensional lattice. Divisibility of the differences of their squared norms and a matrix Parseval identity provide the arithmetic and averaging constraints needed for induction on $m$. Every listed norm is realized explicitly by a sum of two minimal vectors of the lattice.
item.dc:creator: Yuhang Cao, Sihuang Hu, Hexiang Huang, Mengrui Yang

item.title: Quadratic polynomials preserving free infinite divisibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.15320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize non-commutative polynomials of degree 2 which preserve free infinite divisibility as self-adjoint Lie polynomials of degree 2. This extends previous results which characterized homogeneous quadratic forms only. The proof is based on an involution of colored noncrossing partitions cancelling many terms; positive definiteness of the remaining terms is established by an explicit operator model on Fock space. Examples show that higher order Lie polynomials do not preserve free infinite divisibility.
item.dc:creator: Wiktor Ejsmont, Franz Lehner, Mihai Popa, Kamil Szpojankowski

item.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Motegi

item.title: A Four-by-Four Obstruction to Polynomial Removal for Ordered Binary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.15370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We exhibit a fixed $4\times 4$ binary matrix with no polynomial induced ordered removal bound. At depth $h\geq 1$, let $m=2^h$. Our explicit host has order $(14h+2)m$, exactly $2m^6+\frac{1}{2}(m-2)m^5$ induced copies, and exact editing distance $m^2$ cells. Its normalized editing distance is $\Theta(h^{-2})$, while its induced-copy density is $\Theta(4^{-h}h^{-8})$. The lower bound holds against arbitrary cell edits through an injective family of $m^2$ protected selections. An exhaustive arithmetic classification identifies every induced copy and proves that a matching canonical repair creates none. The original-copy transversal number is exactly $m$, yielding an unbounded gap between hitting existing copies and eliminating all copies. The identities and the obstruction at every depth are formalized in Lean, with verification sources included as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: Zinan Wang

item.title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Qiang Chen, Xin-Yue Yan

item.title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
item.description: arXiv:2610.15468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{\Omega(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Laso\'{n}, and Przyby\l{}o [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Ku\v{c}era [Ku\v{c}91], who showed that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^{\epsilon}$ on which FirstFit uses $\Omega(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $\chi(G) = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Yaqiao Li, Xin Li

item.title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.15550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.
item.dc:creator: Lev Vladimirov

item.title: K_1 of matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.15551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.
item.dc:creator: Thor Wittich

item.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $\mu_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Jimenez Ramos

item.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.15785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.
item.dc:creator: Jaume de Dios Pont, Jan Greb\'ik, Rachel Greenfeld, Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15826v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the recent study of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations of finite groups by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of finite groups, with particular emphasis on the abelian case. These structures form a natural relaxation of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and encompass several related families that have previously been studied in different contexts. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Donald L. Kreher, Shuxing Li, Douglas R. Stinson

item.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.
item.dc:creator: Serge Feukoua, Ana S\u{a}l\u{a}gean, Pantelimon St\u{a}nic\u{a}

item.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
item.description: arXiv:2610.16025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class.
