In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024]. Our theorem generalizes the QPTASes for axis-parallel rectangles [Adamaszek and Wiese, FOCS 2013] and polygons [Adamaszek, Har-Peled, and Wiese, JACM 2019], or equivalently for packing connected subgraphs of a planar graph [Pilipczuk, van Leeuwen, and Wiese, Algorithmica 2020]. It also generalizes the QPTAS for MWIS on hereditary classes with strongly sublinear separators measured in vertices [Dvo\v{r}\'ak, EJC 2018; Dvo\v{r}\'ak and Lahiri, ESA 2021], as well as the QPTASes for graphs excluding particular induced minors [Chudnovsky et al., arXiv 2025; Bonnet et al., SWAT 2026; Czy\.zewska et al., arXiv 2026].
item.dc:creator: \'Edouard Bonnet, Yeonsu Chang

item.title: On Mattila's intersection problem in the plane: sharp dimension and positive measure of rotated difference sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.16114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let \(A,B\subset\R^2\) be nonempty Borel sets. We prove that \[ \dimH(gA-B)\ge\min\{\dimH A+\dimH B,2\} \] for almost all \(g\in\mathrm O(2)\). This bound is sharp in general, and the proof gives a corresponding statement for the lower Hausdorff dimension of convolutions of Frostman measures. We also prove that \(\LL^2(gA-B)>0\) for almost all \(g\) if both dimensions exceed \((\sqrt{13}-1)/2\). The second result follows from an angular decomposition, refined decoupling and a two-ends Furstenberg estimate. Some applications on intersection patterns are also addressed.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen, Dung The Tran

item.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
item.description: arXiv:2610.16332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The proof combines a Bruhat atlas compatible with total positivity and a CL-labeling of the augmented face poset. The atlas models the strata locally with open Richardson varieties in the flag variety of a larger Kac-Moody group and identifies their totally nonnegative cells.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He, Kaitao Xie

item.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Tur\'{a}n problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.16358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed graph $T$ and a fixed nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman~[Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. The previously established general cases for this conjecture include $\operatorname{ex}(G, K_2, \mathcal{F})$ by Alon, Shapira and Sudakov~[Ann. of Math., 2009], and $\operatorname{ex}(G, K_m, K_k)$ by Alon and Shikhelman. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for every bipartite graph $T$ and every clique $T$. Our reductions use iterative leaf additions, symmetric rooted extensions and random transversals to encode the maximum number of edges in a $(k-1)$-colorable subgraph of $G$, where $k=\min_{F\in \mathcal{F}}\chi(F)$.
item.dc:creator: Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Xihe Li, Jie Ma, Tianying Xie

item.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Luperi Baglini, Boris \v{S}obot

item.title: AI Discovery in Combinatorics: From Problems to Solutions and Back to Bigger Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.16555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce $qt$Bench, a benchmark of 29 open problems in algebraic combinatorics. These problems ask for a simple combinatorial algorithm that explains given polynomial coefficients or identities. To help AI agents search for such algorithms, we provide a scaffold for playing with combinatorial objects, countering cheating attempts, and testing candidate solutions. To explore how far frontier AI systems can go on these problems, we collaborated with OpenAI, whose researchers obtained proposed solutions to several of them. This highlights bigger meta-problems: is AI discovery at scale ethical? How should these results be released? How should proof digestion be organized? We discuss these questions and give our views.
item.dc:creator: Eugenio Cainelli, Lorenzo Luccioli, Alessandro Iraci, Giovanni Paolini

item.title: Period Piece: NEXPTIME-complete problems on digraphs via Boolean network dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.16561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The central object in this work is the Boolean network, a function $f:\{0,1\}^V \to \{0,1\}^V$. Often identified with $f$ is its dynamics $D_f$, the digraph with exactly $\{x \to y : f(x)=y\}$ as its arcs. The interaction graph of $f$ is the digraph $G$ on $V$ which can be thought of as representing the dependencies of the components of $f$ on one another. On the other hand, model-checking is a major field of study in graph algorithms and complexity. We consider problems at the intersection of these paradigms: for a given property $\phi$, we say that a digraph $G$ is $\phi$-dynamic if $G$ is the interaction graph of some Boolean network $f$ such that $D_f \models \phi$. The corresponding decision problem $\phi$-DYNAMIC asks whether $G$ is $\phi$-dynamic. Problems of this form are well-studied in the Boolean networks community. For example, it is a well-known result that, letting $\phi$ be 'No fixed points' (i.e. $\nexists x:x\to x$), $\phi$-DYNAMIC is equivalent to the structural digraph problem NON-ACYCLIC, which is solvable in linear time. We establish, for the first time, properties $\phi$ for which $\phi$-DYNAMIC is computationally hard. These include the 'Unique fixed point' property $\exists!x:x\to x$, and a range of properties concerning the periodic points of $f$ (i.e. vertices of $D_f$ which lie on a cycle). More widely, we exhibit an infinite family of natural properties $\phi$ such that $\phi$-DYNAMIC is $\mathrm{NEXPTIME}$-complete, which we call PERIOD PIECE. As a special case, these include all properties of the form 'Unique cycle of length $k$' and 'Exactly $k$ fixed points' for any $k \ge 1$. On the other hand, we show that if the input digraph has bounded in-degree, then for those same problems $\phi$-DYNAMIC collapses down to $\mathrm{NP}^{\mathrm{NP}}$, the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, though it remains $\mathrm{NP}^{\mathrm{NP}}$-complete.
item.dc:creator: Florian Bridoux, Maximilien Gadouleau, David C. Kutner, Adrien Richard

item.title: The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $\left[\!\left[ -m,m \right]\!\right]^d$ having a support of size $d+1$. When $d=2$, we find the exact value of this maximal length for all $m \ge 2$, as well as the exact structure of all extremal sequences for this problem. When $d=3$, we obtain lower and upper bounds that asymptotically match each other as $m$ tends to infinity. This allows us to improve on the best known lower bounds for the Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Girard, Alain Plagne

item.title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component. At each truncation level, we obtain the dimension of this variety via a novel Witt-type formula. We propose a Chen-Chow theorem for membranes, provably at the second truncation level, and conjecturally for higher levels with extensive computational evidence in the computer algebra system OSCAR.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Am\'endola, Gabriel Riffo, Leonard Schmitz

item.title: On a Combinatorial Characterization of Abelian Group Actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$ and $X$ a finite $G$-set. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on $G$ for any $X$ to be determined up to isomorphism by certain combinatorial data. Specifically, if $M_H^X$ is the number of $H$-orbits in $X$, and $a_d^X$ is the number of $G$-orbits in $X$ of cardinality $d$, we characterize when equalities $M_H^{X_1} = M_H^{X_2}$ and $a_d^{X_1}=a_d^{X_2}$ for all $H \leq G$ and $d|n$, respectively, force an isomorphism $X_1 \simeq X_2$. Our main result is that this occurs if and only if $G$ is cyclic or $G$ is the direct sum of a finite cyclic group and a cyclic group of prime order. We conclude with an arithmetic application to $L$-function factorization.
item.dc:creator: Carson Gull, Arthur Illidge, Benjamin Mudrak, Joshua Park, Shaver Phagan

item.title: Exponential Local Search in Bounded-Occurrence MAX-CSP
item.description: arXiv:2610.16898v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the number of improving steps that local search may require for $(2,2,r)$-MCA (Maximum Constraint Assignment), a bounded-occurrence version of MAX-CSP with valued constraints in which every constraint involves at most two variables, every variable occurs in at most two constraints, and every variable takes one of $r$ values. We consider the flip neighborhood, where two assignments are neighbors if they differ in the value of exactly one variable; moving to such a neighbor is called a flip. Local search repeatedly performs improving flips, that is, flips that strictly increase the objective value, until a local optimum is reached. Our main result is that $(2,2,5)$-MCA has the all-exp property: there is an infinite family of instances with initial assignments for which every sequence of improving flips ending in a local optimum has length exponential in the number of variables. Thus, on these instances, local search requires exponentially many steps regardless of which improving flip is chosen at each step. This is the first all-exp result for $(2,2,r)$-MCA for any value of $r$, and our result extends to every $r\ge 5$. In contrast, for $(2,2,2)$-MCA every sequence of improving flips has length at most quadratic in the number of variables~\cite{Kaz2020,KCJ2020}. We give a short, direct proof of this result.
item.dc:creator: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

item.title: Graph Distortion Distances, Gromov-Hausdorff and the Hardness of Gromov-Wasserstein
item.description: arXiv:2610.16926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the computational complexity of graph distortion distances, a family of graph metrics measuring how vertex distances differ between two graphs. Formally, these distances are defined in terms of standard matrix norms on the difference of distance matrices under an optimal vertex alignment. The resulting metrics have natural interpretations, corresponding to three ways of measuring the distortion of shortest-path distances: the maximum distortion among all vertex pairs (entrywise maximum norm), global aggregation (entrywise $p$-norms), and local aggregation (operator $p$-norms) of distortions. For maximum distortion, we show that approximation below a factor of two is NP-hard even for highly restricted trees. Due to the close connection to the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, we obtain a similar hardness result for the latter. In both cases, we show essentially optimal additive inapproximability. On the algorithmic side, we give a subcubic-time algorithm for optimal embeddings of connected graphs into paths, based on a structural decomposition along a diametral path. Additionally, we give a simple approximation algorithm when one input graph has a "relatively path-like" metric structure, i.e. has bounded pathlength. For local and global distortion, we derive various hardness results even for restricted inputs. Making use of a close connection between the global distortion distances and Gromov-Wasserstein distances, we give the first formal proof of NP-hardness of the latter, which has been claimed in the literature many times but has, to the best of our knowledge, never been correctly proven.
item.dc:creator: Jens Breitung, Timo Gervens, Julius P\"orzgen

item.title: Solomon--Terao Algebras: Top Degree, Dimension, and Homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.16951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Solomon--Terao algebra and the Solomon--Terao complex of a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal A$ in $\mathbb C^\ell$. Let $\eta$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d\geq2$ whose restriction to every flat of $\mathcal A$ has no critical point away from the origin. We prove that the Solomon--Terao algebra $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,\eta)$ has top degree $|\mathcal A|+\ell(d-2)$ and a one-dimensional top graded component with an explicit generator, solving a conjecture of Abe, Maeno, Murai, and Numata. For $d=2$, we show that the total dimension of $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,\eta)$ is bounded below by that of the Orlik--Solomon algebra. Both results hold without assuming that the arrangement $\mathcal A$ is tame. Finally, we prove that $\mathcal A$ is tame if and only if all positive-degree homology groups of the Solomon--Terao complex associated with $\eta$ vanish.
item.dc:creator: Hanyu Cai, Haiyang Chen, Shixuan Zeng, Shanwei Zhang

item.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.16963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincar\'e inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Kassel, Thierry L\'evy

item.title: Whither quantum advantage? New classical lower bounds for Max-Cut on large-girth 3-regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every 3-regular graph of girth at least $g$ has a cut containing at least a fraction $M_g$ of its edges, and the best rigorous bounds at large girth are $0.912\le \lim_{g\to\infty}M_g \le 0.92386$. Lower bounds on $M_g$ follow from the performance of local algorithms: on a graph of girth $g \ge 2p+2$ a depth-$p$ local algorithm sees the same tree around every edge, so its expected cut fraction on that tree bounds $M_g$ from below. We apply this strategy to the Variational Iterative Rotation Algorithm (VIRAL), a classical local algorithm, and evaluate it on the depth-$p$ tree for every even depth up to $p=32$. The resulting bounds exceed those recently obtained from the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for every $p\ge 4$, by $0.005$ to $0.011$, and they extend the range of girths covered from $g=36$ to $g=66$. Notably, at $g=66$ we obtain $M_{66} \ge 0.9127$ at $99.99999\%$ confidence level, which raises the asymptotic lower bound from $0.912$ to $0.9127$.
item.dc:creator: Flaviano Morone, Shivang Rawat, Dries Sels

item.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.17525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang

item.title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.17631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $\theta$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto x\theta(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.
item.dc:creator: Shixin Wang, Shikang Yu, Tao Feng

item.title: A Minimum Exact Disjunctive Basis for Two-Robot Solvability Profiles
item.description: arXiv:2610.17677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We completely characterize the solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movements. The four standard capability models and the schedulers considered here have a known quotient order Q of thirteen computational classes. A task's solvability profile is the set of classes in which it is solvable, and is necessarily an upset of Q. We prove that every upset is realizable and construct a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen concrete tasks. The basis contains one task for each principal upset. For every antichain of Q, the disjunction of the corresponding tasks has profile exactly equal to the union of their profiles. This exactness is not implied by the individual profiles: an algorithm may satisfy different disjuncts in different executions. We establish it by constructing, for every algorithm in each maximal class outside the target union, a single admissible fair execution violating all selected predicates simultaneously. Consequently, the realizable profiles form the entire finite distributive lattice Up(Q): there are exactly 54 profiles, counted by the antichain polynomial 1 + 13z + 24z^2 + 16z^3, and each has a canonical disjunctive representation using at most three principal tasks. We also identify six tasks whose solvability signatures recover every inclusion and incomparability in Q, and prove that six is minimum even among arbitrary separating tasks. Their profiles are precisely the principal upsets generated by the join-irreducible elements of Q. In contrast, any task family generating every profile by exact disjunctions must contain all thirteen principal profiles. Thus our exact disjunctive basis has minimum size and is unique at the profile level.
item.dc:creator: Tsukasa Ninomiya, Shota Naito, Naoki Kitamura, Yuichi Sudo, Koichi Wada

item.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Liwski

item.title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
item.description: arXiv:2610.18319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $\sigma^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $\psi(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $\sigma(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $\sigma^*(q)$.
item.dc:creator: Nargish Punia, Rahul Kumar

item.title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.18371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (\pi) }s(\pi) \left( \ell(\pi) - s(\pi) \right). \end{equation*} In the present paper, we provide a combinatorial proof of the above identity and extend the result for $p^{(k)}(n)$, where $p^{(k)}(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ distinct part sizes.
item.dc:creator: Archit Agarwal, Meghali Garg

item.title: Full classification of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.18409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}^n$. A $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive code. A recursive construction gives such codes $H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$, of type $(n;t_1,\dots,t_s)$ and length $p^t$, and a partial classification of them is known. In this paper, we complete the classification of these codes for every prime $p$. The main tool is the derived code, obtained by puncturing the code outside a block of coordinates determined by its kernel. For a nonlinear code $H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$ with $t_1\geq2$, the derived code is a $\mathbb{Z}_{p^{s-1}}$-linear GH code of the same family, although the mechanism for odd $p$ differs from the binary one. As a consequence, for $t\geq3$, there are $\mathcal P(t+1)-\mathcal P(t)$ nonequivalent such codes of length $p^t$ if $p$ is odd, and $\mathcal P(t+1)-\mathcal P(t)-1$ if $p=2$, where $\mathcal P(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$. In particular, this completes the classification of the $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes. We also prove a conjecture on the codes with $t_1\geq2$ and $t_s=0$.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K. Bhunia

item.title: Multidimensional Szemer\'edi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.18657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a new approach to the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture of Bergelson, Leibman, and Lesigne for commuting transformations. The conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and, consequently, to the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'edi theorem. We establish the conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials, obtaining the first general result for sequences of arbitrary length beyond the classical one-transformation setting. Our argument is inspired by the Furstenberg-Katznelson approach and its polynomial enhancement due to Bergelson-Leibman. Its main novelty, however, lies in the development of new techniques that allow us to bypass the use of the polynomial van der Waerden theorem, on which these methods traditionally rely, and for which no suitable analogue is currently available in our setting. In particular, we prove a Nil-Bohr returns theorem for compact extensions in systems with nilpotent structure, as well as a nil-plus-null decomposition for polynomial multicorrelation sequences that preserves joint intersectivity and positivity.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Davide Sclosa

item.title: A Randomized Approximation Algorithm for Doubly Free-Boundary Macdonald Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.18698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries. We derive local reconstruction kernels from the skew Cauchy, Littlewood, and branching identities. Bulk and boundary updates combine integer increments with conditional shape sampling at a prescribed size; same-sign swaps use finite conditional resampling. For $K$ reflection periods and an initial partition-size cutoff $M$, the algorithm terminates almost surely and samples the resulting approximating law exactly. We prove total variation convergence to the target process as $K,M\to\infty$ and give explicit bounds for both truncation errors, decaying geometrically in the cutoffs for fixed input parameters. Under fixed parameter bounds, we also bound the expected operation count of direct enumeration in a unit-cost model. We further construct an exact rejection sampler for the initial partition law without a size cutoff or evaluation of its normalizing constant. Using this sampler removes the size-truncation error, leaving only the error from the finite reflection history.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
item.description: arXiv:2610.18740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $V_i(n)$ denote the minimum worst-case number of comparisons needed to find the $i$-th smallest of $n$ distinct elements. We construct algorithms showing $V_7(16)\le28$ and $V_8(16)\le29$, improving the previously reported upper bounds of 30 and 31. Together with known lower bounds, these results establish $V_7(16)=28$ and leave $V_8(16)\in\{28,29\}$. For 17 elements, we establish $V_5(17)=27$ and improve the upper bounds for ranks 6 through 9 to 29, 30, 31, and 31, respectively. Every new upper bound has an explicit decision-graph certificate verified by a static checker developed independently of the search. We also derive a lower bound for selection from a partially ordered state by combining the Fussenegger-Gabow weight with its order-reversed counterpart. All new upper bounds and this lower bound are formally verified in Lean 4. For $V_8(16)$, we show that a lower bound based solely on the total number of decision-tree leaves cannot establish $V_8(16)\ge29$. The algorithms were found using fixed-budget search, information-guided comparison ordering, and proof-number search. Proof-number search was decisive in finding the 28-comparison algorithm; in our experiments, refuting a comparison budget remained substantially more expensive than finding an algorithm within it.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Cremer

item.title: Boolean dimension and dim-boundedness: Planar cover graph with a zero
item.description: arXiv:2206.06942v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1989, Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il and Pudl\'ak posed the following challenging question: Do planar posets have bounded Boolean dimension? We show that every poset with a planar cover graph and a unique minimal element has Boolean dimension at most $10$. As a consequence, we are able to show that there is a reachability labeling scheme with labels consisting of $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ bits for planar digraphs with a single source. The best known scheme for general planar digraphs uses labels with $\mathcal{O}(\log^2 n)$ bits [Thorup JACM 2004], and it remains open to determine whether a scheme using labels with $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ bits exists. The Boolean dimension result is proved in tandem with a second result showing that the dimension of a poset with a planar cover graph and a unique minimal element is bounded by a linear function of its standard example number. However, one of the major challenges in dimension theory is to determine whether dimension is bounded in terms of standard example number for all posets with planar cover graphs.
item.dc:creator: Heather Smith Blake, Piotr Micek, William T. Trotter

item.title: Partition regularity of infinite parallelepiped sets
item.description: arXiv:2212.06887v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A proper infinite parallelepiped (IP) set in a semigroup is an infinite set consisting of a sequence $\myseq{a}$ and its finite sums, or a superset of such a set. Hindman's theorem asserts that the proper IP sets of natural numbers are partition regular: for each finite coloring of a proper IP set of natural numbers there is a monochromatic proper IP subset. Furstenberg generalized this question to arbitrary semigroups, in which the analogous result does not hold in general. We provide a complete classification of the semigroups for which the proper IP sets are partition regular, and show that this property is equivalent to other fundamental notions of additive Ramsey theory.
item.dc:creator: Yonatan Gadot, Boaz Tsaban

item.title: A grid theorem for strong immersions of walls
item.description: arXiv:2301.05134v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a graph contains a large wall as a strong immersion minor if and only if the graph does not admit a tree-cut decomposition of small 'width', which is measured in terms of its adhesion and the path-likeness of its torsos.
item.dc:creator: Reinhard Diestel, Raphael W. Jacobs, Paul Knappe, Paul Wollan

item.title: Monochromatic non-commuting products
item.description: arXiv:2405.03772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a finite coloring of an amenable group contains `many' monochromatic sets of the form $\{x,y,xy,yx\},$ and natural extensions with more variables. This gives the first combinatorial proof and extensions of Bergelson and McCutcheon's non-commutative Schur theorem. Our main new tool is the introduction of what we call `quasirandom colorings,' a condition that is automatically satisfied by colorings of quasirandom groups, and a reduction to this case.
item.dc:creator: Matt Bowen

item.title: The spiders $S(4m+2,\,2m,\,1)$ are $e$-positive
item.description: arXiv:2405.04915v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the composition method, we establish the $e$-positivity of spiders of the form $S(4m+2,\, 2m,\, 1)$, as conjectured by Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang. Following a divide-and-conquer strategy, we group one or two positive-coefficient $e_J$-terms with each negative-coefficient $e_I$-term, where each $J$ is a composition obtained by rearranging the parts of the composition $I$, and prove that the resulting total coefficient is nonnegative. Our main contribution is the explicit construction of the required injections.
item.dc:creator: Davion Q. B. Tang, David G. L. Wang, Monica M. Y. Wang

item.title: Ultra log-concavity and real-rootedness of dependence polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2408.09152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For some positive integer $m$, a real polynomial $P(x)=\sum\limits_{k=0}^ma_kx^k$ with $a_k\geqslant 0$ is called {log-concave} (resp. ultra log-concave) if $a_k^2\geqslant a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ (resp. $a_k^2\geqslant \left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{m-k}\right)\cdot$ $a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$) for all $1\leqslant k\leqslant m-1$. If $P(x)$ has only real roots, then it is called {real-rooted}. It is well-known that the conditions of log-concavity, ultra log-concavity and real-rootedness are ever-stronger. %A famous theorem due to Newton states that if a real polynomial with non-negative coefficients is real-rooted, then it is log-concave. For a graph $G$, a dependent set is a set of vertices which is not independent, i.e., the set of vertices whose induced subgraph contains at least one edge. The dependence polynomial of $G$ is defined as $D(G, x):=\sum\limits_{k\geqslant 0}d_k(G)x^k$, where $d_k(G)$ is the number of dependent sets of size $k$ in $G$. Horrocks proved that $D(G, x)$ is log-concave for every graph $G$ [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 84 (2002) 180--185]. In the present paper, we prove that, for a graph $G$, $D(G, x)$ is ultra log-concave if $G$ is $(K_2\cup 2K_1)$-free or contains an independent set of size $|V(G)|-2$, and give the characterization of graphs whose dependence polynomials are real-rooted. Finally, we focus more attention to the problems of log-concavity about independence systems and pose several conjectures closely related the famous Mason's Conjecture.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Y.-T. Xie, S.-J. Xu, Ultra log-concavity and real-rootedness of dependence polynomials, Electron. J. Combin., 33(4) (2026), #P4.9
item.dc:creator: Yan-Ting Xie, Shou-Jun Xu

item.title: Complete tripartite subgraphs of balanced tripartite graphs with large minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2411.19773v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1975 Bollob\'{a}s, Erd\H{o}s, and Szemer\'{e}di asked what minimum degree guarantees an octahedral subgraph $K_3(2)$ in any tripartite graph $G$ with $n$ vertices in each vertex class. We show that $\delta(G)\geq n+2n^{\frac{5}{6}}$ suffices thus improving the bound $n+(1+o(1))n^{\frac{11}{12}}$ of Bhalkikar and Zhao obtained by following their approach. Bollob\'{a}s, Erd\H{o}s, and Szemer\'{e}di conjectured that $n+cn^{\frac{1}{2}}$ suffices and there are many $K_3(2)$-free tripartite graphs $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq n+cn^{\frac{1}{2}}$. We confirm this conjecture under the additional assumption that every vertex in $G$ is adjacent to at least $(1/5+\varepsilon)n$ vertices in any other vertex class.
item.dc:creator: Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Allan Lo, Cong Luo, Jie Ma, Yi Zhao

item.title: Almost-full transversals in equi-$n$-squares
item.description: arXiv:2412.07733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1975, Stein made a wide generalisation of the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture on transversals in Latin squares, conjecturing that every equi-$n$-square (an $n\times n$ array filled with $n$ symbols where each symbol appears exactly $n$ times) has a transversal of size $n-1$. That is, it should have a collection of $n-1$ entries that share no row, column, or symbol. In 2017, Aharoni, Berger, Kotlar, and Ziv showed that equi-$n$-squares always have a transversal with size at least $2n/3$. In 2019, Pokrovskiy and Sudakov disproved Stein's conjecture by constructing equi-$n$-squares without a transversal of size $n-\frac{\log n}{42}$, but asked whether Stein's conjecture is approximately true. I.e., does an equi-$n$-square always have a transversal with size $(1-o(1))n$? We answer this question in the positive. More specifically, we improve both known bounds, showing that there exist equi-$n$-squares with no transversal of size $n-\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ and that every equi-$n$-square contains $n-n^{1-\Omega(1)}$ disjoint transversals of size $n-n^{1-\Omega(1)}$. Furthermore, we give results for the corresponding problem in globally-bounded colourings of complete graphs, as part of the wider framework of coloured complete directed graphs.
item.dc:creator: Debsoumya Chakraborti, Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Richard Montgomery, Teo Petrov

item.title: Scales, products and the second row of the Scheepers diagram
item.description: arXiv:2503.18615v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider products of sets of reals with a combinatorial structure based on scales parameterized by filters. Sets of this kind have been extensively investigated in products of spaces with combinatorial covering properties such as the Hurewicz, Scheepers, Menger, and Rothberger properties. We will complete this picture by focusing on properties from the second row of the Scheepers diagram. We solve in the affirmative a problem due to Bartoszy\'nski-Tsaban, whether all finite powers of a $\mathfrak{b}$-scale set satisfy the strong covering property $\mathsf{S}_1(\Gamma,\Omega)$. We also show that, in the Miller model, the product of finitely many $\mathfrak{d}$-concentrated sets satisfies $\mathsf{S}_1(\Gamma,\Omega)$. We further provide product counterexamples demonstrating limitations of the methods used.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Pawlikowski, Piotr Szewczak, Lyubomyr Zdomskyy

item.title: On the number of edges of restricted matchstick graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.01589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph whose vertices are points in the plane and whose edges are noncrossing straight-line segments of unit length is called a \emph{matchstick graph}. We prove two somewhat counterintuitive results concerning the maximum number of edges of such graphs in two different scenarios. First, we show that there are triangle-free matchstick graphs on $n$ vertices with more edges than the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ grid. On the other hand, every triangle-free matchstick graph on $n$ vertices has at most $2n-c\sqrt{n}$ edges for some $c > 0$. Second, we prove that for every $r>0$, there is a constant $\varepsilon(r)>0$ with the property that, if $n$ is sufficiently large, every matchstick graph on $n$ vertices contained in a disk of radius $r$ has at most $(2-\varepsilon(r))n$ edges.
item.dc:creator: Panna Geh\'er, J\'anos Pach, Konrad Swanepoel, G\'eza T\'oth

item.title: Bivariate asymptotics via random walks: application to large genus maps
item.description: arXiv:2506.06924v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain bivariate asymptotics for the number of (unicellular) combinatorial maps (a model of discrete surfaces) as both the size and the genus grow. This work is related to two research topics that have been very active recently: multivariate asymptotics and large genus geometry. Our method consists of studying a linear recurrence for these numbers, and can be applied to many other linear recurrences. In particular, we include a general theorem that yields asymptotics for such recurrences, provided that some assumptions are satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Elvey Price, Wenjie Fang, Baptiste Louf, Michael Wallner

item.title: The Origami flip graph of the $2\times n$ Miura-ori
item.description: arXiv:2506.19700v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an origami crease pattern $C=(V,E)$, a straight-line planar graph embedded in a region of $\mathbb{R}^2$, we assign each crease to be either a mountain crease (which bends convexly) or a valley crease (which bends concavely), creating a mountain-valley (MV) assignment $\mu:E\to\{-1,1\}$. An MV assignment $\mu$ is locally valid if the faces around each vertex in $C$ can be folded flat under $\mu$. In this paper, we investigate locally valid MV assignments of the Miura-ori, $M_{m,n}$, an $m\times n$ parallelogram tessellation used in numerous engineering applications. The origami flip graph $OFG(C)$ of $C$ is a graph whose vertices are locally valid MV assignments of $C$, and two vertices are adjacent if they differ by a face flip, an operation that swaps the MV-parity of every crease bordering a given face of $C$. We enumerate the number of vertices and edges in $OFG(M_{2,n})$ and prove several facts about the degrees of vertices in $OFG(M_{2,n})$. By finding recurrence relations, we show that the number of vertices of degree $d$ and $2n-a$ (for $0\leq a$) are both described by polynomials of particular degrees. We then prove that the diameter of $OFG(M_{2,n})$ is $\lceil \frac{n^2}{2}\rceil$ and find lower bounds on the diameter of $OFG(M_{m,n})$ using techniques from $3$-coloring reconfiguration graphs.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications, Vol. 30, No. 1 (2026), 421-444
item.dc:creator: Lumi Christensen, Thomas C. Hull, Emma O'Neil, Valentina Pappano, Natalya Ter-Saakov, Kacey Yang

item.title: On the homogeneity problem of the Kazhdan-Lusztig ideals
item.description: arXiv:2506.20153v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, our purpose is to find some techniques to identify inhomogeneous Kazhdan-Lusztig ideals. A set of generators of a Kazhdan-Lusztig ideal corresponds to some minors in some southwest submatrices inside some ambient matrix. We have defined a notion called a path inside a square matrix as a tool to work with determinants of the above mentioned minors. Using paths, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for when such minors are inhomogeneous, singular, non-singular, and when there is divisibility between two terms of two such distinct minors. As a conclusion, we first provide an algorithm through which we can identify some sufficient conditions for a Kazhdan-Lusztig ideal to be inhomogeneous (by utilizing all the above mentioned results). Secondly, we provide certain sufficient conditions for a Kazhdan-Lusztig ideal to be standard homogeneous, and then we also prove that under certain assumptions, these conditions are also necessary for a Kazhdan-Lusztig ideal to be standard homogeneous.
item.dc:creator: Adhip Ganguly, Shyamashree Upadhyay

item.title: Mutations of quivers with 2-cycles
item.description: arXiv:2508.15022v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a mutation theory for quivers with oriented 2-cycles using a structure called a homotopy, defined as a normal subgroupoid of the quiver's fundamental groupoid. This framework extends Fomin-Zelevinsky mutations of 2-acyclic quivers and yields involutive mutations that preserve the fundamental groupoid quotient by the homotopy. It generalizes orbit mutations arising from quiver coverings and allows for infinite mutation sequences even when orbit mutations are obstructed. We further construct quivers with homotopies from triangulations of marked surfaces with colored punctures, and prove that flips correspond to mutations, extending the Fomin-Shapiro-Thurston model to the setting with 2-cycles.
item.dc:creator: Fang Li, Siyang Liu, Lang Mou, Jie Pan

item.title: Separable convex optimization over indegree polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2509.06182v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study separable discrete convex optimization over indegree vectors of orientations of an undirected graph, focusing on the effect of imposing acyclicity. Since the extreme points of the indegree polytope are precisely the indegree vectors of acyclic orientations, this amounts to comparing optimization over its integer points with optimization over its extreme points. Over all orientations, minimizing a vertex-separable discrete convex objective is strongly polynomial-time solvable by minimum-cost flow. Over acyclic orientations, for every fixed discrete convex function shared by all vertices, we obtain a dichotomy: if the function is linear on the positive integers, the problem is solvable in linear time; otherwise exact optimization is NP-hard on connected simple graphs, and APX-hard when the function is non-negative. We also give strongly polynomial-time constant-factor approximation algorithms for broad classes of convex and concave objectives. For the $p$-power sum of indegrees, this yields a $2^p$-approximation for every fixed integer $p\geq1$, while the problem is APX-complete for every fixed integer $p\geq2$; if $p$ is part of the input, no deterministic polynomial-time $2^{p^{1-\varepsilon}}$-approximation exists for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$ unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. We further give an exact $O(2^{|V|}|V|+\operatorname{poly}(|V|,|E|))$-time dynamic program for general separable objectives, with a matching lower bound in the exponent under the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Finally, decreasingly minimal and increasingly maximal acyclic orientations need not coincide and are both NP-hard, while minimizing the maximum weighted indegree over acyclic orientations remains strongly polynomial-time solvable.
item.dc:creator: N\'ora A. Borsik, P\'eter Madarasi

item.title: Hook immanantal inequalities for totally nonnegative matrices
item.description: arXiv:2510.00327v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a weakly decreasing positive integer sequence $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\dotsc,\lambda_\ell)$ summing to $n$, let $\chi^\lambda$ denote the irreducible character of the symmetric group $S_n$ indexed by $\lambda$. This representation has dimension $\chi^\lambda(e)$, where $e$ is the identity element of $S_n$. Let $\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^\lambda}$ denote the corresponding irreducible character immanant, the function on $n \times n$ matrices $A = (a_{i,j})$ defined by $\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^\lambda}(A) := \sum_{w \in S_n} \chi^\lambda(w) a_{1,w_1} \cdots a_{n,w_n}$. Merris conjectured [Linear Multilinear Algebra 14 (1983) pp. 21--35] and Heyfron proved [Linear Multilinear Algebra 24 (1988) pp. 65--78] that irreducible character immanants indexed by ``hook'' sequences $(k, 1, \dotsc, 1)$ satisfy the inequalities $\mathrm{per}(A)=\frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^n}(A)}{\chi^{n}(e)}\geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{n-1,1}}(A)}{\chi^{n-1,1}(e)}\geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{ n-2,1,1}}(A)}{\chi^{n-2,1,1}(e)}\geq \cdots \geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{1,\dotsc,1}}(A)}{\chi^{1,\dotsc,1}(e)}=\det(A)$ whenever $A$ is an $n \times n$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix. We prove that the same inequalities hold whenever $A$ is an $n \times n$ totally nonnegative matrix.
item.dc:creator: Mark Skandera

item.title: Emerging consecutive pattern avoidance
item.description: arXiv:2511.02442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we study the asymptotic popularity, that is, the limit probability to find a given consecutive pattern at a random position in a random permutation in the eighteen classes of permutations avoiding at least two length 3 consecutive patterns. We show that for ten classes, this popularity can be readily deduced from the structure of the permutations. By combining analytical and bijective approaches, we study in detail two more involved cases. The problem remains open for five classes.
item.dc:creator: Nathana\"el Hassler, Sergey Kirgizov

item.title: Connectivity keeping trees in triangle-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.06622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2012, Mader conjectured that for any tree $T$ of order $m$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ with minimum degree at least $\lfloor \frac{3k}{2}\rfloor+m-1$ contains a subtree $T'\cong T$ such that $G-V(T')$ remains $k$-connected. In 2022, Luo, Tian, and Wu considered an analogous problem for bipartite graphs and conjectured that for any tree $T$ with bipartition $(X,Y)$, every $k$-connected bipartite graph $G$ with minimum degree at least $k+\max\{|X|,|Y|\}$ contains a subtree $T'\cong T$ such that $G-V(T')$ remains $k$-connected. In this paper, we relax the bipartite assumption by considering triangle-free graphs and prove that for any tree $T$ of order $m$, every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with minimum degree at least $2k+3m-4$ contains a subtree $T' \cong T$ such that $G-V(T')$ remains $k$-connected. Furthermore, we establish refined results for specific subclasses such as bipartite graphs or graphs with girth at least five.
item.dc:creator: Hojin Chu, Shinya Fujita, Boram Park, Homoon Ryu

item.title: Subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words
item.description: arXiv:2511.11069v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R_q(n)$ denote the number of rich words of length $n$ over a fixed alphabet of size $q\geq2$. It is known that $R_q(n)^{1/n}\to1$. We establish a nonrecursive subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words, with its asymptotic growth quantified in terms of an iterated logarithm. For every $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ and $\gamma>1$, there exists $c>0$ such that, for every positive function $\phi$ satisfying $\phi(n)\to\infty$ and $n/\phi(n)\to\infty$, the functions \[ f(n)=\left[c\ln^{*}\!\left(\frac{n}{\phi(n)}\ln q\right)\right]^{1/\gamma}, \qquad B(n)=q^{\frac{n}{\phi(n)}+\frac{n}{(2\lambda)^{f(n)-1}}} \] satisfy $R_q(n)\leq B(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and $B(n)^{1/n}\to1$. Here $\ln^{*}$ is the iterated natural logarithm, with value zero on $(0,1]$. The proof iterates a counting inequality based on palindromic factorization and controls the resulting multiplicative constants using the iterated logarithm.
item.dc:creator: Josef Rukavicka

item.title: Ramsey problems for graphs in Euclidean spaces and Cartesian powers
item.description: arXiv:2512.15516v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a graph $H$, let $\chi_H(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be the smallest positive integer $r$ such that there exists an $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with no monochromatic unit-copy of $H$, that is a set of $|V(H)|$ vertices of the same color such that any two vertices corresponding to an edge of $H$ are at distance one. This Ramsey-type function extends the famous Hadwiger--Nelson problem on the chromatic number $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)=\chi_{K_2}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of the space from a complete graph $K_2$ on two vertices to an arbitrary graph $H$. It also extends the classical Euclidean Ramsey problem for congruent monochromatic subsets to the family of those defined by a specific subset of unit distances. Among others, we show that $\chi_H(\mathbb{R}^n)=\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any even cycle $H$ of length $8$ or at least $12$ as well as for any forest and that $\chi_H(\mathbb{R}^n)=\lceil\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)/2\rceil$ for any sufficiently long odd cycle. Our main tools and results, which are of independent interest, establish that Cartesian powers enjoy Ramsey-type properties for graphs with favorable Tur\'an-type characteristics, such as zero hypercube Tur\'an density. In addition, we prove induced variants of these results, find bounds on $\chi_H(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for growing dimensions $n$, and prove a canonical-type result. We conclude with many open problems. One of these is to determine $\chi_{C_4}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, for a cycle $C_4$ on four vertices.
item.dc:creator: Maria Axenovich, Dingyuan Liu, Arsenii Sagdeev

item.title: Combinatorial formulas for Macdonald polynomials by superizations
item.description: arXiv:2602.12672v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we derive new combinatorial formulas for symmetric Macdonald polynomials $P_{\lambda}(X;q,t)$ and non-symmetric Macdonald polynomials $E_{\gamma}(X;q,t)$, in terms of several new statistics and the major index, for a partition $\lambda$ and a weak composition $\gamma$. Compared to previous formulas, these new formulas contain the fewest terms and lead to explicit $(q,t)$-formulas for the coefficients in the monomial expansion of $P_{\lambda}(X;q,t)$. In particular, the combinatorial formula for $E_{\gamma}(X;q,t)$ extends the one for $E_{\lambda}(X;q,t)$ indexed by a partition $\lambda$, due to Corteel, Mandelshtam and Williams (2022). Three existing formulas for $P_{\lambda}(X;q,t)$ established by Corteel, Mandelshtam and Williams (2022), by Corteel, Haglund, Mandelshtam, Mason and Williams (2022), and by Mandelshtam (2025) are recovered. Our proof relies on two new statistics on super fillings, employing the superization formulas of Haglund--Haiman--Loehr (2005) and Ayyer--Mandelshtam--Martin (2023), together with our recent approach to modified Macdonald polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin

item.title: Flips and Merge-Width in Sparse Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.12926v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A flip of a graph is obtained by complementing the edge relation within a set of vertices. Flips are typically used to separate vertices in a graph, by increasing the distances between them. We show that in $K_{t,t}$-free graphs, every short sequence of flips can be simulated by a short sequence of vertex deletions that achieves a similar degree of separation: distances in the resulting graph are, up to a factor of three, at least as large as those obtained after the flips. This result provides a simple and uniform explanation of an emerging pattern in structural graph theory and finite model theory: the $K_{t,t}$-free fragment of a tameness notion for dense graphs often coincides with a tameness notion for sparse graphs. As immediate applications, we recover the following known equivalences. In the $K_{t,t}$-free setting, the dense notions (1) bounded shrub-depth, (2) bounded clique-width, (3) bounded flip-width, (4) monadic dependence, respectively, coincide with the sparse notions (1) bounded tree-depth, (2) bounded tree-width, (3) bounded expansion, and (4) no-where dense-ness. Furthermore, we reprove the result by Dreier and Toru\'nczyk (STOC 2025) stating that $K_{t,t}$-free classes of bounded merge-width have bounded expansion. Our proof provides explicit bounds and is direct, as it shows how to construct strong coloring orders (witnesses of bounded expansion) from merge sequences (witnesses of bounded merge-width). Along the way, we identify a new family of graph parameters, dubbed separation-width, that is sandwiched between the strong and weak coloring numbers, and is closely related to the merge-width parameters. We provide evidence that this family of graph parameters, apparently overlooked in the literature, may play a fundamental role in the study of sparse graphs.
item.dc:creator: Karolina Drabik, Ma\"el Dumas, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Wojciech Przybyszewski, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: G\"odel Implication on Finite Chains: Catalan Enumeration and a Continuum Limit Law
item.description: arXiv:2602.16135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distribution of output values produced by all fully bracketed implication terms on $n$ distinct variables in G\"odel $m$-valued logic on the finite chain $V_m$. The Catalan decomposition of bracketings yields a stratified system of recurrences for the output counts. Passing to tail sums reduces this system to a finite iteration of a single map $\Phi_x$ and its inverse branch $\Psi_x$. For each fixed $m$, this reduction gives a common dominant square-root singularity at $r=1/(4m)$, coefficient asymptotics of order $(4m)^n n^{-3/2}$, and limiting proportions for every truth level. In the four-valued case these proportions are obtained explicitly in nested radicals. The main new phenomenon appears when the number of truth values also tends to infinity. If $K_m$ denotes the output level under the limiting $n\to\infty$ distribution and $X_m=K_m/(m-1)$, then $X_m\Rightarrow X$, where $X$ has density $(1+2t)^{-3/2}$ on $[0,1)$ together with an atom of mass $1/\sqrt{3}$ at $1$. In particular, the top mass converges to $1/\sqrt{3}$, while the bottom mass is asymptotic to $1/m$. We further show that the same probability law arises intrinsically when G\"odel implication is defined directly on $[0,1]$ and valuations are sampled from Lebesgue product measure: the continuum tail generating function satisfies an exact first-order differential equation whose critical specialization is the ODE appearing in the finite-chain Euler limit. We also record a root-split refinement whose pair-count generating functions factor as products of the level generating functions and inherit the same square-root scale.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Yildiz

item.title: The Smallest String Attractors of Fibonacci, Period-Doubling, and Thue--Morse Words
item.description: arXiv:2602.16152v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A string attractor of a string $T[1..|T|]$ is a set of positions $\Gamma$ of $T$ such that any nonempty substring $w$ of $T$ has an occurrence that crosses a position in $\Gamma$, i.e., there is a position $i$ such that $w = T[i..i+|w|-1]$ and the intersection $[i,i+|w|-1]\cap \Gamma$ is nonempty. The size of the smallest string attractor of Fibonacci words and period-doubling words of length at least $2$ is known to be $2$. The size of the smallest string attractor of Thue--Morse words of length at least $25$ is known to be $4$. We completely characterize the set of all smallest string attractors of Fibonacci words, period-doubling words, and Thue--Morse words. For Fibonacci words, we show a recursive formula describing the $2^{n-4} + 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil - 2}$ distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Fibonacci word for $n \geq 7$. For period-doubling words, we show that the $n$th period-doubling word has exactly two smallest string attractors for every $n\geq 2$, and give them explicitly. For Thue--Morse words, we show a formula describing the 32 sets of four positions that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Thue--Morse word for $n\geq 6$. Our results show that strings with the same smallest attractor size can have a drastically different number of distinct smallest attractors.
item.dc:creator: Mutsunori Banbara, Hideo Bannai, Peaker Guo, Dominik K\"oppl, Takuya Mieno, Yoshio Okamoto

item.title: An Ore-type Theorem for Oriented Discrepancy of Hamilton Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2603.18915v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Oriented discrepancy concerns the existence of prescribed subgraphs whose edges exhibit a substantial imbalance between the two directions. The Hamilton cycle case was first investigated by Gishboliner, Krivelevich, and Michaeli. Subsequently, Freschi and Lo established a sharp minimum-degree result and raised the question of whether a corresponding Ore-type theorem holds. For an oriented graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, define $\sigma_2(G):=\min\{d_G(x)+d_G(y):x\neq y,\ xy,yx\notin E(G)\},$ with $\sigma_2(G):=2(n-1)$ when $G$ is a tournament. Given a cycle $C$ in an oriented graph, let $\sigma_{\max}(C)$ denote the maximum number of edges oriented consistently with one of the two traversal directions of $C$. We prove that for every $\gamma>0$ there exists $n_0$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with $\sigma_2(G)\ge n$ contains a Hamilton cycle $C$ satisfying $$ \sigma_{\max}(C)\geq \max\left\{\frac n2,\frac{\sigma_2(G)}2-\gamma n\right\}. $$ This partially answers a question of Freschi and Lo and gives an asymptotic affirmative answer to a conjecture of Ai et al. The bound is asymptotically best possible.
item.dc:creator: Yufei Chang, Yangyang Cheng, Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei, Jin Yan

item.title: Note on the thickness of the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path
item.description: arXiv:2603.27968v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the thickness of the Cartesian product $K_{6p+4} \, \square \, P_2$ for $p \ge 0$ and of the Cartesian product $K_8 \, \square \, P_m$ for $m \ge 1$, where $K_n$ and $P_m$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices and the path on $m$ vertices, respectively. These are two of the three remaining cases from the results of Chen, Kohonen, and Yang (2026). Combined with their results, the thickness of $K_n \, \square \, P_2$ is completely determined.
item.dc:creator: Kenta Noguchi

item.title: Immanantal polynomials of the linear combination matrices of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.04489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The immanant is a generalized matrix function associated with irreducible characters of the symmetric group. The immanantal polynomial of matrix $M$ is defined as the immanant of matrix $(xI - M)$, where $I$ is the identity matrix. The characteristic polynomials and permanental polynomials of graph matrices (adjacency matrix, Laplacian matrix, signless Laplacian matrix and $A_{\alpha}(G)$ matrix) have been extensively studied, yielding fascinating results. As a unification of the characteristic polynomial and permanental polynomial, the immanantal polynomial has also attracted attention and led to several important findings. In this paper, we focus on the study of immanantal polynomials for linear combination matrices composed of the degree matrix and adjacency matrix of a graph. First, applying the concept of vertex orientation for general graphs, we provide a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the immanantal polynomials for the linear combination matrices of graphs, and we also characterize the bounds of these coefficients. These bounds implicitly encompass the existing results of Chan and Lam on trees and bipartite graphs. Furthermore, we give a solution to the open problem posed by Merris. Second, we characterize the first six coefficients of the hook immanantal polynomial. And the necessary and sufficient condition under which the linear combination matrices of two regular graphs have the same hook immanantal polynomial is proved. Third, we generalize the Frobenius--K\"onig theorem and the Laplace expansion theorem to immanants. Using these two theorems, we show that the star degree of a graph is always a lower bound for the multiplicity of a certain root of the immanantal polynomial of its linear combination matrix. Finally, we derive formulas for the first six coefficients of the hook immanantal polynomial for several important graph matrices.
item.dc:creator: Xiangshuai Dong, Tingzeng Wu

item.title: There exist Steiner systems $S(2,7,505)$ and $S(2,7,589)$
item.description: arXiv:2604.04975v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note two Steiner systems $S(2,7,505)$ and two Steiner systems $S(2,7,589)$ are presented. This resolves two of $21$ undecided cases for block designs with block length $7$, mentioned in Handbook of Combinatorial Designs.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Hetman

item.title: Stability and ribbon bases for the rank-selected homology of geometric lattices
item.description: arXiv:2604.06479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper analyzes the representation theoretic stability, in the sense of Thomas Church and Benson Farb, of the rank-selected homology of the Boolean lattice and the partition lattice, proving sharp uniform representation stability bounds in both cases. It proves a conjecture of the first author and Reiner by giving the sharp stability bound for general rank sets for the partition lattice. Along the way, a new homology basis sharing useful features with the polytabloid basis for Specht modules is introduced for the rank-selected homology and for the rank-selected Whitney homology of any geometric lattice, resolving an old open question of Bj\"orner. These bases give a matroid theoretic analogue of Specht modules.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hersh, Sheila Sundaram

item.title: 4-cycle-free induced subgraphs of grid graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.08397v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we consider sets $S$ of vertices of the $n \times n$ grid graph $G_n$ where the induced subgraph $G_S$ having vertex set $S$ contains no $4$-cycles. We first quickly establish the maximum size of any such induced subgraph. Then, for even $n$ we estimate the number of $4$-cycle-free induced subgraphs of maximum and near-maximum size. If ${\mathcal F}_\varepsilon$ denotes the family of $4$-cycle-free induced subgraphs with at least $(3/4-\varepsilon)n^2$ vertices, then we show $$ \log|{\mathcal F}_0|=(1+o(1))n\log n. $$ Then, we also establish exponential upper and lower bounds for $|{\mathcal F}_\varepsilon|$. This estimate is proved using a local letter-pattern encoding of the unique missing vertex in a set of $2\times2$ blocks that tile the grid; the upper bound for $|{\mathcal F}_\varepsilon|$ uses a coarser block tiling (using larger blocks). We discuss the problem of closing the gap between our upper and lower bounds for $|{\mathcal F}_\varepsilon|$, and a possible defect-container approach.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Aiba, Ernie Croot

item.title: New results on the odd- and unique-Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2605.07322v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The odd-Ramsey number $r_{\text{odd}}(n,H)$ of a graph $H$ is the minimum number of colors needed to edge-color $K_n$ so that in every copy of $H$ some color occurs an odd number of times, and the unique-Ramsey number $r_{\text{u}}(n,H)$ is the corresponding notion in which some color is required to occur not only an odd number of times but exactly once. In this paper, we address three questions from previous papers. We show $r_{\text{odd}}(n,K_{s,t})> n^{1/\left(\frac s2+\frac 1{2\lfloor t/8 \rfloor}\right)}$ when $s\leq t$ and $s$ is odd and $t$ is even, which is log-asymptotically tight when $s$ is fixed and $t\to\infty$. Next, we consider the odd-Ramsey number when the host graph to be edge-colored is a super-Dirac graph, and show that the smallest minimum degree that forces a non-trivial odd-Ramsey number of Hamilton cycles is $n/2+1$. Finally, we show that $r_\text{u}(n,C_n)> n/4$, which leads to a polynomial gap between $r_\text{odd}(n,C_n)$ and $r_\text{u}(n,C_n)$.
item.dc:creator: Shagnik Das, Ying-Sian Wu

item.title: Book Ramsey numbers via algebraic constructions
item.description: arXiv:2606.07214v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(B_n\) denote the book graph consisting of \(n\) triangles sharing a common edge. Rousseau and Sheehan (1978) proved, using Paley graphs, that \(R(B_n,B_n)=4n+2\) whenever \(4n+1\) is a prime power. Since then, only a few additional exact values of \(R(B_n,B_n)\) have been obtained. In this paper, we obtain \(R(B_n,B_n)=4n+1\) for infinitely many \(n\) by constructing graphs from pseudo-cyclic strongly regular graphs (PC-graphs). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first new infinite family of exact diagonal book Ramsey numbers since 1978. We also prove that \(R(B_{n-2},B_n)\le 4n-3\) for every \(n\ge 3\) with \(n\ne 6\), removing the original condition \(n\equiv 2\pmod 3\) imposed by Rousseau and Sheehan. Moreover, equality \(R(B_{n-2},B_n)=4n-3\) holds if there exists a symmetric Hadamard matrix of order \(2n-2\) with all diagonal entries equal to \(1\). In particular, this equality holds for every \(n=2^{2\ell-1}+1\) with \(\ell\ge 1\).
item.dc:creator: Lulu Dai, Qizhong Lin

item.title: On mesh patterns of short length: Equidistribution and enumeration
item.description: arXiv:2606.14367v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classification and enumeration of short mesh patterns have emerged as two central directions in the area. We make substantial progress on both fronts. We construct an involution and a bijection that establish distributional equivalences for two classes of length-$2$ mesh patterns, thereby resolving a conjecture from 2019 and a recent conjecture. As a consequence, the best known upper bounds for the numbers of distribution-equivalence and Wilf-equivalence classes drop to $106$ and $47$, respectively. Combined with the known lower bounds of 105 and 46, conjectured to be exact, these results leave both classifications hinging on a single distribution-equivalence question conjectured in 2019, whose resolution would at once settle the remaining Wilf-equivalence case. We further conjecture that this unresolved equidistribution also holds for involutions, a subclass of all permutations. We also determine the distributions of three additional classes of length-$2$ mesh patterns through a detailed structural analysis. Our work combines bijective techniques with generating-function methods, yielding new insights into the structure and enumeration of short mesh patterns.
item.dc:creator: Qi Fang, Shishuo Fu, Sergey Kitaev, Haijun Li, Xinyu Su, Ziyao Sun

item.title: (Approximate) Symmetric Extension Complexity of the Spanning Tree Polytope
item.description: arXiv:2606.17017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a tight lower bound on symmetric LP formulations for the spanning tree polytope of the complete graph. More precisely, let $P_{ST}(K_n)$ be the spanning tree polytope of $K_n$. We show that, for all $n\ge13$, every symmetric extended formulation for $P_{ST}(K_n)$ has at least $\binom n3$ inequalities. Since the classical Martin formulation has a symmetric formulation of size $O(n^3)$, this gives \[ \operatorname{xcs}(P_{ST}(K_n))=\Theta(n^3). \] We also study outer relaxations of the spanning tree polytope of $K_n$ for maximization with nonnegative edge weights. We show that for every fixed approximation factor below $3/2$, symmetric LP formulations still require $\Theta(n^3)$ inequalities for all sufficiently large $n$, whereas factor $3/2$ admits a formulation of size $O(n^2)$. Moreover, we provide an exact symmetric SDP formulation of size $O(n^2)$, measured by PSD matrix order, which implies $\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{psd}}(P_{ST}(K_n))= \Theta(n^2)$. Thus symmetric LP and SDP sizes already differ for exact formulations, and for every fixed approximation factor $1\le\beta<3/2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Pokutta

item.title: Saturation numbers for joins with graphs containing isolated vertices
item.description: arXiv:2606.22011v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ is $H$-saturated if $G$ contains no $H$-copy as a subgraph, but adding any edge between two non-adjacent vertices in $G$ creates a copy of $H$. The saturation number $\mathrm{sat}(n,H)$ is the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-saturated graph. Cameron and Puleo [Discrete Math. 345 (2022), 112867] showed that $\mathrm{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)\le n-1+\mathrm{sat}(n-1,F)$ for all $n>|V(F)|$. It is natural to ask when the equality holds. Most known results on this bound consider non-empty graphs $F$ without isolated vertices. We study families in which $F$ contains isolated vertices. For $F=K_{p-1}\cup qK_1$, where $p\ge4$ and $q\ge p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)=(p-2)n-\binom{p-1}{2}$ for $n\ge\max\{p+q,\binom p2\}$ and determine the unique extremal graph. We also give the exact result for $q=1$, where the extremal graph has a different structure. For $F=pK_2\cup qK_1$, in the natural range $n\ge2p+q+1$, we prove that $\mathrm{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)=n+3p-4$ holds exactly when $n\ge3p-2$, and the order condition is sharp. Furthermore, we characterize all extremal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Xinying Hua, Yuejian Peng

item.title: Polar Degrees of Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2606.26281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the polar degrees of the coordinate-wise inverse of a linear subspace $L \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ are given by the coefficients of a substitution of the reduced characteristic polynomial of the associated matroid $\mathrm{M}(L)$. Our proof connects the geometry of conormal varieties of reciprocal linear spaces to the combinatorial conormal fan of $\mathrm{M}(L)$. As a corollary, we settle two open conjectures regarding matroid discriminants.
item.dc:creator: Clara Briand, Leonie Kayser, Julian Weigert

item.title: Polynomial Binary Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.08908v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a binary polynomial optimization problem (BPO, in short) we are maximizing a multilinear polynomial expression depending on n binary variables. This is a hard optimization class, containing many NP-hard problems, including unconstrained quadratic binary optimization. Several tractable special classes were considered in the literature, including problems with bounded tree-width (Crama, Hansen, Jaumard, 1990), Berge-acyclic problems (Buchheim, Crama, and Heck, 2019), $\beta$-acyclic problems (Del Pia and Di Gregorio, 2022, 2023), limited reach problems (Clausen, Crama, Lusby, Rodr\'iguez, and Ropke, 2024), and $\alpha$-acyclic problems with bounded rank (Del Pia and Khajavirad, 2025). We focus on a general variable elimination scheme for BPO, and develop the unique explicit multi-linear polynomial form for the equivalent BPO problem obtained after the elimination of a given subset of the variables. The obtained closed form representation of such an equivalent BPO problem allows us to characterize new special classes for which this elimination method, when applied recursively, provides a computationally efficient solution. Our approach is elementary1, algebraic, and provides efficient solution to a wide problem class that properly generalizes all of the above mentioned tractable special cases.
item.dc:creator: Endre Boros

item.title: Acyclic Dichromatic Number of Tournaments: these are the Champions
item.description: arXiv:2607.14694v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The acyclic dichromatic number of an oriented graph is the minimum size of a vertex-partition such that the digraphs induced by any single part are acyclic, and the oriented bipartite graphs between any two parts are acyclic too. We characterize the subtournaments that must appear in every tournament with sufficiently large acyclic dichromatic number, thereby confirming a conjecture of Bang-Jensen, Picasarri-Arrieta, and Yeo and prove that acyclic dichromatic number satisfies a local to global property.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Aboulker, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, Kathryn Nurse, Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta

item.title: Linear Tur\'an Numbers of Uniform Hypertrees
item.description: arXiv:2607.16854v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A hypergraph is linear if every pair of vertices is contained in at most one hyperedge. We study linear Tur\'an numbers of acyclic $r$-uniform hypergraphs, extending earlier work of Gy\'arf\'as, Ruszink\'o, and S\'ark\"ozy from uniformity $3$ to general $r$, with emphasis on hypertrees with four hyperedges. For the linear path $P_4^r$, we prove $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{lin}}_r(n,P_4^r)\le (r+1)n/r$, with equality precisely for disjoint unions of Steiner systems $S(2,r,r^2)$, whenever such systems exist. We also give counterexamples to a structural claim used in a previously proposed proof for $r=4$. The same bound and equality characterization hold for the broom $B_4^r$. For the crown $E_4^r$, writing $B=\{v:d(v)\le r\}$ and $C=\{v:r+1\le d(v)\le2r-1\}$, we prove $|E(H)|\le r|B|/(r-1)+(2r-1)|C|/r$, and hence $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{lin}}_r(n,E_4^r)\le(2r-1)n/r$. We also give a lower-bound construction and formulate a sharper conjecture. Finally, for the linear star $S_k^r$, we prove $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{lin}}_r(n,S_k^r)\le n(k-1)/r$, with equality precisely for $(k-1)$-regular linear $r$-uniform hypergraphs, whenever such hypergraphs exist. Under suitable divisibility and existence assumptions, we also construct $T_k^r$-free examples with $n(k-1)/r$ edges for every linear $r$-uniform hypertree $T_k^r$ with $k$ hyperedges.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Adak, Pragya Verma

item.title: Graphon as a Bridge between Graphs and Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.20213v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that there exist graphons that interpolate between Riemannian manifolds and weighted geometric graphs. Specifically, the graph-to-manifold approximation used in manifold learning can be regarded as the composition of a graph-to-graphon convergence and a graphon-to-manifold convergence in a certain sense. Furthermore, we establish a monotonicity inequality which reveals an implicit relationship between numerous combinatorial parameters and geometric quantities on graphons. Using this inequality, we find relations among conductance, maxcut problem, capacity, and packing radius, as well as their limiting behaviors under graph-to-graphon and graphon-to-manifold convergences; some of these relations are novel even for simple graphs and closed manifolds. We also find that in the graphon-to-manifold limiting process, the purely combinatorial parameters diverge, leading to a ``blowup'' phenomenon; and continuous versions of some graph parameters cannot be realized via Riemannian manifolds, but can be realized via graphons.
item.dc:creator: Dong Zhang

item.title: Monochromatic cycle partitions in 3-mean edge-colourings
item.description: arXiv:2607.29336v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and an edge-coloured complete graph such that the average number of colours incident with a vertex is at most $r$, Conlon and Stein asked whether there is a vertex partition into a bounded number of monochromatic cycles, and proved this for $r=2$. We settle the first open case by proving the corresponding statement for $r=3$.
