item.dc:creator: Csaba Bir\'o, Richard Lang, Ryan R. Martin, Guilherme Oliveira Mota, Alexey Pokrovskiy, Mikl\'os Ruszink\'o, G\'abor N. S\'ark\"ozy

item.title: On Hamilton cycles in connected vertex-transitive graphs of order $2pq$
item.description: arXiv:2608.02349v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The existence of Hamilton cycles in connected vertex-transitive graphs is a core open problem in algebraic graph theory, originating from Lov\'asz's 1969 conjecture. All connected vertex-transitive graphs of order $pq$ are known to be Hamiltonian except the Petersen graph, and primitive graph of order $2pq$ are resolved except the Coxeter graph. This paper considers connected vertex-transitive graphs of order $2pq$ where every transitive automorphism subgroup admits a maximal intransitive normal subgroup inducing prime-length orbits. We prove that all such graphs contain a Hamilton cycle, with no new exceptions beyond the already characterized non-qualifying graphs. This result covers a large non-quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$, advancing the full resolution of the $2pq$.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Tianlei

item.title: Minimal Cayley graphs with large chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2608.06254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Resolving Babai's minimal Cayley graph problem, we construct finite minimal Cayley graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number.
item.dc:creator: James Davies, Meike Hatzel, Liana Yepremyan

item.title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.07646v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=\Theta(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.
item.dc:creator: Richard P. Anstee, Attila Sali, Pei Wu

item.title: The Hajnal-Szemer\'edi theorem in digraphs revisited
item.description: arXiv:2608.12207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hajnal--Szemer\'edi theorem states that every graph with $\Delta(G)\le k-1$ admits an equitable $k$-coloring. Using a reduction implicit in Aboulker, Oijid, Petit, Rocton, and Simon (which itself builds on the literature surrounding feedback arc sets), we prove that this theorem is equivalent to each of four digraph analogues guaranteeing equitable acyclic $k$-colorings under various degree conditions. A minor modification of the proof method in makes the construction algorithmic, so the equitable acyclic coloring guaranteed by these statements can be found in polynomial time. The same reduction shows that the Ore-type Hajnal--Szemer\'edi theorem is equivalent to its four digraph analogues. These equivalences settle the conjecture of Treglown that every $n$-vertex digraph with $r\mid n$ and $\delta^{\max}(D)\ge(1-\frac{1}{r})n$ contains a $T_r$-factor, answer a question of Molla and Treglown by determining the exact Ore-type threshold for $T_r$-factors, and recover the directed Hajnal--Szemer\'edi theorems of Czygrinow, DeBiasio, Kierstead, and Molla as immediate corollaries of this reduction. We also discuss related problems for oriented graphs which do not follow immediately from the reduction mentioned above.
item.dc:creator: Yufei Chang, Louis DeBiasio, H. A. Kierstead, Shuo Wei, Jin Yan

item.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.15925v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study unordered triples of order-$n$ floretion base vectors whose tile centroids form nondegenerate equilateral triangles. A scaled integer centroid map turns Euclidean completion into exact arithmetic on a triangular lattice, and a residue obstruction modulo $3$ shows that every equilateral centroid triangle uses three tiles of one orientation. Combined with finite triangular-lattice completion counts, this gives $|E_n|=4^n(4^n-1)/12$. Equilateral triangles containing the identity word $e_n$ as a vertex form an entirely nonlocal family of cardinality $(4^n+(-2)^n-2)/3$. For synchronized local $\gamma$-cycles, $|L_n|=(7^n-4^n)/3$ and $|L_n|/|E_n|\sim4(7/16)^n$, while on the no-$e$ support $S_n=\{i,j,k\}^n$ locality is exhaustive and $|E_n^S|=|L_n^S|=(2^n-1)3^{n-1}$. The union of the three main axes supports exactly $|E_n^{\rm ax}|=4^{n-1}+2^n-2$ equilateral triangles, split into the branches $x=y=z$ and $x+y+z=0$. For $T\in E_n$, the unsigned vertex product defines a product point $C_T$; a digitwise parity criterion characterizes $C_T=Q_T$ on local cycles and yields Fibonacci subfamilies. Multiplication-generation is equivalent to $p(T)=e_n$, hence $C_T=0$; locally this gives exactly the nontrivial global $\gamma$-orbits, and exact enumeration through order $6$ finds no nonlocal example. Retaining the signs discarded by the unsigned product gives a second classifier: a triangle has scalar vertex-sum square exactly when its three vertices pairwise anticommute. For local cycles this occurs exactly when $|S|$ is odd, giving $|\mathrm{AC}_n\cap L_n|=(7^n-1)/6$, while nonlocal pairwise-anticommuting examples already occur in order $3$.
item.dc:creator: Creighton Dement

item.title: Schur positivity from signed elementary expansions: clique-spiders and spiders $S(a,b,2)$
item.description: arXiv:2608.22184v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Determining when the chromatic symmetric function of a graph is Schur positive is a central problem in algebraic combinatorics. Elementary expansions can help answer this question, but negative coefficients obstruct a direct positivity argument. We develop methods for proving Schur positivity from signed elementary expansions and apply them to chromatic symmetric functions of clique-spiders and three-legged spiders. We first give the Schur alpha-omega lemma, which bounds Schur support. We then give four equivalent sufficient criteria for Schur positivity from a fixed composition-indexed elementary expansion. The matrix, order-ideal, negative Hall, and positive Hall formulations treat positive coefficients as capacities and negative coefficients as demands, with admissible assignments governed by dominance order. These criteria provide certificates of Schur positivity especially when elementary coefficients are negative. For the four basic families of $3$-clique-spiders with total leg length at most one, we obtain complete classifications of both $e$-positivity and Schur positivity. These classifications show how the position of a single leg edge changes positivity. Using selected clique-spider cases and a path-clique bootstrap, we prove that all spiders of the form $S(a,b,2)$ are Schur positive.
item.dc:creator: David G. L. Wang, Watson Z. Y. Wang

item.title: Leading term strandings for webs
item.description: arXiv:2608.27425v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A web is a plane graph encoding an invariant vector in a tensor product of fundamental representations of a quantum group. A stranding of an $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ web is a system of colored oriented curves recording one monomial of the vector it encodes. This article focuses on identifying and constructing leading term strandings, those recording the leading term of a web's vector with respect to a lexicographic order on monomials. We show that every open strand of a leading term stranding is clockwise, so the boundary data of such a stranding is recorded by a row-strict tableau. From a row-strict tableau, we construct a web with a prescribed leading term, and the resulting webs form a web basis. This non recursive construction recovers Fontaine's bases and produces others. For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ webs with no flat vertices, we identify a leading term stranding using the depths of the faces of the web. Finally, we ask whether any two strandings of a web are connected by a sequence of local moves called strand reversals. We answer this question affirmatively for $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, extending a known result for closed webs to webs with boundary; in particular, a leading term stranding of any $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ web is always reachable from an arbitrary stranding.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bo, Madelyn Burns, Junyang Chen, Blaise Marsho, Jacob Martin, Jade Mawn, Bella Mohren, Heather M. Russell, Caitlin Sales, Lance Wong

item.title: A Proof of Albertson's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.01682v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Albertson's conjecture states that every graph of chromatic number r has crossing number at least that of the complete graph K_r. We prove the conjecture for all r. The proof combines new clique-sensitive edge bounds for critical graphs, maximum-clique sampling, and a reserved immersion construction. For graphs of order close to r, we construct edge-disjoint routes while preserving a complete bipartite subgraph whose forced crossings compensate for those introduced when the immersion is smoothed into a drawing. For larger orders, we derive explicit edge bounds using independent-triple deletion and structural properties of critical graphs, then combine them with sampling inequalities that account for crossings within a maximum clique. The remaining numerical inequalities are certified using exact rational arithmetic, with a reproducible certificate and standalone Python verifier.
item.dc:creator: Ankan Sadhu

item.title: The size-Ramsey numbers of $k$-uniform relaxed $\ell$-trees
item.description: arXiv:2609.04713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The size-Ramsey number $\widehat{R}_k(\mathcal G)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal G$ is the minimum number of edges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ such that every $2$-edge-coloring of $\mathcal H$ contains a monochromatic copy of $\mathcal G$. Fox asked whether, for fixed $2\le \ell<k$, the size-Ramsey number of every $k$-uniform relaxed $\ell$-tree on $n$ vertices is bounded by a polynomial in $n$, as recorded by Dudek, La Fleur, Mubayi and R\"odl. We give a negative answer when $\ell+1\le k\le 2\ell-2$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large $n$, we construct a $k$-uniform relaxed $\ell$-tree $\bar{\mathcal T}_{n,\ell}^{(k)}$ on exactly $n$ vertices such that \[ \widehat{R}_k\bigl(\bar{\mathcal T}_{n,\ell}^{(k)}\bigr) \ge 2^{c_{k,\ell}n^{\,1-1/(2\ell-k)}}, \] where $c_{k,\ell}>0$ depends only on $k$ and $\ell$. Moreover, any two distinct edges of the construction intersect in at most $2\ell-k-1$ vertices. In contrast, for $k\ge 2\ell$, we prove that every $k$-uniform relaxed $\ell$-tree $\bar{\mathcal T}_{n,\ell}^{(k)}$ on $n$ vertices satisfies \[ \widehat{R}_k\bigl(\bar{\mathcal T}_{n,\ell}^{(k)}\bigr) =O_{k,\ell}(n^{2k}). \]
item.dc:creator: Meng Ji, Yulai Ma

item.title: The Negami Polynomial and Broken-Circuit Stanley--Reisner Rings
item.description: arXiv:2609.05936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We summarize the classical passage from the chromatic specialization of Negami's polynomial to the Hilbert series of a broken-circuit Stanley--Reisner ring, and record formulas for several graph families with their connectivity hypotheses made explicit. Our main construction in this revision is the associated graded algebra of the squarefree edge algebra under the graphic-matroid rank filtration, for an arbitrary finite loopless graph. Its basis is indexed by all edge subsets, and its multiplication is governed by disjointness and rank additivity. Its bigraded Hilbert polynomial recovers the full three-variable Negami polynomial. We prove that its socle has a basis indexed by edge subsets of full matroid rank; for a connected graph, these are precisely the connected spanning subgraphs. A vertex-degree refinement counts connected regular spanning subgraphs. This finite-dimensional algebra is distinct from a broken-circuit Stanley--Reisner ring. We distinguish these elementary structural results from the unresolved question of whether abstract algebra isomorphism can distinguish graphs with the same Negami polynomial; no priority claim is made for the construction or its Hilbert identity.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Mizukai

item.title: Overlap-Helly theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.10023v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we introduce a generalization of Helly's theorem closely connected to B\'ar\'any-Gromov overlap theorems (also called selection lemmas). Our main result implies both the topological colorful Helly of Kalai and Meschulam and Karasev's topological centerpoint theorem. We further investigate the topological fractional Helly theorem from this overlap perspective, and show an overlap theorem for dense complexes (a continuous second selection lemma for tame maps).
item.dc:creator: Andreas F. Holmsen, Alfredo Hubard

item.title: The VC-dimension of strongly regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.10330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ is $n$-existentially closed or $n$-e.c. if, for all subsets $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=n$ and for all partitions $S=A\sqcup B$, there exists a vertex in $V(G)\setminus S$ adjacent to all vertices in $A$ and no vertices in $B$. We study the minimum number of edges $m(v,n)$ of a $v$-vertex $n$-e.c. graph, and show that $m(v,2)=3v+O(1)$ while $m(v,n)=\Theta(v\log v)$ for fixed $n\ge 3$. The latter result uses a connection to binary covering arrays. A related parameter is the VC-dimension of $G$, defined as the size of the largest subset of vertices shattered by the neighborhoods of vertices in $G$. We initiate systematic study of the VC-dimensions of strongly regular graphs (SRGs). We characterize the sufficiently large SRGs with VC-dimension 2. Furthermore, we determine the VC-dimension of sufficiently large Latin square graphs and of all SRGs of order at most 28, and prove upper bounds for SRGs arising from orthogonal arrays or Steiner systems.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Byrne, John Byrne, Sebastian M. Cioab\u{a}

item.title: Robust order properties in the HLM construction
item.description: arXiv:2609.19015v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Green's arithmetic regularity lemma over $G=\F_2^n$ has tower-type lower bounds. We show that the large order properties in the Hosseini--Lovett--Moshkovitz--Shapira (HLM) construction survive sparse edits. If $d$ is the top block dimension, then changing at most $|G|/16$ points of the top HLM set $A_s$ still leaves a half-graph of height $d/8$. For a suitable choice of the HLM maps, changing at most $\eps|G|$ points of a superlevel set of the averaged witness still leaves a half-graph of height $d/(8\sqrt{s})\ge{\rm twr}(s-2)$. The proofs use Sauer's lemma and the binary code formed by the top-level row traces.
item.dc:creator: Dean Matthew Menezes

item.title: Positive formulas for q-Zeta numerators of root and Ferrers-cell posets
item.description: arXiv:2609.24541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove coefficientwise positivity of Chapoton's $q$-Zeta numerator for the positive-root poset of every finite reduced irreducible crystallographic root system, using root height minus one as the rank function and Chapoton's fixed denominator. Adjoining a minimum gives a lower-semimodular lattice, and a classical labelling of its dual yields a weighted descent formula. The same argument proves positivity on every interval of the augmented root poset. Signed EL-labellings give explicit path formulas for Ferrers-cell posets with arbitrary admissible nonincreasing boundaries, including the root posets of types $A$, $B$, and $C$, and for their intervals. A coloured lift gives a root-height-weighted formula in type $D$. For trapezoidal boundaries, we obtain Gaussian-binomial formulas and sharp coefficient bounds. At $q=1$, a Jacobi-polynomial representation gives simple negative zeros, strict interlacing along fixed-offset sequences, and a limiting zero distribution. The main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow using OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic Claude Fable 5, Grok 4.6, OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol, and Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1. Further details appear in the disclosure at the end of the paper.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Weiye Li

item.title: Sub-quorum colorings of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.25128v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A sub-quorum coloring is a partial vertex coloring in which every colored vertex sees at least half of its colored closed neighborhood in its own color. We study the maximum number of colors $\psq(G)$ from structural, algorithmic and extremal viewpoints. Every $2$-independent set yields a sub-quorum coloring, so $\psq(G)\ge\beta_2(G)$. We prove the degree bound $\psq(G)\le \Delta(G)|V(G)|/(\Delta(G)+\delta(G)-1)$ for $\delta(G)\ge2$, and obtain an exact matching characterization for graphs of maximum degree at most three. Consequently every cubic graph of order $n$ satisfies $n/2\le\psq(G)\le3n/5$, with a stability identity at the upper endpoint. For trees we give an edge representation and a linear-time dynamic program that computes both $\psq(T)$ and an optimal coloring; we also show on the double star $S_{2,2}$ that $\psq$ can exceed the dissociation number even on trees. We prove NP-completeness even for bipartite graphs and determine exact values for several classical families. For rectangular grids, we formulate the conjecture $\psq(G_{m,n})=\beta_2(G_{m,n})=F(m,n)$, recover the dissociation-number formula from known $3$-path vertex-cover results, prove the ladder case directly, and verify the conjecture for every fixed width $2\le m\le11$; widths $3$ through $11$ use exact transfer certificates. For hypercubes we prove $\psq(Q_n)=\beta_2(Q_n)=2^{n-1}$ for every $n\ge2$. Finally, a Nordhaus--Gaddum argument gives $\psq(G)+\psq(\overline G)>\log_2 |V(G)|$ and leads to a complementary upper-bound problem.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Rafik Sahbi, Zhang Wenlin

item.title: Simple symmetric Venn diagrams with 17, 19 and 23 curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.26546v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exhibit simple, rotationally symmetric Venn diagrams with 17 curves, with 19 curves and with 23 curves: $n$ Jordan curves carried to one another by rotation through $2\pi/n$, with every one of the $2^n$ regions present and connected and, since the diagrams are simple, every crossing on exactly two curves. Symmetric Venn diagrams exist for every prime number of curves (Griggs, Killian and Savage, 2004), but those diagrams have many curves through a point; simple ones were known only up to 13 curves (Mamakani and Ruskey, 2014). Four 17-curve, twelve 19-curve and six 23-curve diagrams were found by a Metropolis walk on rotation-invariant quadrangulations of the sphere in which regions may temporarily be duplicated, started from the Griggs-Killian-Savage diagram with its multiple crossings resolved. At 23 curves the walk was held for two weeks by duplicated regions near the poles; the two lineages that finished were the first whose $E=92$ states had none. Every diagram is given by a machine-checkable certificate; one certificate each of the 17-, 19- and 23-curve sizes has been verified by a formal proof in Lean 4. All of the diagrams are non-monotone, which is why the crossing-sequence searches that found the 11- and 13-curve diagrams could not have found them.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dzoba

item.title: On the Binary Rank of Matrices with Constant Real Rank
item.description: arXiv:2609.30203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of determining upper bounds on the maximal binary rank, $b_d$, of a $0,1$ matrix with real rank $d$, for small constant $d$. We prove a general upper bound of $b_d \leq \left\lfloor \sqrt{d2^d + 2d}\right\rfloor -1$. We also develop a general dimension reduction technique of bounding $b_d$ using known upper bounds on $b_{d-1}$ and $b_{d-2}$, as well as prove interesting general structural results on extremal matrices with binary rank $b_d$. This allows us to get improved non-trivial upper bounds on $b_d$ for constant values of $d$, which imply tight bounds on $b_d$ for $3 \leq d \leq 5$. Our results also imply bounds on the equivalent problem of finding the minimum number of bicliques needed to partition the edges of a bipartite graph whose reduced adjacency matrix has real rank at most $d$.
item.dc:creator: Michal Parnas

item.title: Tight bounds for positive discrepancy via eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2609.37961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix $M$ with largest eigenvalue $\lambda_1\geq 0$, it is easy to show that the solution of the optimisation problem $\max_{v\in [-1,1]^n}v^TMv$ is at most $\lambda_1 n$. We prove the following converse: if every $n'\times n'$ principal submatrix of $M$ has maximal eigenvalue at least $\lambda$, then $\max_{v\in [-1,1]^n}v^TMv\geq \lambda(n-n'+1)$. This allows us to lift results about the second largest and the smallest eigenvalue of graphs to the (a priori more difficult) setting of positive discrepancy and MaxCut. Using this new connection, we prove that every $n$-vertex $m$-edge graph that is far from a disjoint union of cliques has a cut of size at least $m/2+n^{5/4-o(1)}$, which is sharp up to the $o(1)$-term. Moreover, we prove that every $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph has bisection width at most $dn/4-\Omega_{\varepsilon}(d^{1/3}n)$ for $d\leq (1-\varepsilon)n/2$, which is optimal for $d=\Omega(n)$. This confirms a conjecture of R\"aty, Sudakov and Tomon.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Janzer, Istv\'an Tomon, Fredy Yip

item.title: A nearly linear bound for the Lov\'asz conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.38135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The celebrated conjecture of Lov\'asz from 1969 asks whether every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path. Buci\'c, Christoph, Pokrovskiy and Steiner recently proved that every such graph on $n$ vertices contains a cycle of length $n^{2/3-o(1)}$. In this paper, we improve this bound to $n^{1-o(1)}$. Our proof uses a structure theorem of Tessera and Tointon to first obtain a partition of the vertex set into sets of small diameter in the original graph. When the parts are large, we repeatedly traverse a spanning tree of maximum degree at most three in the quotient graph, and use the Lov\'asz local lemma to join random short paths along this traversal and extract a long path in the original graph. When the parts are small, we apply Babai's contraction lemma to reduce the problem to finding a long path in a connected Cayley graph of a nilpotent group with boundedly many generators and bounded nilpotency class, and then show that such a Cayley graph on $m$ vertices contains a path on $m^{1-o(1)}$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li, Abhishek Methuku

item.title: The List Total Colouring Conjecture is False
item.description: arXiv:2609.38417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exhibit a cubic graph with total chromatic number equal to four and list total chromatic number five. This disproves the List Total Colouring Conjecture of Borodin--Kostochka--Woodall, Juvan--Mohar--\v{S}krekovski and Hilton--Johnson from the late 1990s. ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra discovered the counterexample with little input from the author.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Noel

item.title: Lower bounds for the magnitude of the minimum eigenvalue of graphs with applications to MaxCut and Chowla's cosine problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.01657v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Jin, Milojevi\'c, Tomon and Zhang established a powerful recursive estimate relating the positive eigenvalues of a graph whose least eigenvalue is small in absolute value. We establish a refinement of this result, yielding improved estimates across spectral graph theory and discrepancy theory, and for Chowla's cosine problem. Recent results of Janzer, Tomon and Yip allow us to directly transfer least eigenvalue estimates to the corresponding surplus estimates. Using these tools, we fully resolve a conjecture of R\"aty, Sudakov and Tomon. We show that, for an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with least eigenvalue $\lambda_n$ and surplus $\operatorname{sp}(G)$, if $G$ is $\epsilon$-far from all disjoint unions of cliques, then $|\lambda_n|\geq \Omega_\epsilon(n^{1/4})$ and $\operatorname{sp}(G)\geq \Omega_\epsilon(n^{5/4})$. Furthermore, we show that when $G$ is $n^{-o(1)}$-far from all disjoint unions of cliques, we have $|\lambda_n|\geq n^{1/4 - o(1)}$ and $\operatorname{sp}(G)\geq n^{5/4 - o(1)}$. Finally, we show that the surplus of a $K_t$-free graph with $m$ edges is at least $m^{0.614 - o(1)}$ as $m$ tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Fredy Yip

item.title: A shorter proof of the linear list Hadwiger conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.01946v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The linear list Hadwiger conjecture asserts that every $K_t$-minor-free graph is $O(t)$-choosable. Following an approach outlined by Delcourt and Postle, we recently established $O(t\log\log t)$-choosability. Soon afterward, OpenAI provided a proof of the conjecture. A key new ingredient of their proof is a linear bound on the choice number of $K_t$-minor-free graphs with at most $t^{11/10}$ vertices. In this paper, we give a relatively simple proof of this small-graph bound for graphs with at most $t(\ln t)^5$ vertices.Combining this with the argument from our earlier $O(t\log\log t)$ bound, we obtain a shorter and somewhat more accessible proof of the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yangyan Gu, Rongxing Xu

item.title: Hilbert fragments
item.description: arXiv:2610.02450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In earlier work, we proved that the length polyhedron of an interval order has a unique Hilbert basis and that every element of this basis is a binary vector. The supports of these binary vectors form a set system whose intersection graph is a cocomparability graph. This leads naturally to the question of which graphs can arise as intersection graphs of such Hilbert-basis supports. We introduce Hilbert fragments, defined as induced subgraphs of these intersection graphs. Thus Hilbert fragments form a hereditary class of cocomparability graphs recording the intersection patterns among the supports of Hilbert-basis elements of interval-order length polyhedra. We characterize Hilbert fragments by an axiomatically defined vertex-labeling, called a track-labeling, and give applications illustrating how this characterization can reveal an underlying one-dimensional structure even when the Hilbert fragments themselves are not interval graphs.
item.dc:creator: Csaba Bir\'o, Andr\'e E. K\'ezdy, Jen\Ho Lehel

item.title: Upper $k$-Star-Forming Sets, $k$-Independence, and Upper Domination
item.description: arXiv:2610.03785v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $\beta_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing maximum degree less than $k$, and let $SF_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a minimal $k$-star-forming set. The known inequality $\beta_k(G)\le SF_k(G)$ suggests asking when equality holds. We place this question in the framework of upper domination: at $k=1$, $\beta_1(G)=\alpha(G)$ and $SF_1(G)=\Gamma(G)$, so the classical equality $\Gamma=\alpha$ on bipartite graphs is exactly the first member of the proposed hierarchy. We prove the equality for complete bipartite graphs for every $k$, obtaining \[ \beta_k(K_{a,b})=SF_k(K_{a,b})=\max\{a,b,2k-2\}\qquad(a,b\ge k), \] and record the elementary low-degree case $\Delta(G)<k$. For $k=2$ we derive certificate restrictions for minimal $2$-star-forming sets in bipartite graphs. For chain graphs we go further: we prove $\beta_2(G)=SF_2(G)$ and obtain an exact formula for their common value. The proof uses the nested-neighborhood structure together with a classification of witnesses to the indispensability of a high internal-degree vertex. We retain the equality problem for chain graphs as a conjecture only for $k\ge3$, and formulate the broader bipartite conjecture. We also determine the upper domination number of every rectangular grid and combine it with the known exact dissociation number to compare $\Gamma$, $\beta_2$, and $SF_2$. In particular, $\Gamma=\beta_2$ on every even-by-even rectangular grid, while $\beta_2\le SF_2$ always; this motivates a grid equality conjecture whose even-by-even case would yield a three-parameter identity.
item.dc:creator: Rafik Sahbi

item.title: A refinement of the edge theorem for order and chain polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.07413v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite poset, we partition the edges of the order polytope and of the chain polytope into classes indexed by the connected convex subsets of the poset, and we establish that corresponding classes have the same cardinality. This yields a closed formula for the common number of edges, and it identifies the bijection of Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama, given by them through an explicit formula, as a disjoint union of simple bijections between corresponding classes, which explains why it is a bijection and how it acts on edge directions and lengths. As consequences, the two polytopes have equally many edge directions, with matching multiplicities; the chain polytope has at least as many edges parallel to each coordinate subspace as the order polytope; and the edge lengths of the chain polytope are dominated by those of the order polytope. Strict inequality occurs in the last two comparisons exactly when the poset contains a three-element chain. We discuss implications for linear and convex combinatorial optimization over ideals and antichains. We also express the number of edges in terms of the comparability graph, in a form that extends to stable-set polytopes of arbitrary graphs, give a recursion for series-parallel posets and closed formulas for layered, zigzag and crown posets, characterize the distributive lattices for which the two polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, and demonstrate that, although the two polytopes have the same number of edges, either one can have the larger diameter, by an arbitrary amount; on the other hand, both diameters are bounded by the width of the poset, and they coincide for ordinal sums, series-parallel posets, and zigzag and crown posets.
item.dc:creator: Jon Lee

item.title: Dynamic Coloring and Graph Squares of Regular Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.09565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An $r$-dynamic coloring of a graph $G$ is a proper vertex coloring in which every vertex $v$ sees at least $\min\{r,d(v)\}$ distinct colors in its neighborhood. The minimum number of colors in such a coloring is the $r$-dynamic chromatic number $\chi_r^d(G)$. We study dynamic colorings of regular graphs. A straighforward observation shows that $\chi_r^d(G)=\chi(G^2)$, for any $r$-regular graph $G$. We prove that $\chi_3^d(G)=\chi(G^2)\le6$ for every claw-free cubic graph $G$, and the bound is sharp. For Hamiltonian claw-free cubic graphs, we improve the bound to $5$ apart from four explicit exceptions. We also determine exactly the $r$-dynamic chromatic number of the $4$-regular circulant graph $C_p(1,3)$ for each $r\in\{2,3,4\}$. In particular, the case $r=4$ determines $\chi(C^2_p(1,3))$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Gutierrez, Grover Ugarte

item.title: Resolving Pisanski's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Pisanski's conjecture on quadrilateral embeddings of regular bipartite graphs. For integers $m\geq d\geq4$ with $4\mid md$, we construct both a connected simple $d$-regular bipartite graph $G$ with $m$ vertices in each bipartition class and an orientable quadrangulation. This graph's genus is \[ \ga(G)=1+\frac{m(d-4)}4. \] These quadrangulations attain the lower bound on the genus from Euler's formula. We give dihedral constructions for even $m$ and a cyclic construction for every $m\geq d$ with $4\mid d$. In each case, two cyclic permutations of a connection set of size $d$ determine all of the local rotations.
item.dc:creator: Austin Ulrigg, Alexander Metzger

item.title: List chromatic number of $G(n,r,s)$ graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13723v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the list chromatic number of generalized Johnson graphs. Recall that the vertices of such graphs are all possible $r$-element subsets of $[n] = \{1, \dotsc, n\}$ and an edge is drawn between two vertices if and only if corresponding sets have exactly $s$ common elements. We prove that for any fixed $s \geq 1$ and $r \geq 2s + 2$ we have $\chi_L(G(n,r,s)) = \Theta(n^{s+1}\ln n)$. In case where $s = 0$ we prove that for all $4\ln n \leq r \leq n/20$ we have $\chi_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \frac{n}{120}\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)$. Together with previous results of Bulankina, Inozemtsev and Kupavskii this proves that $\chi_L(G(n,r,0)) = \Theta\left(n\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)\right)$ uniformly for $2 \leq r \leq (1/2-\varepsilon)n$.
item.dc:creator: M. Koshelev

item.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2305.14138v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.
item.dc:creator: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

item.title: Balls in groups: volume, structure and growth
item.description: arXiv:2403.02485v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a fine-scale structural theory for balls of polynomial volume in finitely generated groups. Our main result shows that a polynomial-volume hypothesis on a single ball implies that every larger ball can, after quotienting by a certain canonical finite normal subgroup, be embedded in a lattice of a Lie group whose connected component is nilpotent with sharply bounded index and dimension. These Lie groups and lattices form chains of successive quotients that are essentially unique, giving a quantitative fine-scale analogue of Losert's strengthening of the Mal'cev completion. This describes the fine structure of the group with sharp algebraic and quantitative precision; for example, it leads to sharp bounds in Breuillard, Green and Tao's finitary version of Gromov's polynomial-growth theorem. These results have a wide range of applications in various aspects of the theory of vertex-transitive graphs, including for instance random walks, percolation, and scaling limits. We obtain some of these applications in the present paper, and treat others in companion papers. Some are due to or joint with other authors.
item.dc:creator: Romain Tessera, Matthew Tointon

item.title: Random $2$-SAT: The set of atoms of the limiting empirical marginal distribution
item.description: arXiv:2410.17749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the set of atoms of the limiting empirical marginal distribution in the random $2$-SAT model is $\mathbb Q \cap (0,1)$, for all clause-to-variable densities up to the satisfiability threshold. While for densities up to $1/2$, the measure is purely discrete, we additionally establish the existence of a nontrivial continuous part for any density in $(1/2, 1)$. Our proof is based on the construction of a random variable with the correct distribution as the the root marginal of a multi-type Galton-Watson tree, along with a subsequent analysis of the resulting almost sure recursion.
item.dc:creator: Noela M\"uller, Ralph Neininger, Haodong Zhu

item.title: Realizing resolutions of powers of extremal ideals
item.description: arXiv:2502.09585v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extremal ideals are a class of square-free monomial ideals which dominate and determine many algebraic invariants of powers of all square-free monomial ideals. For example, the $r^{th}$ power ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ of the extremal ideal on $q$ generators has the maximum Betti numbers among the $r^{th}$ power of any square-free monomial ideal with $q$ generators. In this paper we study the combinatorial and geometric structure of the (minimal) free resolutions of powers of square-free monomial ideals via the resolutions of powers of extremal ideals. Although the end results are algebraic, this problem has a natural interpretation in terms of polytopes and discrete geometry. Our guiding conjecture is that all powers ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ of extremal ideals have resolutions supported on their Scarf simplicial complexes, and thus their resolutions are as small as possible. This conjecture is known to hold for $r \leq 2$ or $q \leq 4$. In this paper we prove the conjecture holds for $r=3$ and any $q\geq 1$ by giving a complete description of the Scarf complex of ${\mathcal{E}_q}^3$. This effectively gives us a sharp bound on the betti numbers and projective dimension of the third power of any square-free momomial ideal. For large $i$ and $q$, our bounds on the $i^{th}$ betti numbers are an exponential improvement over previously known bounds. We also describe a large number of faces of the Scarf complex of ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ for any $r,q \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Trung Chau, Art M. Duval, Sara Faridi, Thiago Holleben, Susan Morey, Liana M. \c{S}ega

item.title: Hilbert polynomials of configuration spaces over graphs of circumference at most 1
item.description: arXiv:2505.24416v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $ k $-configuration space $ B_k\Gamma $ of a topological space $ \Gamma $ is the space of sets of $ k $ distinct points in $ \Gamma $. In this paper, we consider the case where $ \Gamma $ is a graph of circumference at most $1$. We show that for all $ k\ge0 $, the $ i $-th Betti number of $ B_k\Gamma $ is given by a polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in $ k $, called the Hilbert polynomial of $ \Gamma $. We find an expression for the Hilbert polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in terms of those coming from the canonical $1$-bridge decomposition of $ \Gamma $. We also give a combinatorial description of the coefficients of $P_\Gamma^i(k)$.
item.dc:creator: Byung Hee An, Jang Soo Kim

item.title: CoS++: Towards More General and Explicit Implementations for Sampling High-Order Feynman Diagrammatic Series
item.description: arXiv:2507.12349v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend combinatorial summation (CoS) of connected Feynman diagrams to Hubbard mod- els with flavor-dependent propagators and counterterm shifts. The construction combines an interaction-occupancy mask with labels for the open fermion cycle, allowing equivalent endpoint his- tories to be accumulated while retaining the flavor and sublattice information needed by subsequent contractions. In the flavor-dependent version, denoted symmetry-broken CoS (SB-CoS), normal heads carry the cycle flavor and counterterm heads inherit the flavor at their interaction partner. We prove the correctness of the resulting recurrence and introduce terminal readouts that return all nonempty interaction-subset values from a shared circuit, as required by a many-configuration Markov-chain sampler. For three flavors, a second formulation uses determinant polynomials and a local interaction tensor, with connected coefficients extracted by subset recursion or Fourier interpo- lation and a support sieve. Applications to the two-spin honeycomb and three-flavor square-lattice Hubbard models illustrate the treatment of sublattice structure and non-uniform reference shifts.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Shi

item.title: Recurrence for pretentious systems along generalized Pythagorean triples
item.description: arXiv:2508.09778v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish multiple recurrence results for pretentious measure-preserving multiplicative actions along generalized Pythagorean triples, that is, solutions to the equation $ax^2 + b y^2 = c z^2$. This confirms the ergodic-theoretic form of the generalized Pythagorean partition regularity conjecture in this critical case of structured measure-preserving actions. As a consequence of our main theorem, any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the level sets of finitely many pretentious completely multiplicative functions, must contain a monochromatic generalized Pythagorean triple.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Andreas Mountakis

item.title: Global positroid varieties
item.description: arXiv:2509.07476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Positroid subvarieties of complex Grassmannians are the images of the Richardson subvarieties of the full flag varieties under the natural projection map. Positroid varieties admit natural embeddings into certain quiver Grassmannians for equioriented cyclic quivers. Varying representations of the quiver, one defines global positroid varieties inside the type A global affine Grassmannian. The general fiber of the family is isomorphic to the corresponding classical positroid variety and the special fiber is a subvariety of the juggling variety. We show that the global positroid families are flat and describe their (conjecturally reduced) scheme structures. We also describe the special fibers inside the product of classical positroid varieties and realize the irreducible components of the special fibers in terms of the affine Richardson varieties.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin

item.title: Stranding $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs
item.description: arXiv:2510.12035v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Webs are planar directed graphs that encode invariant vectors for tensor products of fundamental $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-representations. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, web calculus is governed by effective reduction rules and well-understood reduced-web bases, but these features break down in higher rank. In this paper we develop a global combinatorial framework for untagged $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs, called \emph{strandings}, which organizes local labeling data into systems of colored directed paths on the web graph. Our main result is an explicit state-sum formula for the invariant vector of an untagged web as a weighted sum over its valid strandings. The usual labeling-based construction requires a choice of decomposition into elementary web pieces and a vertex-by-vertex coefficient calculation. Our global reformulation avoids both. We prove that the vectors produced by strandings are $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-invariant, compare the untagged theory with the tagged-web framework of Cautis, Kamnitzer, and Morrison, and use this comparison to obtain a complete set of relations for untagged web graphs. We also give applications of strandings to nonvanishing results, basis constructions from tableaux, and connections with Springer-theoretic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Heather M. Russell, Julianna Tymoczko

item.title: Combinatorial Bounds for List Recovery via Discrete Brascamp--Lieb Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2510.13775v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In coding theory, the problem of list recovery asks one to find all codewords $c$ of a given code $C$ which such that at least $1-\rho$ fraction of the symbols of $c$ lie in some predetermined set of $\ell$ symbols for each coordinate of the code. A key question is bounding the maximum possible list size $L$ of such codewords for the given code $C$. In this paper, we give novel combinatorial bounds on the list recoverability of various families of linear and folded linear codes, including random linear codes, random Reed--Solomon codes, explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes, and explicit univariate multiplicity codes. Our main result is that in all of these settings, we show that for code of rate $R$, when $\rho = 1 - R - \epsilon$ approaches capacity, the list size $L$ is at most $(\ell/(R+\epsilon))^{O(R/\epsilon)}$. These results also apply in the average-radius regime. Our result resolves a long-standing open question on whether $L$ can be bounded by a polynomial in $\ell$. In the zero-error regime, our bound on $L$ perfectly matches known lower bounds. The primary technique is a novel application of a discrete entropic Brascamp--Lieb inequality to the problem of list recovery, allowing us to relate the local structure of each coordinate with the global structure of the recovered list. As a result of independent interest, we show that a recent result by Chen and Zhang (STOC 2025) on the list decodability of folded Reed--Solomon codes can be generalized into a novel Brascamp--Lieb type inequality.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Manik Dhar, Zihan Zhang

item.title: Adapting Polyhedral Dominance Cones to Ordinal Preference Structures
item.description: arXiv:2601.02796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In combinatorial optimization, ordinal costs can be used to model the quality of elements whenever numerical values are not available. When considering, for example, routing problems for cyclists, the safety of a street can be ranked in ordered categories like safe (separate bike lane), medium safe (street with a bike lane) and unsafe (street without a bike lane). However, ordinal optimization may suggest unrealistic solutions with huge detours to avoid unsafe street segments. In this paper, we investigate how partial preference information regarding the relative quality of the ordinal categories can be used to improve the relevance of the computed solutions. By introducing preference weights which describe how much better a category is at least or at most, compared to the subsequent category, we enlarge the ordinal dominance cone. This leads to a smaller set of alternatives, i. e., of ordinally efficient solutions. The corresponding weighted ordinal ordering cone is a polyhedral cone and we provide descriptions via its extreme rays and via its facets. The latter implies a linear transformation to an associated multi-objective optimization problem w. r. t. Pareto dominance. This paves the way for the application of standard multi-objective solution approaches. We demonstrate the usefulness of the weighted ordinal ordering cone by investigating a safest path problem with different preference weights. Moreover, we investigate the interrelation between the weighted ordering cone to standard dominance concepts of multi-objective optimization, like, e. g., Pareto dominance, lexicographic dominance and weighted sum dominance.
item.dc:creator: Kathrin Klamroth, Michael Stiglmayr, Julia Sudhoff Santos

item.title: There are infinitely many Hilbert cubes of dimension 3 in the set of squares
item.description: arXiv:2604.05459v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For an integer tuple $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ with $a_i\neq0$ for $i=1,\ldots,d$, we define the associated Hilbert cube by \[ H(a_0;a_1,\ldots,a_d) = \left\{ a_0+\sum_{i=1}^d \varepsilon_i a_i: \varepsilon_i\in\{0,1\} \right\}. \] We call $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ a $d$-dimensional Hilbert-cube presentation. We prove that there are $\gg N^{1/4}$ reduced Hilbert-cube presentations $(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)$ with $a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in[0,N]$ such that \[ H(a_0;a_1,a_2,a_3)\subset \mathcal{S}, \] where $\mathcal{S}=\{m^2:\;m\in\Z\}$. Moreover, we prove that for each $i, j\in\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $i<j$, the set $$ \left\{\frac{a_{i}}{a_{j}}:\;H(a_{0}; a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3})\subset \cal{S} \;\text{and}\;a_{i}>0\;\text{for}\;i=0, 1, 2, 3\;\right\} $$ is dense in the set of positive real numbers (in the Euclidean topology).
item.dc:creator: Andrew Bremner, Christian Elsholtz, Maciej Ulas

item.title: Asymptotically Faster Algorithms for Recognizing $(k,\ell)$-Sparse Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.13025v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For fixed integers $k,\ell$ with $0\leq\ell<3k$, we study the problem of deciding whether a graph is $(k,\ell)$-sparse, a notion arising in combinatorial optimization and rigidity theory. Standard pebble-game algorithms take $O(n^2)$ time for $0\leq\ell<2k$ and $O(n^3)$ time for $2k\leq\ell<3k$, although faster algorithms were known for some parameter choices. We develop efficient recognition algorithms using bounded-indegree orientations, reductions to rooted arc-connectivity, augmenting paths, and centroid decomposition. For $0\leq\ell<2k$, they run in $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ time, yielding the first subquadratic bound valid throughout the entire range. Purely combinatorial implementations run in $O(n\sqrt n)$ time throughout this range. For graphs with $O(n)$ edges, we also improve the purely combinatorial running time for decomposing the edge set into a fixed number of forests, or certifying that no such decomposition exists, from $O(n\sqrt{n\log n})$ to $O(n\sqrt n)$. For simple graphs with $2k\leq\ell<3k$, the general recognition algorithm runs in $O(n^2)$ time when $\ell\leq2k+2$ and in $O(n^2\log n)$ time otherwise. When $\ell=2k$ and $k\leq3$, a specialized algorithm improves this to $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ and admits a purely combinatorial $O(n\sqrt n)$ implementation. Whenever the input graph is not $(k,\ell)$-sparse, our recognition algorithms return an explicit violating vertex set.
item.dc:creator: Bence De\'ak, P\'eter Madarasi

item.title: Local network evolution rules driving shortest path multiplicity
item.description: arXiv:2605.25237v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The shortest path multiplicity, here denoted by $\mu$, is an important metric of complex networks. For real networks $\mu$ is high and it correlates with the network community structure. Since local network evolution induces network communities, it is possible that a high shortest path multiplicity is the natural expectation of local evolution rules. Here I demonstrate, by means of numerical simulations and exact results, that this is indeed the case. For random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions $p_k$, $\langle\mu\rangle\sim \langle k(k-1)\rangle / (\langle k\rangle e)$, growing with the network size when $p_k\sim k^{-\gamma}$ and $\gamma\leq3$. For networks generated by stochastic local rules, $\langle\mu\rangle$ increases with the network size and it does so faster than what is observed in their randomized versions. Furthermore, the number of communities increases with the network size and the correlation with $\langle \mu\rangle$ follows.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Vazquez

item.title: From Trees to All Loops: The Combinatorial Geometry of Two-Site Cosmological Wavefunctions
item.description: arXiv:2605.30797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove, at arbitrary loop order and including arbitrary tadpole decorations, the shifted-tree decomposition of two-site cosmological wavefunction coefficients proposed in our previous work, and uncover the combinatorial and geometric structure underlying it. For conformally coupled scalars with polynomial interactions, this decomposition expresses each loop coefficient as a finite signed sum of tree coefficients evaluated at shifted energies. For bubble-like graphs, the alternating sum over a Boolean lattice can be written in terms of finite differences or maximal chains. We prove the maximal-chain identity algebraically by induction on loop order and geometrically by decomposing a cubical Laplace integral into simplices. The maximal chains correspond to permutohedron vertices, whose incident facets encode the chain-dependent divisors. For tadpole-decorated graphs, the finite-difference Leibniz rule gives an explicit expansion indexed by ordered partitions and local maximal chains, which glue into global maximal chains and organize the coefficient as a combinatorial "path integral". A natural ordering of the divisors yields a term-by-term match with graph tubings and completes the all-loop proof, while other orderings give alternative tubing representations of the same coefficient. These identities hold before spatial loop-momentum integration and extend to power-law FRW backgrounds by linearity of the twisted integral. Two-site loop coefficients can therefore be obtained directly from known tree coefficients without solving new loop-level differential systems.
item.dc:creator: Yanfeng Hang, Cong Shen

item.title: $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideals of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.08159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate the $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideal of a graph, a natural generalization of the closed neighborhood ideal. Let $G$ be a simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $S=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring over a field $K$. For a vector $\textbf{k}=(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\in \mathbb{N}^n$ satisfying $1\leq k_i\leq \textrm{deg}_G(i)+1$ for all $i$, the $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideal of $G$ is defined as the squarefree monomial ideal $$\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n\, (\textbf{x}_W:\, W\subseteq N_G[i],\, |W|=k_i)$$ of $S$, where $\textbf{x}_W=\prod_{i\in W} x_i$. We study homological invariants and properties of $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ focusing on its Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, projective dimension and Cohen-Macaulayness. Special attention is devoted to the case where the vector ${\textbf{k}}$ is the degree-vector of the graph, i.e., $k_i=\textrm{deg}_G(i)$ for all vertices $i$, and to the case where $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ coincides with the edge ideal of a graph. In these settings, we provide combinatorial characterizations and bounds for the regularity and projective dimension of $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ for several classes of graphs, and further investigate the Cohen-Macaulay property of these ideals.
item.dc:creator: Somayeh Moradi, Leila Sharifan

item.title: Total positivity and symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.25516v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a notion of total positivity for the symmetric space $G/K$ by taking the Hausdorff closure of the image of Lusztig's totally positive part $G_{>0}$ in $G/K$. We introduce double Bruhat cells for the symmetric space and define their totally positive pieces. We prove a cell decomposition of the totally nonnegative symmetric space, give explicit positive parametrizations of all cells, establish closure relations, and show that the transition maps between the two natural families of parametrizations are subtraction-free.
item.dc:creator: Huanchen Bao

item.title: Sign Patterns in a Two Colored Partition Companion series
item.description: arXiv:2607.10576v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study three closely related questions arising from the recent work of Andrews and El Bachraoui on the two-color partition series \[ S_1(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}s_1(n)q^n=\sum_{a\ge0}q^a(-q^{a+1};q)_\infty^2 \] and its odd companion, denoted by $T_o(q)$. First, for the eta-normalized companion \[ C(q)=(q;q)_\infty T_o(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}c(n)q^n, \] we prove a strong form of the Andrews--El Bachraoui sign conjecture that $\limsup c(n)=+\infty$ and $\liminf c(n)=-\infty$. Second, we construct an involution using the Franklin-type involution of Chen and Liu to combinatorially explain Andrews--El Bachraoui congruence for $s_1(n)$ modulo 4. Third, we introduce a two-variable refinement of $S_1(q)$ which records the difference of the lengths of the two colored components. Using Ramanujan's partial theta identity and heat-type equations, we obtain a closed formula for all of its even moments, and we show that the eta-normalized moments satisfy termwise congruences modulo $p^{2k}$ for every prime $p\equiv5\pmod6$.
item.dc:creator: Aritram Dhar, Ankush Goswami, Mohit Tripathi

item.title: The Five Distance Theorem For An Arbitrary Norm
item.description: arXiv:2608.12405v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The three gap theorem states that the points of the Kronecker sequence $\alpha,2\alpha,\ldots,N\alpha$, considered modulo one, divide the circle into intervals of at most three distinct lengths. In a two-dimensional nearest-neighbour analogue, Haynes and Marklof proved that the Kronecker sequence modulo an arbitrary unimodular lattice determines at most five distinct nearest-neighbour distances in the Euclidean norm, and that this bound is sharp. Dettmann subsequently constructed examples attaining five distinct distances for every $\ell_p$-norm, $1\leq p\leq\infty$. We prove the corresponding upper bound for every norm on $\mathbb R^2$: for every full-rank lattice $L$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb R^2$, and every $N\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct nearest-neighbour distances is at most five. For every norm, this bound is attained for some $L$ and $\alpha$. For strictly convex norms, the proof extends the lattice-theoretic argument of Haynes and Marklof by replacing the Euclidean angular estimates with a cone lemma based on a proper Brass angular measure. The result for arbitrary norms is then obtained by a strictly convex perturbation and a limiting argument.
item.dc:creator: Nikita A. Mironov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Further results on binary linear covering codes and saturating sets in projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.16078v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The binary length function $\ell_2(r,R)$ is the smallest length of a binary linear code with codimension (redundancy) $r$ and covering radius $R$. Let $s_2(N,\rho)$ be the smallest size of a $\rho$-saturating set in the binary projective space $\mathrm{PG}(N,2)$. It is known that the binary length function satisfies $\ell_2(r,R)=s_2(r-1,R-1)$. We obtain the following new upper bounds on $\ell_2(r,R)$, improving the previously known upper bounds by $\Delta(r,R)$: $R=2,r=2t\ge28$, and $r=10,18,20$, $\ell_2(r,2)=s_2(r-1,1)\le51\cdot2^{r/2-5}-1,\Delta(r,2)=2^{r/2-5}$; $R=3,r=3t-1\ge41$ and $r=26$, $\ell_2(r,3)=s_2(r-1,2)\le818\cdot2^{(r-26)/3}-1$, $\Delta(41,3)=63,\Delta(r,3)=2^{(r-26)/3}$ if $r\ge44$. To obtain these bounds, we construct new infinite code families, using distinct versions of the $q^m$-concatenating constructions of covering codes, including new versions proposed in this paper. We also obtain new useful partitions of column sets of parity check matrices of some codes. The new code families provide the asymptotic covering-density bounds $\overline{\mu}(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $\overline{\mu}(3)\le1.35935$, improving the previously known bounds and giving rise to the new upper bounds $f(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $f(3)\le1.35935$ on the constants $f(2),f(3)$ of the Green's Open Problem 40.
item.dc:creator: Alexander A. Davydov, Stefano Marcugini, Fernanda Pambianco, Stephen Wu

item.title: Positive Eigenvalues of Hadamard Square Roots on Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.22744v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\mu_2(G)$ be the minimum number of positive eigenvalues of an entrywise positive real symmetric group-circulant matrix whose entrywise square is positive definite. We prove that $\mu_2(G)\le5$ precisely when $|G|\le15$, and that $\mu_2(G)=6$ precisely when $|G|=16$ or $G$ is cyclic of order $18$, $20$ or $22$. For the noncyclic groups of order at most fifteen, the minimum is three for $C_2^2$ and five otherwise. If the positive Fourier support of such a matrix is $\{0,\pm r_1,\ldots,\pm r_d\}$, where $d\ge1$ and all $2d+1$ displayed elements are distinct, then there are integers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$, not all zero, such that $\sum_i\alpha_i r_i=0$ and $\sum_i|\alpha_i|\le\max\{5,d+2\}$. The bound five is sharp for $d=2$ and $d=3$.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xie

item.title: The structure of almost symmetric almost complete intersection numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2609.24880v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a structure theorem for numerical semigroups H that are almost symmetric and almost complete intersections. We show that a row-factorization (RF) matrix of H must possess a highly regular structure, which we call a cascade matrix. Consequently, the defining ideal I_H of the semigroup ring k[H] also exhibits a highly regular structure, derived from this cascade matrix. Both the RF-matrix and the binomial minimal generating set of I_H are unique. Conversely, this structure completely characterizes almost symmetric almost complete intersection numerical semigroups: to every cascade matrix M we associate a monoid H and, whenever this is a numerical semigroup, we prove that H is pseudo-symmetric, almost complete intersection, and has M as RF-matrix. As a consequence of our study, we obtain several key results. 1) Rigidty: if an almost complete intersection semigroup is almost symmetric, then it is forced to have odd embedding dimension and to be pseudo-symmetric. This result is a ``next step'' after Kunz's theorem, which states that an almost complete intersection semigroup is never symmetric. 2) Huneke-Ulrich structure: the toric ideal can be realized as the ideal of entries of an alternating matrix multiplied by a vector of variables, and this yields the licci property. 3) Cascade polynomials: for each odd positive integer e, we construct a multivariate squarefree polynomial P_e with integer coefficients, arising from a cascade matrix of variables. We provide an enumerative interpretation of its coefficients, thereby proving their non-negativity. 4) Herzog--Watanabe question: we prove that every minimal relation of an arbitrary numerical semigroup H can be obtained by subtracting two rows in some RF-matrix of H, affirmatively answering a 2019 question by Herzog and Watanabe.
item.dc:creator: Kazufumi Eto, Naoyuki Matsuoka, Alessio Moscariello, Takahiro Numata, Alessio Sammartano, Kei-ichi Watanabe

item.title: Graphical Discreteness, Coxeter Doublings and Generalized Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2609.28550v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graphical discreteness is not preserved under quasi-isometry in general. We prove that, for every finite thick generalized $m$-gon $\Gamma$ with $m\geq 3$, graphical discreteness is nevertheless constant on the class of finitely generated groups quasi-isometric to the right-angled Coxeter group $W_\Gamma$: such a group $\Lambda$ is graphically discrete if and only if $\Gamma$ is nonflexible, meaning that no nontrivial graph automorphism of $\Gamma$ fixes a closed star pointwise. The proof combines quasi-isometric rigidity of Fuchsian buildings with a metric-strata argument that recovers the standard Coxeter Cayley graph from the building metric. For finite-rank Coxeter systems, we also show that the automorphism group of the standard Cayley graph is compact-by-discrete if and only if it is discrete, equivalently, if and only if the defining diagram is nonflexible. We further obtain obstructions to graphical discreteness from one-vertex doublings, classify compact-by-discreteness for standard chamber graphs of graph products of finite groups, and derive applications to finite projective planes and to right-angled Coxeter groups with Menger curve boundary. Our methods do not settle whether nonflexible finite thick generalized polygons exist.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Theoretical Analysis of DomiRank Centrality: Automorphism, Entropy, and Graph Transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.00107v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: DomiRank is a node-importance algorithm for unweighted networks, defined by a dynamical model governed by a competition-strength parameter, a dominance threshold, and a decay rate. We study its relations with graph automorphism: automorphism-related vertices share the same DomiRank value, and a graph whose values are pairwise distinct must be asymmetric; we derive DomiRank properties of regular and vertex-transitive graphs and bound the number of distinct values by that of the orbits. For DomiRank entropy, the maximum over connected graphs is attained only by regular graphs, and on the effective (truncated) distribution it decreases monotonically with the competition parameter on all four tested networks, while a sufficient-condition theorem and a refined conjecture cover the theoretical entropy; we further identify the initial entropy derivative with the degree--log-degree edge covariance, making the decrease rigorous near vanishing competition for structurally disassortative graphs (including all tested networks) and yielding an assortative counterexample; tuning sigma shifts node identification from important to dominant. We study how graph transformations (vertex similarity, partitions, edge swaps, m-products) affect the DomiRank vector, and characterize sigma's sensitivity and limits: the normalized distribution is sigma-invariant iff the degree vector is an adjacency-matrix eigenvector, and sigma interpolates between degree and least-eigenvector centrality; experiments on four real networks confirm it. DomiRank is thus a tunable complement to principal-eigenvector centrality. Since parameterization by sigma is a structural property of the measure, not a guarantee of downstream advantage, we also relate these results to the companion null-model study of how much of DomiRank's task-level edge over a degree baseline survives a degree correction.
item.dc:creator: Yingying Zhang, Chengye Zhao

item.title: Recovery Set Structures and Service Rates of Codes Obtained by the Plotkin-type Construction
item.description: arXiv:2610.01900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In distributed storage systems, redundancy enables a single data object to be reconstructed using several disjoint groups of servers. The resulting service rate region (SRR) captures all combinations of object request rates that the system can support simultaneously without overloading any individual server. We analyze the SRR of binary codes obtained via the Plotkin-type construction. We demonstrate that each recovery set for an information object of the Plotkin-type code $\mathcal{C}_p$ induces a corresponding recovery set for the same data object characterized by the underlying code $\mathcal{C}$. Furthermore, by characterizing the recovery sets structure of $\mathcal{C}_p$ in terms of the recovery set structure of $\mathcal{C}$, we identify the additional recovery sets introduced by this construction. Using the associated recovery hypergraphs, we establish bounds on the SRRs of $\mathcal{C}_p$ and iterated code $\mathcal{C}_{p^m}$ in terms of the SRR of $\mathcal{C}$. We consider the family of first-order binary Reed-Muller codes and show how the recovery structure, and consequently, the service rates of R$(1,m)$ for arbitrary $m$ can be recursively derived from a generator matrix of R$(1,2)$ through our results for successive Plotkin-type constructions.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka Choudhary, Maheshanand Bhaintwal

item.title: The optimal van der Corput property for squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.07765v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative form of the van der Corput property for squares. For all sufficiently large $N$, we construct a real trigonometric polynomial $P(\theta)=a_0+\sum_{1\le n\le\sqrt N}a_n\cos(2\pi n^2\theta)$ satisfying \begin{equation}\tag{1}\label{eq:abstract-vdc} P(\theta)\ge0\quad(\theta\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}),\qquad P(0)=1, \end{equation} with \[0\le a_0\le\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. As a consequence, if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}\cap[1,N]$ has no nonzero square difference, then \[|A|\le N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] improving upon a recent result of Green and Sawhney. Our construction builds on previous work of Slijep\v{c}evi\'c, Slijep\v{c}evi\'c--Nin\v{c}evi\'c, and Fan--Lott, and the proof of the upper bound is elementary and self-contained. We also show that every real trigonometric polynomial of the above form satisfying \eqref{eq:abstract-vdc} has \[a_0\ge\exp(-C\sqrt{\log N\log\log N})\] for an absolute constant $C>0$. Thus the van der Corput property cannot be used to obtain a power-saving bound for the Furstenberg--S\'ark\"ozy theorem.
item.dc:creator: Steve Fan, Andrew Lott

item.title: Random $3$-regular graphs are not globally synchronizing
item.description: arXiv:2610.09135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the homogeneous Kuramoto model on random 3-regular graphs. A connected graph $G$ is globally synchronizing if, for almost every initial condition, the gradient flow converges to a fully synchronized state, in which all phases coincide. It has been conjectured by Bandeira [Oberwolfach Rep. 21 (2024) 1163-1226] that a random 3-regular graph $G_{2n,3}$ is globally synchronizing with high probability. We disprove this conjecture in a strong way: $G_{2n,3}$ is not globally synchronizing with probability tending to 1.
item.dc:creator: Ciro Carvallo, Pablo Groisman, Dieter Mitsche

item.title: Categorified Cluster Structures on Coulomb Branches of Certain Star-Shaped Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.11427v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the quantized $K$-theoretic Coulomb branches of framed star-shaped quivers with central gauge dimension $n\geq2$, $r-1$ one-dimensional outer gauge vertices, and a one-dimensional framing at the central vertex. For $n=2$ and arbitrary $r\geq1$, and for every $n\geq2$ with $1\leq r\leq5$, we prove that the loop-graded Koszul-perverse heart is a monoidal categorification of the associated quantum cluster algebra over $\mathbb{Z}[v^{\pm1}]$. This quantum cluster algebra coincides with its upper quantum cluster algebra. For all $n\geq2$ and $r\geq1$, we construct an explicit initial seed and identify the associated upper quantum cluster algebra with the Grothendieck ring of this heart. Every mutation is realized by a short exact sequence, and every quantum cluster monomial is represented by a simple object.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13204v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.
